VA Handbook 6500, Appendix E (VA privacy control overlay, Rev 4-based, cross-referenced to PT family)
metadata.notes: VA 6500 predates Rev 5 and uses Rev 4 control numbering/baselines. Where a VA 6500 control number has no direct Rev 5 equivalent (withdrawn/renumbered/incorporated), this is flagged in va_overlay.mapping_notes. Priority codes (P0-P3) are VA's own sequencing guidance, not a NIST construct. VA Appendix E privacy controls (AP/AR/DI/DM/IP/SE/TR/UL) are attached as cross-references under the PT family rather than merged as direct equivalents.

control_families.family_description: Governs who or what can access systems and information, under what conditions, and with what restrictions. Covers account lifecycle, session controls, remote and wireless access, mobile device access, and information flow between systems.

nist_800_53.control_statement: The organization develops, documents, and disseminates an access control policy and procedures, and reviews/updates them on an organization-defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: This control requires the establishment of policy and procedures for the effective implementation of selected security controls in the AC family. Policy and procedures reflect applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, and standards. Security program policy typically addresses the purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, and compliance for the whole organization, while system-level procedures address the how of implementing that policy for a specific system.
assessment_objectives: Determine if an access control policy is developed and documented.
Determine if the access control policy is disseminated to defined personnel or roles.
Determine if access control procedures are developed and documented.
Determine if access control procedures are disseminated to defined personnel or roles.
Determine if the access control policy and procedures are reviewed and updated at the organization-defined frequency.

parameters.description: personnel or roles to whom policy/procedures are disseminated
frequency of policy and procedure review/update

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years, per VA Directive/Handbook 6330
Policy disseminated enterprise-wide; procedures disseminated to those responsible for implementation

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA Handbook 6500 itself, along with the other 6500-series handbooks, fulfills the national-level policy requirement. Local facilities are responsible for issuing a local policy stating that VA Handbook 6500 policy/procedures are followed locally, and for developing local SOPs as needed.
va_specific_requirements: Local policy must state VA Directive/Handbook 6500 is followed locally.
Local policy may be more stringent than VA policy but not less stringent.
Local policies reviewed/updated annually.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean 1:1 mapping; no numbering conflict between VA 6500 and Rev 5.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written access control policy (the 'why' and 'what,' at an enterprise level) and procedures (the 'how,' typically at the local/system level) covering how access to systems is granted, managed, and reviewed. Both must be formally reviewed and updated periodically, not just written once and forgotten.

evidence_required.description: Enterprise-level access control policy document.
Local/system-specific access control procedures.
Documented evidence of periodic policy review (e.g., signed review log, revision history).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Personnel sanctions policy shares the same policy-and-procedure documentation pattern and enterprise dissemination requirement.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Define and document account types; assign account managers; require prerequisites/criteria for group and role membership; specify authorized users, group/role membership, and access authorizations for each account; require approval for account creation; create/enable/modify/disable/remove accounts per organization-defined procedures; monitor account use; notify account managers of changes in status; authorize access based on need; review accounts for compliance; and establish a process for reissuing shared/group credentials.
nist_800_53.discussion: Examples of account types include individual, shared/group, system, guest/anonymous, emergency, developer/manufacturer/vendor, temporary, and service accounts. Some organizations may consider the notification of pending transfers and separations of individuals a personnel-related action rather than an account management action. Automated mechanisms can include email, phone, or system alerts.
assessment_objectives: Determine if account types allowed and specifically prohibited for use are defined and documented.
Determine if account managers are assigned.
Determine if prerequisites and criteria for group/role membership are defined.
Determine if authorized users, group/role membership, and access authorizations are specified for each account.
Determine if approvals are required for requests to create accounts.
Determine if accounts are created, enabled, modified, disabled, and removed per defined procedures.
Determine if account usage is monitored.
Determine if account managers are notified when accounts are no longer required, users are terminated/transferred, or usage/need-to-know changes.
Determine if access is authorized based on valid access authorization, intended system usage, and other defined attributes.
Determine if accounts are reviewed for compliance with account management requirements at a defined frequency.
Determine if a process exists for reissuing shared/group credentials when individuals are removed from the group.

parameters.description: prerequisites/criteria for group and role membership
personnel or roles required to approve account creation requests
frequency of account review for compliance

nist_800_53.control_statement: Support the management of system accounts using automated mechanisms.
nist_800_53.discussion: Automated system account management includes using automated mechanisms to create, enable, modify, disable, and remove accounts; notify account managers; and track/report atypical usage.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Instead of an admin manually creating/disabling every account by hand, the system uses automated tools (like Active Directory scripts or an identity management platform) to handle account lifecycle actions and flag unusual account activity.

evidence_required.description: Identity/account management automation tool configuration (e.g., provisioning workflow rules).

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Automated Temporary and Emergency Account Management

nist_800_53.control_statement: Automatically remove or disable temporary and emergency accounts after an organization-defined time period for each type of account.
nist_800_53.discussion: Temporary and emergency accounts are intended for short-term, limited use. Automating removal reduces the risk that such accounts remain active indefinitely.

va_odp_values.value: Automatic termination date established at time of account creation
Removed immediately upon conclusion of the emergency situation

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Temporary accounts (like a short-term contractor login) and emergency accounts (like a break-glass admin login) automatically expire on their own — nobody has to remember to manually turn them off.

evidence_required.description: Temporary/emergency account expiration configuration and removal logs.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Disable accounts within an organization-defined time period when accounts have expired, are no longer associated with a user, violate policy, or have been inactive for a defined period.
nist_800_53.discussion: Disabling instead of deleting may be necessary to preserve historical records.

va_odp_values.value: 90 days of inactivity

va_overlay.mapping_notes: VA 6500 labels this 'Disable Inactive Accounts' (Rev 4 naming); functionally maps to Rev 5 AC-2(3).

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: If an account sits unused for 90 days, it gets automatically disabled — this catches accounts that were never properly deactivated after someone left or stopped needing access.

evidence_required.description: Report of accounts auto-disabled due to 90-day inactivity threshold.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Automatically audit account creation, modification, enabling, disabling, and removal actions, and notify defined personnel/roles.
nist_800_53.discussion: Supports accountability and after-the-fact investigation of account-related incidents.

va_odp_values.value: Defined by Information System Owner in SSP

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Every time an account is created, changed, or removed, that action is automatically logged and specific people are notified — so there's a clear record of who changed what account and when.

evidence_required.description: Automated audit log of account lifecycle actions with notification records.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require users to log out after an organization-defined time period of expected inactivity or per specific triggers.
nist_800_53.discussion: This differs from a session lock (AC-11); it requires actually logging out rather than just locking the session.

va_odp_values.value: Upon completion of required input; users must log off or lock console before walking away

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, users must actually log all the way out (not just lock the screen) once they're done working or step away, rather than leaving an active logged-in session unattended.

evidence_required.description: User logout requirement documented in acceptable use policy/ROB.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Enforce organization-defined circumstances and/or usage conditions for accounts.
nist_800_53.discussion: Example conditions include restricting usage to certain days of the week, times of day, or physical locations.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping; VA leaves specific usage conditions to Information System Owner (Attachment 3).

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, an account might be restricted to only work during certain hours, days, or from certain locations — for example, a batch-processing service account that should only ever run overnight.

evidence_required.description: Account usage condition/restriction configuration (time-of-day, location-based access rules).

nist_800_53.control_statement: Monitor system accounts for atypical usage and report atypical usage to defined personnel/roles.
nist_800_53.discussion: Atypical usage includes access at unusual times or from unusual locations, which may indicate compromise.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Reported to the ISO.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Accounts are watched for behavior that doesn't match their normal pattern — like a login from an unusual country at 3 AM — and the ISO is alerted, since this could indicate the account has been compromised.

evidence_required.description: Atypical account usage alerts/reports sent to the ISO.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Disable accounts of users posing a significant risk within an organization-defined time period of discovery.
nist_800_53.discussion: Speed is critical here; delay increases exposure from an already-identified risk.

va_odp_values.value: Immediately, after notification

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: If someone is identified as a significant risk (for example, being investigated for misconduct or a security violation), their account access is cut off immediately — not on the next scheduled review cycle.

evidence_required.description: Account disablement timestamp showing immediate action following risk identification.

va_odp_values.value: Individual, group, system, application, guest/anonymous, emergency, developer/manufacturer/vendor, temporary, service
At least semi-annually, or per SSP-approved frequency
Approved by user's supervisor and CIO before system administrator/designee creates account
Within 24 hours of notification of status change (departure, transfer, suspension, long-term detail, need-to-know change)

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: The Information System Owner, local CIO, or designee identifies account types, assigns account managers, establishes group/role conditions, requires supervisor and CIO approval prior to account creation, and monitors account usage. ISOs perform regular audits of access requests to confirm prerequisite training, signed ROB, and background screening were completed before access was granted.
va_specific_requirements: Accounts terminated/disabled within 24 hours of notification of a status change.
ISO performs regular audits of access requests for compliance with training/background screening prerequisites.
Contractor account requests are routed through the CO/COR to the ISO for verification before the Information System Owner grants access.
Emergency access is granted per contingency procedures and terminated immediately upon conclusion of the emergency.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: VA 6500 AC-2 numbering and enhancement structure align cleanly with Rev 5 AC-2 and its sub-enhancements.

controls.plain_english_explanation: This is the full lifecycle management of user accounts: deciding what kinds of accounts exist, who approves creating them, how they're monitored while active, and how quickly they're disabled or removed when no longer needed. VA adds hard deadlines (e.g., 24-hour disablement) and specific approval chains (supervisor + CIO) that go beyond the generic NIST 'organization-defined' language.

evidence_required.description: Account management policy defining account types and lifecycle.
Local SOP for provisioning, approval routing, and de-provisioning, including VA's 24-hour timeline.
Account creation/modification/removal logs; list of active and recently disabled accounts; account review/compliance reports.
Documented supervisor/CIO approval for account creation requests.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Account creation relies on identity verification performed under IA-2.
Identifier management and account management are tightly coupled; account records reference IA-4 identifiers.
Personnel termination triggers account disablement; VA's 24-hour SLA is shared language across both controls.
Personnel transfer triggers account access modification.
Account management events (creation, modification, removal) are a defined category of auditable events.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Enforce approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources in accordance with applicable access control policies.
nist_800_53.discussion: Access control policies control access between active entities (users/processes) and passive entities (devices, files, records). Access enforcement mechanisms can be employed at the application and service level to provide increased protection.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the system enforces approved authorizations for logical access to information and system resources per applicable access control policies.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Access enforcement may be accomplished via identity-based, role-based, or rule-based policies and mechanisms such as access control lists, matrices, or cryptography, applied at both the system and application level where necessary. Any encryption used as an access enforcement mechanism must be FIPS 140-2 (or successor) validated.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Once someone is authorized to access something, the system must actually enforce that authorization technically — not just rely on policy. This is the mechanism (access control lists, role-based permissions, encryption) that physically prevents unauthorized access even if someone tries.

evidence_required.description: Access control list / permission configuration exports demonstrating enforcement mechanism.
Access control policy referenced by the enforcement mechanism.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Least privilege is enforced through the same technical mechanisms as general access enforcement.
When encryption is used as an access enforcement mechanism, it must meet SC-13 cryptographic protection requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Enforce approved authorizations for controlling the flow of information within the system and between interconnected systems based on defined information flow control policies.
nist_800_53.discussion: Information flow control regulates where information can travel, as opposed to who can access it. Enforcement mechanisms include boundary protection devices that filter based on header data or content (e.g., keyword searches).
assessment_objectives: Determine if the system enforces approved authorizations for controlling information flow within the system and between interconnected systems, based on defined information flow control policies.

va_odp_values.value: VA-NSOC flow control policy — e.g., blocking export-controlled information from transmitting in the clear to the Internet, blocking spoofed internal traffic, restricting web requests not routed through internal proxy

controls.plain_english_explanation: This isn't about who can log in — it's about controlling where data is allowed to travel once someone has access. For example, blocking sensitive data from being sent unencrypted to the public internet, even by an authorized user.

evidence_required.description: Firewall/proxy/gateway rule sets demonstrating flow control enforcement.
Network/data flow diagram showing enforcement points.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Boundary protection devices are often the same technical mechanism enforcing both AC-4 flow control and SC-7 boundary protection.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify and document duties requiring separation; define system access authorizations to support that separation.
nist_800_53.discussion: Separation of duties addresses the potential for abuse of authorized privileges and reduces the risk of malicious activity without collusion. Examples include dividing mission functions among different individuals, and ensuring security personnel administering access control do not also administer audit functions.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the organization identifies and documents duties requiring separation.
Determine if the organization defines system access authorizations to support separation of duties.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Privileged users must not use elevated-privilege accounts for routine activities and must use a separate standard account for non-privileged tasks. OI&T conducts a quarterly review of elevated privilege accounts. Supervisors ensure no single individual performs conflicting duties (e.g., data entry and its own verification/reconciliation).
va_specific_requirements: Quarterly review of elevated privilege accounts by OI&T.
System administrators must not conduct audits/reviews of the systems they administer.
The ISO should not also serve as a system administrator.
Privileged users prohibited from reviewing/accessing individual accounts or devices for investigations without senior management authorization, except continuous monitoring/OIG activity.

controls.plain_english_explanation: No single person should have enough unchecked access to both perform and cover up a fraudulent or malicious action alone. VA gets specific: the person who manages a system can't be the one auditing it, and privileged (admin) accounts must be reserved strictly for admin tasks, not daily work.

evidence_required.description: Separation of duties policy/matrix defining conflicting duty combinations.
Quarterly privileged account review records.
Position descriptions reflecting separation of duties.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Least privilege and separation of duties are complementary; evidence of privileged account restriction supports both.
Position risk designation and separation of duties both rely on documented role responsibilities.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ the principle of least privilege, allowing only authorized accesses necessary to accomplish assigned organizational tasks.
nist_800_53.discussion: Organizations employ least privilege for specific duties and information systems, including for information system processes, which should operate at privilege levels no higher than necessary.
assessment_objectives: Determine if only authorized accesses for users/processes necessary to accomplish assigned tasks are employed.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Explicitly authorize access to organization-defined security functions and security-relevant information.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Access to security-related functions (like firewall configuration or audit log settings) requires specific, explicit authorization — it's not something granted by default even to otherwise privileged users.

evidence_required.description: List of security functions and the individuals explicitly authorized to access them.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require users of privileged accounts to use non-privileged accounts when accessing non-security functions.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: VA 6500 text labels this enhancement '(1) Non-Privileged Access' under a numbering quirk in the source Attachment table but functionally aligns to Rev 5 AC-6(2).

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: An administrator checking email or browsing the web should be using their regular, non-privileged account — not their admin account — for those everyday tasks.

evidence_required.description: Policy requiring separate privileged/non-privileged accounts for admin users.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Authorize network access to privileged commands only for compelling operational needs and document rationale in the security plan.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Running powerful administrative commands over the network (rather than locally at the machine) is only allowed when there's a genuine operational need, and that need has to be documented and justified in the SSP.

evidence_required.description: SSP documentation justifying network-based privileged command access.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Restrict privileged accounts on the system to organization-defined personnel or roles.

va_odp_values.value: Individuals approved by supervisor, ISO, and Information System Owner; must have background investigation, signed Elevated Privileges ROB, and completed TMS elevated-privileges training

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Only specific, pre-approved people can hold privileged/admin accounts — VA requires those individuals to have passed a background check, signed a special Rules of Behavior for elevated access, and completed dedicated training before getting admin rights.

evidence_required.description: List of privileged account holders with supporting approval/screening/training records.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Log the execution of privileged functions.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Every time someone uses an admin-level function (like changing a security setting or accessing another user's data), that action is logged so there's a record of it.

evidence_required.description: Privileged function execution log.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Prohibit Non-Privileged Users from Executing Privileged Functions

nist_800_53.control_statement: Prevent non-privileged users from executing privileged functions.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The system technically blocks regular users from running admin-level functions at all — it's not just a policy request, it's enforced by the software itself.

evidence_required.description: Access control configuration demonstrating non-privileged users cannot execute privileged functions.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Each user or process is assigned the most restrictive set of privileges needed to perform authorized tasks. OI&T audits use of privileged functions as a key method of detecting insider-threat or advanced-persistent-threat behavior.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping across base control and enhancements.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Give people (and system processes) only the access they actually need to do their job — nothing more. Admins should have a separate 'regular' account for everyday work and only use their admin account when doing admin tasks, and every use of a privileged/admin function should be logged.

evidence_required.description: Least privilege policy.
Privileged function execution logs; list of accounts with elevated privileges and their justifications.
Elevated Privileges ROB signature and TMS training completion for privileged users.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Least privilege and separation of duties share privileged-account review evidence.
Logging of privileged function use ties into audit information protection requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Enforce a limit of consecutive invalid logon attempts by a user during an organization-defined time period, and automatically take a defined action when the limit is exceeded.
nist_800_53.discussion: This control applies regardless of whether the logon occurs via local or network connection. Automatic lockouts are typically temporary and release after a defined period, or require administrator unlock for privileged accounts.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a limit on consecutive invalid logon attempts is enforced during a defined time period.
Determine if the system automatically takes a defined action when the maximum number of unsuccessful attempts is exceeded.

va_odp_values.value: 5 attempts during a 1-hour period (Low); 5 attempts during a 1-day/24-hour period (Moderate and High)
Locks the account; 1-hour lockout for Low; locked until released by Administrator for Moderate/High

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Locked accounts with privileged access (e.g., root/administrator) remain locked until unlocked by the Help Desk or other authorized account management personnel.

controls.plain_english_explanation: If someone repeatedly enters the wrong password, the system locks the account rather than letting unlimited guessing continue. VA sets the actual numbers: 5 failed attempts, then lockout — and for admin accounts, only the Help Desk can unlock it.

evidence_required.description: Account lockout policy configuration (attempt threshold, lockout duration).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Authenticator management and lockout thresholds are often configured together.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Display an approved system use notification message before granting access, stating that users are accessing a government system, usage may be monitored/recorded, unauthorized use is prohibited, and use constitutes consent; retain the notification until acknowledged.
nist_800_53.discussion: System use notifications can be implemented via electronic banners. This control applies to logon interfaces with human users and is not required for machine-to-machine communications.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the system displays an approved use notification banner before granting access.
Determine if the notification is retained until the user acknowledges usage conditions and takes explicit action to proceed.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA has a standard, approved warning banner text (specified in Handbook 6500) that must be deployed on all capable VA computer systems, servers, workstations, routers, switches, and other devices. The ISO verifies deployment of the banner as part of the annual FISMA review.
va_specific_requirements: Use of VA's specific approved banner text where technically possible.
Annual ISO verification of banner deployment across capable equipment.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Before anyone can log in, they must see a warning banner stating this is a government system, that their activity may be monitored, and that unauthorized use is illegal — and they have to actively acknowledge it before proceeding.

evidence_required.description: Screenshot of the login banner as displayed on representative systems.
Annual ISO verification/attestation of banner deployment.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System use notification content overlaps conceptually with Rules of Behavior acknowledgment.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Notify the user, upon successful logon, of the date/time of the last logon.
nist_800_53.discussion: Applicable to logons via human user interfaces and other architectures (e.g., service-oriented architectures).

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time; OI&T may elect to implement it at their discretion.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — systems are not mandated to show users their last login date/time, though OI&T may choose to implement it voluntarily.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Limit the number of concurrent sessions for each account and/or account type to a defined maximum number.
nist_800_53.discussion: Certain roles/situations may require multiple concurrent sessions.

va_odp_values.value: 3 sessions for general users; 5 sessions for users with elevated privileges

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Exceptions handled case-by-case with justification and Information System Owner/CIO concurrence, documented in the SSP.

controls.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, users are limited to a set number of simultaneous logged-in sessions (3 for regular users, 5 for privileged users) to reduce the risk of session hijacking or unnoticed unauthorized access.

evidence_required.description: Concurrent session limit configuration.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Both controls manage active session lifecycle.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Prevent further access by initiating a device lock after an organization-defined time period of inactivity or upon user request, and retain the lock until the user re-authenticates.
nist_800_53.discussion: Device locks are temporary actions to prevent logical access, not a substitute for logging out, particularly at the end of the workday.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a device lock is initiated after a defined period of inactivity or upon request.
Determine if the lock is retained until the user re-authenticates.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Conceal, via the device lock, information previously visible on the display with a publicly viewable image.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: When the screen locks, it doesn't just dim or freeze on the last screen — it shows something generic like a screensaver pattern or blank screen so nobody can read sensitive information that was on-screen before the lock triggered.

evidence_required.description: Screen lock configuration showing a concealing image/screensaver rather than the frozen application view.

va_odp_values.value: 15 minutes (extensions for specific individuals require Information System Owner/CIO approval)

va_overlay.mapping_notes: VA 6500 calls this 'Session Lock' (Rev 4 naming); maps cleanly to Rev 5 AC-11 'Device Lock.'

controls.plain_english_explanation: After 15 minutes of no activity, the screen locks automatically and requires the user to log back in — this isn't the same as fully logging out, just a temporary screen block that hides what was on screen.

evidence_required.description: Screen lock / idle timeout policy configuration (e.g., Group Policy setting).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Device lock (session-level) and session termination (logical session end) are closely related but distinct controls; often configured together.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Automatically terminate a user session after organization-defined conditions or trigger events requiring session disconnect.
nist_800_53.discussion: This addresses logical session termination (as opposed to network connection termination under SC-10). Triggers can include periods of inactivity, targeted incident response, or time-of-day restrictions.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the system automatically terminates a user session after defined conditions or trigger events.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The system automatically ends a user's logical session (not just locking the screen, but fully closing it) based on defined triggers such as prolonged inactivity or a security event.

evidence_required.description: Session timeout/termination configuration.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Session termination (logical) and network disconnect (SC-10) are often implemented via the same timeout mechanism.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Withdrawn; incorporated into AC-2 and AU-6.
nist_800_53.discussion: This control was withdrawn in a prior revision and its requirements folded into AC-2 (Account Management) and AU-6 (Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting).

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Withdrawn control; not separately tracked by VA 6500.

controls.plain_english_explanation: This control no longer exists on its own — its requirements are now covered under Account Management (AC-2) and Audit Review (AU-6).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Absorbed this withdrawn control's requirements.
Absorbed this withdrawn control's requirements.

controls.control_name: Permitted Actions Without Identification or Authentication

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify user actions that can be performed without identification or authentication consistent with organizational missions, and document the rationale in the security plan.
nist_800_53.discussion: Examples include public website access, or receiving a fax. This does not apply to situations requiring identification/authentication for related administrative purposes.
assessment_objectives: Determine if user actions performable without identification/authentication are identified and the rationale documented.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA also defines a formal emergency access procedure allowing supervisory review of a departed/unavailable employee's account under documented, approved, and audited circumstances (e.g., justification, ISO coordination, logging of all activity, restoration to original state afterward).
va_specific_requirements: Emergency access requests require documented justification and CIO-level approval per VA's defined process.
All emergency access activity must be logged and access restored to original state upon completion.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping; VA adds a specific emergency-access procedure not detailed in the generic NIST control.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Some very limited actions (like viewing a public website) don't require anyone to log in first — but the organization must explicitly document which actions these are and why. VA also has a formal, audited process for supervisors to access a departed employee's files in emergencies without needing that employee's login.

evidence_required.description: List of permitted unauthenticated actions and rationale, documented in the SSP.
Emergency access request/approval procedure.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Publicly accessible content controls overlap with permitted unauthenticated actions on public-facing systems.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Withdrawn; incorporated into MP-3.
nist_800_53.discussion: Requirements folded into MP-3 (Media Marking).

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Withdrawn control; not separately tracked by VA 6500.

controls.plain_english_explanation: This control no longer exists on its own — its requirements are now covered under Media Marking (MP-3).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Absorbed this withdrawn control's requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide the means to associate defined security/privacy attributes with information in storage, in process, and in transmission.
nist_800_53.discussion: Establishes permitted attributes and their values/ranges.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would involve tagging data with security/privacy labels that follow it through storage and transmission.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish and document usage restrictions, configuration/connection requirements, and implementation guidance for each type of remote access allowed; authorize remote access prior to allowing connections.
nist_800_53.discussion: Remote access is access by users communicating through an external network such as the internet. Includes dial-up, broadband, and wireless.
assessment_objectives: Determine if usage restrictions and configuration/connection requirements are established for each type of remote access.
Determine if remote access is authorized prior to allowing connections.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automated mechanisms to monitor and control remote access methods.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Remote access connections (VPN, remote desktop, etc.) are automatically monitored and controlled by tools, not just governed by a written policy — so unusual or unauthorized remote sessions can be detected and cut off.

evidence_required.description: Remote access monitoring tool logs/dashboard.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Protection of Confidentiality and Integrity Using Encryption

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality and integrity of remote access sessions.

va_odp_values.value: FIPS 140-2 (or successor) validated encryption

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Data traveling over a remote access connection (like a VPN tunnel) is encrypted using federally-validated encryption, so it can't be read or altered by someone intercepting the traffic.

evidence_required.description: VPN/remote access encryption configuration showing FIPS 140-2 validated cipher suites.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Route all remote accesses through authorized and managed network access control points.

va_odp_values.value: VA-approved Trusted Internet Connection (TIC) gateways or approved connections

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: All remote connections must funnel through a small number of approved, monitored gateways (VA's TIC connections) rather than allowing many scattered, unmonitored entry points into the network.

evidence_required.description: Network diagram showing remote access routed exclusively through approved TIC gateways.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Authorize execution of privileged commands and access to security-relevant information via remote access only for defined needs, documenting rationale.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Running admin-level commands remotely (rather than being physically present at the machine) is restricted to specific, justified needs — this isn't something any remote user can casually do.

evidence_required.description: SSP documentation justifying remote privileged command access.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA has an extensive remote access implementation section covering: prohibition on simultaneous VA/non-VA network connections, restrictions on dial-up (must use FIPS 140-2 validated encryption or written authorization), international travel notification requirements, restricted-country access prohibitions absent authorization, and a defined request/approval workflow through supervisor, ISO, and Information System Owner.
va_specific_requirements: Users may not simultaneously maintain a VA network connection and any non-VA network connection unless explicitly authorized.
Remote access requests require supervisor approval and ISO/Information System Owner review before granting.
Users must notify supervisor/ISO/Information System Owner prior to international travel with a mobile device.
Access to VA's internal network from certain restricted countries is prohibited absent documented risk-based authorization.
ISOs are responsible for auditing remote access authorizations.
Remote access privileges must be terminated promptly upon employee separation, transfer, or when access is no longer needed.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping across base and enhancements; VA's implementation guidance for this control is unusually extensive relative to most other AC controls.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Anyone connecting to VA systems from outside the office (via VPN, dial-up, etc.) must be explicitly authorized in advance, and the connection must be encrypted and routed through approved gateways. VA adds strict rules: no mixing VA and personal network connections at the same time, mandatory notice before international travel with VA devices, and prohibited access from certain high-risk countries without special approval.

evidence_required.description: Remote access policy defining allowed methods and restrictions.
VPN/remote access gateway configuration; encryption configuration (FIPS 140-2 validation).
Remote access request/approval forms signed by supervisor and ISO.
ISO's periodic audit of remote access authorizations.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Wireless access is a subtype of remote access and shares authorization/encryption requirements.
Mobile device access control shares the same remote-connection authorization workflow.
Remote access requires multi-factor authentication per IA-2 enhancements.
FIPS 140-2 validated encryption requirement is shared between remote access and general cryptographic protection.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish usage restrictions, configuration/connection requirements, and implementation guidance for wireless access; authorize wireless access prior to allowing connections.
nist_800_53.discussion: Wireless technologies include microwave, satellite, packet radio, 802.11x, and Bluetooth.
assessment_objectives: Determine if usage restrictions and connection requirements are established for wireless access.
Determine if wireless access is authorized prior to allowing connections.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Protect wireless access using authentication and encryption.

va_odp_values.value: FIPS 140-2 (or successor) validated encryption

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Wi-Fi connections require both a login/authentication step and encryption of the traffic — an attacker within radio range can't just connect or eavesdrop without both a valid credential and breaking the encryption.

evidence_required.description: Wireless access point authentication/encryption configuration (e.g., WPA2/3-Enterprise with FIPS validated encryption).

nist_800_53.control_statement: Disable, when not intended for use, wireless networking capabilities internally embedded within system components.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: VA 6500 does not separately allocate a matching enhancement; superseded/renumbered relative to Rev 4 source. Best-effort: conceptually covered by VA's general wireless restriction guidance under base AC-18.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Not separately allocated by VA — this would require disabling built-in wireless radios on devices that aren't supposed to use wireless at all (e.g., a desktop with a Wi-Fi card that should stay wired-only).

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify and explicitly authorize users allowed to independently configure wireless networking capabilities.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, regular users can't just turn on or reconfigure their device's wireless settings themselves — only specifically authorized individuals can change wireless configuration.

evidence_required.description: List of individuals authorized to independently configure wireless settings.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Select radio antennas and calibrate transmission power to reduce probability of signals being received outside organization-controlled boundaries.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Wireless access points are configured with directional antennas and reduced power levels so the Wi-Fi signal doesn't reach far outside the physical building where someone could intercept it from the parking lot.

evidence_required.description: Wireless signal survey/antenna calibration documentation.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Operating Units must follow VA Directive 6512, Secure Wireless Technology. Wireless devices must be kept current on anti-viral/security patches. Actions to limit unauthorized reception include reducing transmission power, using TEMPEST controls, and directional antennas.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping for base control and most enhancements; AC-18(3) (Disable Wireless Networking) has no distinct VA 6500 allocation, flagged above.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Wireless connections (Wi-Fi, Bluetooth, etc.) to VA systems must be authorized, encrypted, and configured to limit how far the signal reaches outside the building — reducing the chance someone outside could intercept it.

evidence_required.description: Wireless access policy (VA Directive 6512 compliance).
Wireless access point configuration showing encryption and authentication settings.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Wireless is a form of remote access and shares authorization/encryption evidence.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish usage restrictions, configuration requirements, connection requirements, and implementation guidance for organization-controlled mobile devices; authorize connection of mobile devices.
nist_800_53.discussion: Mobile devices include smartphones and tablets. Devices with limited storage or communication capability may not be subject to full requirements.
assessment_objectives: Determine if usage restrictions and configuration requirements are established for mobile devices.
Determine if connection of mobile devices is authorized.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ full-device or container encryption to protect confidentiality/integrity of information on mobile devices.

va_odp_values.value: FIPS 140-2 (or successor) validated encryption; full-device or TRM-approved container encryption

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping; VA applies this enhancement at Low as well, which is broader than the generic Rev 5 baseline allocation (Moderate/High only) — VA's baseline table explicitly lists AC-19(5) at Low.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Every phone, tablet, or laptop that holds VA data must have its entire storage encrypted (or use an approved secure container/app-wrapping solution) — if the device is lost or stolen, the data on it remains unreadable.

evidence_required.description: MDM configuration showing enforced full-device or container encryption on all mobile devices.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: All VA-owned mobile devices storing/transmitting VA data must be encrypted (FIPS 140-2 or successor validated), either via full-device encryption or a validated container/wrapping solution. Devices used internationally require notification and may require reimaging upon return. Non-VA-approved USB flash drives are prohibited; only FIPS 140-2 validated USB devices are permitted.
va_specific_requirements: Supervisor documentation required for storing VA sensitive information on a mobile/portable storage device.
ISO and Information System Owner must approve/document mobile or portable storage device use.
International travel with a mobile device requires prior notification to supervisor/ISO/Information System Owner.
Only FIPS 140-2 (or successor) validated USB flash drives permitted; non-approved drives prohibited.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: VA notably applies the encryption enhancement AC-19(5) even at the Low baseline, exceeding the generic Rev 5 allocation.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Phones, tablets, and laptops that connect to VA systems and hold VA data must be encrypted, and their use must be pre-approved. VA is stricter than the generic federal baseline here — even 'Low' impact systems must have encrypted mobile devices, and only VA-approved encrypted USB drives are allowed.

evidence_required.description: Mobile device management policy.
MDM configuration showing enforced encryption on mobile devices.
Supervisor/ISO documentation approving mobile/portable storage device use.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Media use restrictions for portable storage devices overlap heavily with mobile device access control.
FIPS 140-2 encryption requirement shared with general cryptographic protection control.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish terms and conditions for authorized individuals to access the system from external systems, and to process/store/transmit organization-controlled information using external systems.
nist_800_53.discussion: External systems are outside the organization's authorization boundary, and the organization typically has no direct control over the security controls applied to them.
assessment_objectives: Determine if terms and conditions are established for authorized individuals to access the system from external systems.
Determine if terms and conditions are established for processing/storing/transmitting information using external systems.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Permit authorized individuals to use an external system only when the organization can verify required security controls or retains approved connection/processing agreements.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Before someone can use an outside system (like a partner agency's network) to access VA data, the organization must either verify that system meets the required security controls or have a signed agreement in place covering it.

evidence_required.description: Connection/processing agreement or security control verification for the external system.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Restrict or prohibit the use of organization-controlled portable storage devices by authorized individuals on external systems.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: VA-owned USB drives or other portable storage carrying VA data generally can't be plugged into non-VA computers/systems, to prevent VA data from ending up on uncontrolled external systems.

evidence_required.description: Policy restricting VA portable storage device use on external/non-VA systems.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Security controls/requirements for external systems must be documented in an MOU/ISA, contract, or other agreement (e.g., Data Use Agreement). Personally-owned information systems may not be used on-site to perform official duties without Information System Owner/local CIO approval.
va_specific_requirements: MOU/ISA or contract required documenting security requirements before connecting external systems.
Personally-owned devices require explicit approval before performing official duties on-site.

controls.plain_english_explanation: If someone wants to access VA systems from a device or network VA doesn't own or control (e.g., a personal laptop or a partner organization's system), there must be a documented agreement in place first spelling out the security requirements that device/network must meet.

evidence_required.description: MOU/ISA, contract, or Data Use Agreement documenting external system security requirements.
Information System Owner/CIO approval for personally-owned device use on-site.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System interconnection agreements (ISAs) are the same artifact referenced by both AC-20 and CA-3.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Enable authorized users to determine whether access authorizations assigned to a sharing partner match access restrictions on the information, for circumstances requiring user discretion; employ mechanisms or manual processes to assist in information-sharing decisions.
nist_800_53.discussion: Applies to information that may be restricted in some manner (e.g., privileged medical information, proprietary information, PII).
assessment_objectives: Determine if authorized users can determine whether sharing partner access authorizations match information access restrictions.
Determine if mechanisms/processes assist users in making information-sharing decisions.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Information System Owners must confirm VA Privacy requirements and other mission/business process requirements (VHA, VBA, NCA) are met before enabling electronic data sharing. Privacy Officers manually review/approve data sharing to confirm legal authority and privacy compliance.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Before sharing information with another party, someone has to verify the recipient is actually authorized to see it — VA requires the Privacy Officer to manually review and approve data-sharing arrangements to confirm there's legal authority to share.

evidence_required.description: Data Use Agreement, MOU/ISA, or contract governing the information sharing.
Privacy Officer review/approval of the data-sharing arrangement.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Information flow enforcement technically implements decisions made under information sharing controls.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Designate individuals authorized to post information onto a publicly accessible system; train them to ensure no non-public information is included; review proposed content before posting; and review existing content periodically, removing non-public information if discovered.
nist_800_53.discussion: This control addresses systems controlled by the organization and accessible to the public, typically without identification/authentication.
assessment_objectives: Determine if individuals are designated as authorized to post to publicly accessible systems.
Determine if those individuals are trained to ensure no non-public information is included.
Determine if content is reviewed prior to posting.
Determine if existing content is periodically reviewed and non-public information removed if found.

va_odp_values.value: As discovered, or no less than quarterly

controls.plain_english_explanation: Only specific, trained people are allowed to post content to public-facing VA websites, and someone reviews what's posted (and periodically re-reviews what's already posted) to make sure no private or sensitive information accidentally ends up public.

evidence_required.description: List of individuals authorized to post to public systems.
Training records for authorized content publishers.
Quarterly (or more frequent) public content review log.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Both controls govern what's accessible without authentication.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ data mining prevention/detection techniques for data storage objects.
nist_800_53.discussion: Protects against unauthorized data mining/harvesting of sensitive information.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this control would address protecting against unauthorized bulk extraction/analysis of stored data.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish procedures to ensure access control decisions are applied to each access request prior to access enforcement.
nist_800_53.discussion: Separates the decision-making function from the enforcement function in some architectures.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement a reference monitor for access control policies that is tamperproof, always invoked, and small enough to be subject to analysis/testing.
nist_800_53.discussion: A high-assurance architectural concept typically applied to specialized high-security systems.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — a specialized, high-assurance access enforcement architecture not typically used outside specialized high-security systems.

control_families.family_description: Governs security and privacy awareness training for all users, and role-based training for personnel with significant security responsibilities.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate an awareness and training policy and procedures; review and update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Security awareness and training policy addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance.
assessment_objectives: Determine if an awareness and training policy is developed, documented, and disseminated.
Determine if awareness and training procedures are developed, documented, and disseminated.
Determine if the policy and procedures are reviewed and updated at a defined frequency.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written policy describing its security awareness and training program, reviewed periodically rather than left static.

evidence_required.description: Security awareness and training policy.
Local training procedures.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same policy/procedure documentation and 5-year review pattern.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide security and privacy literacy training to system users as part of initial training, when required by system changes, and thereafter at a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Awareness techniques include displays, alerts, computer-based training, and phishing simulations. This control also addresses awareness of social engineering and social mining given the increasing use of social media.
assessment_objectives: Determine if literacy training is provided as part of initial training for new users.
Determine if literacy training is provided when required by system changes.
Determine if literacy training is provided at a defined frequency thereafter.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential indicators of insider threat.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Security awareness training includes specific content on recognizing warning signs of an insider threat (like a disgruntled coworker exhibiting unusual data access patterns) and how to report those concerns.

evidence_required.description: Training materials/completion records showing insider threat awareness content.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide awareness training on recognizing and reporting potential and actual instances of social engineering and social mining.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not separately allocated in VA 6500 (Rev 4-based); conceptually folded into VA's general security awareness training content.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Not separately allocated by VA as a distinct enhancement — though social engineering awareness is typically covered within VA's general annual security awareness training content rather than as its own dedicated module.

va_odp_values.value: Annually thereafter

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: All users of VA information or information systems must complete VA-approved security and privacy awareness training as part of initial access, upon significant system change, and annually thereafter. Failure to complete training may result in suspension of access. VA provides training reciprocity for other Federal agency employees who complete FISMA-compliant training at their own agency, provided they still sign VA's Rules of Behavior.
va_specific_requirements: Failure to complete required training may result in suspension/termination of access.
Reciprocity available for other Federal agency employees with equivalent annual training, contingent on signing VA ROB.
If a reciprocity employee causes an unauthorized disclosure, they must complete VA's full security/privacy training as part of incident remediation.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Everyone who uses VA systems must complete security/privacy awareness training when they start, whenever there's a major system change, and then every year after that. Skipping it can get your access suspended.

evidence_required.description: Completion records for initial and annual security/privacy awareness training (e.g., TMS transcripts).
Training policy specifying frequency and consequences of non-completion.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Rules of Behavior signature is often bundled with the same training event.
Role-based training builds on the same TMS record-keeping infrastructure as general awareness training.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide role-based security and privacy training to personnel with assigned security/privacy roles and responsibilities before authorizing access, when required by system changes, and thereafter at a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Role-based training is tied to the specific duties personnel perform; system administrators, developers, and privacy officers require different training content than general users.
assessment_objectives: Determine if role-based training is provided before authorizing access, when required by changes, and at a defined frequency thereafter.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Information Assurance is a core competency across OI&T competency models. Role-based training is assigned via TMS based on manager/supervisor/COR discretion as cybersecurity duties of a position change (e.g., system administrators, network administrators, database administrators receive elevated-proficiency training).

controls.plain_english_explanation: People with specialized security responsibilities (system admins, database admins, privacy officers, etc.) need training specific to their role — beyond the general awareness training everyone gets.

evidence_required.description: Role-based training completion records tied to specific job functions.
Mapping of roles/positions to required role-based training modules.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Position risk designation determines which role-based training is required.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Document and monitor individual information security and privacy training, including basic awareness training and specific system training; retain records for a defined time period.
nist_800_53.discussion: Training records provide evidence of compliance with training requirements.
assessment_objectives: Determine if individual training activities are documented and monitored.
Determine if training records are retained for a defined time period.

va_odp_values.value: 7 years

controls.plain_english_explanation: Records of who completed what training and when must be kept and retained — VA specifies 7 years.

evidence_required.description: TMS training transcripts/records retained per the defined schedule.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Training records are the direct evidentiary output of AT-2 training completion.

controls.control_name: Contacts with Security Groups and Associations

nist_800_53.control_statement: Withdrawn; incorporated into PM-15.
nist_800_53.discussion: Requirements folded into PM-15 (Contacts with Security Groups and Associations).

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Withdrawn control; VA 6500 tracks this under PM-15 (Attachment 1, common controls).

controls.plain_english_explanation: This control no longer exists on its own — its requirements are now covered under Program Management's PM-15 (Contacts with Security Groups and Associations).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Absorbed this withdrawn control's requirements.

control_families.family_description: Governs the generation, review, protection, and retention of audit records to support accountability, incident investigation, and non-repudiation.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate an audit and accountability policy and procedures; review and update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for the audit function.
assessment_objectives: Determine if audit and accountability policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written audit and accountability policy, reviewed periodically.

evidence_required.description: Audit and accountability policy document.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares same policy documentation pattern and review cadence.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify the types of events the system is capable of logging; coordinate the event logging function with other organizational entities; provide rationale for why the events are adequate; and determine which events require logging, including frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Event types include password changes, failed logons, and administrator actions. The organization considers which events are auditable on an ongoing basis based on current threat information.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the system is capable of auditing the defined events.
Determine if the audit function is coordinated with other organizational entities.
Determine if rationale for adequacy of auditable events is documented.
Determine if events to be audited, including frequency, are determined.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Review and update the events to be logged.

va_odp_values.value: Annually or following an incident

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The list of what gets logged isn't set once and forgotten — it's revisited at least annually (or right after an incident) to make sure it still captures the right events as threats and systems evolve.

evidence_required.description: Annual (or post-incident) review record of the auditable events list.

va_odp_values.value: At minimum: system admin/operator actions, printed output production, object creation/deletion in user address space, security-relevant events, configuration activities, privilege use events, identification/authentication events, user identifier settings
Quarterly for Low; monthly for Moderate; weekly for High; immediate when threat identified for all levels

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must decide what kinds of events its systems will log (like failed logins, privilege use, configuration changes), justify why that list is sufficient, and periodically revisit that list as threats evolve.

evidence_required.description: List of defined auditable events and justification for adequacy.
Periodic review/update record for the auditable events list.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: AU-12 (Audit Generation) implements the event types defined in AU-2.
Account management actions are a category of events defined under AU-2.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Ensure audit records contain information establishing what type of event occurred, when, where, the source, the outcome, and identity of individuals/subjects involved.
nist_800_53.discussion: Audit record content includes time stamps, source/destination addresses, user/process identifiers, event descriptions, and success/fail indications.
assessment_objectives: Determine if audit records contain sufficient information to establish event type, time, location, source, outcome, and identity of associated individuals/subjects.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Generate audit records containing additional, more detailed information.

va_odp_values.value: Individual identities of group account users

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: When a shared/group account is used, the logs still capture which specific individual actually performed the action, not just that 'the shared account' did something.

evidence_required.description: Sample audit log showing individual identity attribution for group account activity.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Centralized Management of Planned Audit Record Content

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide centralized management and configuration of the content captured in audit records.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, what gets recorded in logs is managed from a central location rather than each individual server/component being configured separately, ensuring consistency across the system.

evidence_required.description: Centralized logging management console configuration.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Audit logs must be sufficiently detailed to reconstruct events, treated as restricted/limited-access information, backed up and stored securely, and retired per the approved records schedule.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Logs must record enough detail — who, what, when, where, and whether the action succeeded — to actually reconstruct what happened during an investigation.

evidence_required.description: Sample audit log output demonstrating required fields are captured.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Time stamps required in audit record content are governed in detail by AU-8.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Allocate audit log storage capacity to accommodate defined audit log retention requirements.
nist_800_53.discussion: Sufficient storage capacity reduces the likelihood of exceeding capacity and losing audit data.
assessment_objectives: Determine if audit log storage capacity is allocated in accordance with retention requirements.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping; Information System Owner defines capacity based on operational needs.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Systems need enough storage set aside for logs so that logs aren't lost or overwritten before they're supposed to be retained.

evidence_required.description: Log storage allocation configuration/sizing documentation.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Storage capacity must accommodate the retention period defined in AU-11.

controls.control_name: Response to Audit Logging Process Failures

nist_800_53.control_statement: Alert defined personnel/roles in the event of an audit logging process failure, and take defined additional actions.
nist_800_53.discussion: Audit processing failures include software/hardware errors, failures in audit capturing mechanisms, and audit storage reaching/exceeding capacity.
assessment_objectives: Determine if defined personnel/roles are alerted in the event of an audit logging process failure.
Determine if additional defined actions are taken in the event of a failure.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide a warning when allocated audit record storage volume reaches a defined percentage of maximum capacity.

va_odp_values.value: 75% of repository maximum audit record storage capacity

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Before log storage actually fills up, an alert goes out at 75% capacity, giving administrators time to expand storage or archive old logs before anything is lost.

evidence_required.description: Storage capacity alert threshold configuration (set at 75%).

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide a real-time alert when defined audit failure events occur.

va_odp_values.value: Immediately

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: If the audit logging system itself fails, administrators are notified immediately (in real time), not discovered days later during a routine check.

evidence_required.description: Real-time alert configuration and sample alert notification for audit failure events.

controls.plain_english_explanation: If the logging system itself fails (e.g., runs out of storage or crashes), someone must be alerted immediately, and the system takes a defined action (like alerting admins or stopping certain processing) rather than silently losing audit data.

evidence_required.description: Audit failure alerting configuration.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Storage capacity warnings directly relate to the capacity allocated under AU-4.

controls.control_name: Audit Record Review, Analysis, and Reporting

nist_800_53.control_statement: Review and analyze system audit records for indications of inappropriate or unusual activity and report findings to defined personnel/roles.
nist_800_53.discussion: Audit review covers monitoring of account usage, remote access, wireless connectivity, mobile device connections, configuration settings, and more.
assessment_objectives: Determine if audit records are reviewed and analyzed for indications of inappropriate/unusual activity.
Determine if findings are reported to defined personnel/roles.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Integrate audit record review, analysis, and reporting using automated mechanisms.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Reviewing and analyzing logs isn't a fully manual process — automated tools (like a SIEM) help pull together, correlate, and flag findings from audit records for analysts.

evidence_required.description: SIEM/log analysis tool configuration and sample automated analysis output.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Analyze and correlate audit records across different repositories for organization-wide situational awareness.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Logs from different systems and sources aren't reviewed in isolation — they're correlated together to build a fuller, organization-wide picture of what's happening (e.g., linking a failed login on one system to suspicious network traffic on another).

evidence_required.description: Cross-repository log correlation reports/dashboard.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Integrate analysis of audit records with vulnerability scanning, performance data, and system monitoring information.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Audit log analysis is combined with other data sources like vulnerability scan results and performance metrics, giving a richer picture — for example, connecting unusual log activity with a known unpatched vulnerability on that same system.

evidence_required.description: Integrated analysis report combining audit logs with vulnerability/performance/monitoring data.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Correlate audit record information with physical access monitoring information.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Digital log data is cross-referenced with physical access records (like badge swipe logs) — for example, flagging a system login that occurred while the associated employee's badge shows they weren't physically in the building.

evidence_required.description: Correlated report linking audit logs with physical access control system data.

va_odp_values.value: At least weekly

controls.plain_english_explanation: Someone must actually look at the logs on a regular basis (at least weekly at VA) and flag anything unusual, then report those findings to the right people — collecting logs is useless if nobody reviews them.

evidence_required.description: Weekly (or more frequent) audit log review/analysis reports.
SIEM or log correlation tool output demonstrating automated analysis.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Audit review and information system monitoring are closely related and often use the same tooling (SIEM).
Findings from audit review feed directly into incident handling.

controls.control_name: Audit Record Reduction and Report Generation

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide an audit record reduction and report generation capability that supports on-demand review/analysis/reporting and does not alter original content or time ordering.
nist_800_53.discussion: Audit reduction is a process that manipulates collected audit information into a more meaningful summary format for analysts.
assessment_objectives: Determine if an audit reduction and report generation capability is provided.
Determine if the capability supports on-demand review and after-the-fact investigation.
Determine if the capability does not alter original content or time ordering of audit records.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide the capability to process audit records for events of interest based on defined audit fields within audit records.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The logging system can automatically filter and pull out records matching specific criteria (like all failed logins from a particular IP address), rather than requiring an analyst to manually search through every log entry.

evidence_required.description: Sample filtered/processed audit report based on defined search criteria.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The system can generate readable, summarized reports from raw audit logs (rather than requiring someone to manually sift through massive log files), and the summarization tools cannot alter or falsify the underlying original logs.

evidence_required.description: Sample audit reduction/report generation output.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Reduction/reporting tools directly support the review and analysis required by AU-6.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Use internal system clocks to generate time stamps for audit records, and record time stamps that can be mapped to UTC or GMT, meeting a defined granularity.
nist_800_53.discussion: Time stamps include both date and time and may be expressed as UTC, GMT, or local time with an offset.
assessment_objectives: Determine if internal system clocks are used to generate time stamps.
Determine if time stamps can be mapped to UTC/GMT and meet a defined granularity.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Compare internal system clocks with a defined authoritative time source and synchronize when the time difference exceeds a defined threshold.

va_odp_values.value: Reset to default authoritative source if time sync varies by more than two minutes

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The system's internal clock is regularly checked against an authoritative time source (like an NTP server), and automatically corrected if it drifts by more than two minutes — ensuring timestamps across all systems stay consistent for investigations.

evidence_required.description: NTP synchronization configuration with drift-correction threshold.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Every log entry must have an accurate, synchronized timestamp — without this, correlating events across different systems during an investigation becomes nearly impossible.

evidence_required.description: NTP/time synchronization configuration.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Time stamps are a required field of audit record content under AU-3.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Protect audit information and audit logging tools from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion.
