nist_800_53.discussion: Audit information includes audit records, settings, and reports. This control focuses on technical protection of that information.
assessment_objectives: Determine if audit information and audit logging tools are protected from unauthorized access, modification, and deletion.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Store on Separate Physical Systems or Components

nist_800_53.control_statement: Back up audit records onto a physically different system or component than the system being audited.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Audit log backups are stored on a completely separate physical system, so if the original system is compromised (and its local logs deleted or altered), an untouched copy still exists elsewhere.

evidence_required.description: Log backup configuration showing storage on a separate physical system.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to protect the integrity of audit information and audit tools.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Audit logs are cryptographically protected (e.g., with hashes or digital signatures) so any tampering with the log content would be detectable.

evidence_required.description: Cryptographic integrity protection mechanism (hashing/signing) applied to audit logs.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Access by Subset of Privileged Users

nist_800_53.control_statement: Authorize access to management of audit logging functionality to only a subset of privileged users.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Not every system administrator can manage the audit logging configuration — that ability is restricted to a small, specific group, reducing the risk that a compromised admin account could tamper with the logging system itself.

evidence_required.description: List of the specific subset of privileged users authorized to manage audit logging functionality.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Audit logs themselves must be protected from tampering — even a system administrator shouldn't necessarily be able to alter or delete the logs that would record their own actions. Access to manage the audit function is restricted to a small, specific subset of trusted individuals.

evidence_required.description: Access control configuration restricting audit log management access.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Restricting audit management to a privileged subset is an application of least privilege.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Protect against an individual (or process acting on behalf of an individual) falsely denying having performed actions covered by non-repudiation.
nist_800_53.discussion: Types of actions covered include creating information, sending/receiving messages, and approving information. Techniques include digital signatures and digital message receipts.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the system protects against an individual falsely denying having performed actions covered by non-repudiation.

controls.plain_english_explanation: For high-risk systems, there must be a way to prove someone actually performed a specific action (like signing a document or approving a transaction) so they can't later falsely deny having done it — typically implemented via digital signatures.

evidence_required.description: Digital signature/non-repudiation mechanism configuration.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Non-repudiation techniques rely on the same cryptographic protection mechanisms.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Retain audit records for a defined time period to support after-the-fact investigations and to meet regulatory/organizational retention requirements.
nist_800_53.discussion: Includes retention relative to Freedom of Information Act requests, subpoenas, and law enforcement actions. NARA General Records Schedules provide federal retention policy.
assessment_objectives: Determine if audit records are retained for a defined time period.

va_odp_values.value: Minimum 1 year, or per NARA/HIPAA retention schedule, whichever is greater; audit logs describing a security breach retained 6 years (HIPAA)

controls.plain_english_explanation: Logs must be kept for a set minimum period so they're available if needed for an investigation later — VA requires at least a year, longer (6 years) if the logs relate to a security breach involving health information.

evidence_required.description: Audit log retention policy/schedule.
Evidence of retained historical logs matching the retention schedule.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Storage capacity must be sized to accommodate this retention period.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide audit record generation capability for the events defined in AU-2, at defined system components; allow designated personnel to select which auditable events are audited by specific components; generate audit records with content defined in AU-3.
nist_800_53.discussion: Audit records can be generated from many different system components; the events audited are typically a subset of all events the system is capable of auditing.
assessment_objectives: Determine if audit record generation capability is provided for defined events at defined components.
Determine if designated personnel can select which auditable events are audited by specific components.
Determine if audit records are generated with the content defined in AU-3.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Compile audit records from defined system components into a system-wide, time-correlated audit trail.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Logs from different components across the system (servers, network devices, applications) are pulled together into one unified, chronologically-ordered trail, making it possible to reconstruct a sequence of events across the whole system.

evidence_required.description: Sample system-wide, time-correlated audit trail output.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide the capability for designated personnel to change the auditing performed on system components based on selectable event criteria.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Authorized personnel have the ability to adjust what specific events get logged on individual system components, giving flexibility to tighten or focus logging when investigating a specific concern.

evidence_required.description: List of personnel authorized to modify auditing configuration, with change records.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The technical capability to actually generate audit logs must exist at the system/component level (servers, network devices, etc.), matching the event types and content requirements defined elsewhere in this family.

evidence_required.description: Audit logging configuration on representative system components.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Implements the event list defined by AU-2.
Generated records must contain the content required by AU-3.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Monitor open source information and/or information sites for evidence of unauthorized exfiltration or disclosure of organizational information.
nist_800_53.discussion: Involves scanning public sources (paste sites, forums, social media) for leaked organizational data.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time; OI&T may elect to monitor for information disclosure at their discretion.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would involve actively scanning public sources like paste sites or forums for leaked VA data.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide the capability for authorized users to select a user session to capture/record or view/hear.
nist_800_53.discussion: Typically used for high-assurance monitoring of specific user sessions in real time or after the fact.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would allow authorized staff to record or watch a specific user's session in real time.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide an alternate audit capability in the event of a failure in the primary audit capability.
nist_800_53.discussion: Ensures continuity of audit logging even if the primary logging mechanism fails.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would provide a backup logging mechanism if the primary one fails.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ methods for coordinating audit information among external organizations when audit information is transmitted across organizational boundaries.
nist_800_53.discussion: Relevant when systems span multiple organizations and audit data needs to be correlated across those boundaries.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would coordinate audit log sharing when a system spans multiple organizations.

control_families.family_description: Governs how security controls are assessed, how systems are authorized to operate, how systems interconnect, and how continuous monitoring is performed.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate an assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and procedures; review/update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for the CA family.
assessment_objectives: Determine if assessment, authorization, and monitoring policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written policy governing how it assesses controls, authorizes systems to operate, and continuously monitors them.

evidence_required.description: Security assessment and authorization policy.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same policy documentation pattern.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop a control assessment plan; assess controls to determine the extent to which they are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome; produce a security assessment report; provide results to defined personnel/roles.
nist_800_53.discussion: Assessments may also check non-security functions to ensure they do not introduce vulnerabilities.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a control assessment plan is developed.
Determine if controls are assessed to determine correct implementation and effectiveness.
Determine if a security assessment report documenting results is produced.
Determine if assessment results are provided to defined personnel/roles.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ independent assessors or assessment teams to conduct control assessments.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: External assessors, or internal assessors outside of OIS.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Security controls are assessed by someone independent of the team that built or operates the system (either an external firm or an internal team outside OIS), so the assessment isn't just self-graded by the people responsible for the controls.

evidence_required.description: Documentation identifying the independent assessor/team and confirming their independence from the system being assessed.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Include specialized assessment types (e.g., in-depth monitoring, vulnerability scanning, malicious user testing, penetration testing) as part of control assessments.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: As part of initial security authorizations and continuous monitoring, OIS with Service Delivery and Engineering performs announced/unannounced assessments including in-depth monitoring, vulnerability scanning, malicious user testing, insider threat assessments, and performance/load testing.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For high-risk systems, control assessments go beyond a paperwork review — they include hands-on specialized testing like vulnerability scans, simulated malicious-user activity, and load testing, sometimes conducted without advance warning to the system team.

evidence_required.description: Reports from specialized assessment activities (vulnerability scanning, malicious user testing, etc.).

nist_800_53.control_statement: Leverage the results of control assessments performed by external organizations on a system when the assessment meets defined requirements.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA as a distinct enhancement — this would allow reusing another organization's assessment results (e.g., a cloud provider's independent audit) instead of conducting a fully separate assessment.

va_odp_values.value: Prior to receiving initial authorization; when significant/major changes require reauthorization; continuously per Information Security Continuous Monitoring program requirements

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping. See VA Handbook 6500.3 for additional detail on the A&A process.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Security controls aren't just implemented and forgotten — someone must actually test whether they work as intended, document the results in a formal report, and share that report with relevant stakeholders (system owner, ISO, etc.).

evidence_required.description: Security control assessment plan (scope, procedures, roles).
Security assessment report (SAR) documenting results and findings.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Findings from assessments feed directly into the POA&M process.
Vulnerability scanning is often a component of the broader control assessment.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Approve and manage the exchange of information between the system and other systems using interconnection security agreements, mapping and documenting interface characteristics, security requirements, and the nature of the information communicated; review and update agreements on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: This applies to dedicated connections between systems (system interconnections), not transitory user-controlled connections like email or web browsing.
assessment_objectives: Determine if information exchange is approved and managed via interconnection security agreements.
Determine if interface characteristics, security requirements, and nature of the information are documented.
Determine if agreements are reviewed and updated on a defined frequency.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ a deny-all, permit-by-exception policy for allowing systems to connect to external systems.

va_odp_values.value: Permit-by-exception for VA-owned systems

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: By default, VA systems cannot connect to any external system — a connection is only allowed as a specific, documented exception, not the other way around (deny-all rather than allow-all).

evidence_required.description: Firewall/network policy configuration demonstrating deny-all, permit-by-exception for external connections.

va_odp_values.value: Annually

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: An MOU (terms/conditions for sharing data) and an ISA (technical/security requirements) are required for each external connection, approved by the Information System Owner/CIO/designee and ISO, in coordination with the Enterprise Security Change Control Board. VA Handbook 6500.6 governs contractor systems. If interconnecting systems share the same AO (VA CIO), an ISA is not required.
va_specific_requirements: MOU/ISA obtained prior to connection or data sharing.
Annual review of MOU/ISA validity and continued need.
Contractor system connections require inclusion of security/privacy language per VA Handbook 6500.6.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Any dedicated connection between VA's system and an outside system needs a documented agreement (MOU/ISA) spelling out the technical and security terms, reviewed annually to confirm it's still needed and still valid.

evidence_required.description: Signed MOU and ISA for each system interconnection.
Annual review record confirming interconnection agreements remain valid.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Use of external systems and system interconnection agreements reference the same MOU/ISA documentation.
External system services agreements overlap with interconnection security agreements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Withdrawn; incorporated into CA-2.
nist_800_53.discussion: Requirements folded into CA-2 (Control Assessments).

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Withdrawn control; VA 6500 explicitly notes this as incorporated into CA-2 (Security Assessments).

controls.plain_english_explanation: This control no longer exists on its own — its requirements are now covered under Control Assessments (CA-2).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Absorbed this withdrawn control's requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop a plan of action and milestones (POA&M) to document planned remedial actions to correct weaknesses/deficiencies and reduce/eliminate known vulnerabilities; update the POA&M based on assessment findings.
nist_800_53.discussion: The POA&M is a key document in the security authorization package and is subject to federal reporting requirements.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a POA&M is developed to document planned remedial actions.
Determine if the POA&M is updated based on findings from assessments, impact analyses, and continuous monitoring.

va_odp_values.value: At least quarterly

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: The ISO coordinates with VA officials to prepare the program-level POA&M and tracks all POA&M activity within the VA-approved FISMA database.

controls.plain_english_explanation: When an assessment finds a security weakness, the organization must document a formal plan (POA&M) for fixing it, including milestones and dates, and keep that plan updated — this is the master 'to-do list' for closing security gaps.

evidence_required.description: Current Plan of Action and Milestones tracking open findings.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: POA&M items originate from control assessment findings.
Vulnerability scan findings often become POA&M line items.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Assign a senior official as the authorizing official for the system; ensure the AO authorizes the system for processing before commencing operations and updates the authorization on a defined frequency or per triggering event.
nist_800_53.discussion: The authorization is the official management decision to accept the risk of operating the system, based on the implementation of an agreed-upon set of controls.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a senior official is assigned as the AO.
Determine if the AO authorizes the system prior to operation.
Determine if the authorization is updated per defined conditions.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: The role of Authorizing Official (AO) is assigned to the VA CIO. VA's A&A process follows NIST SP 800-37 and is further detailed in VA Handbook 6500.3. Through continuous monitoring, the authorization package is updated on an ongoing basis rather than solely via periodic re-authorization.

controls.plain_english_explanation: A designated senior official (at VA, the CIO) must formally accept the risk and authorize a system to operate before it goes live, and that authorization must be kept current as conditions change.

evidence_required.description: Signed Authority to Operate (ATO) memo/package.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Continuous monitoring supports ongoing/updated authorization decisions.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop a continuous monitoring strategy and implement a continuous monitoring program including metrics, monitoring/assessment frequencies, ongoing security status monitoring, correlation and analysis of security-related information, response actions, and reporting.
nist_800_53.discussion: A rigorous continuous monitoring program significantly reduces the level of effort required for reauthorization.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a continuous monitoring strategy and program are developed and implemented, including metrics, frequencies, ongoing status monitoring, correlation/analysis, response actions, and reporting.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ independent assessors or assessment teams to monitor controls on an ongoing basis.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Ongoing (continuous) monitoring of security controls isn't done solely by the system's own team — independent assessors are periodically involved to verify controls are still working as intended.

evidence_required.description: Documentation showing independent assessor involvement in continuous monitoring activities.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Ensure risk monitoring is an integral part of the continuous monitoring strategy, addressing effectiveness monitoring, compliance monitoring, and change monitoring.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not separately allocated in VA 6500 (Rev 4-based); conceptually addressed within VA's broader continuous monitoring program.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Not separately allocated by VA as a distinct enhancement — though VA's continuous monitoring program already covers similar ground (checking control effectiveness, compliance, and tracking changes) as part of its overall approach.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA uses a risk-based, tiered approach to testing security controls per its Information Security Continuous Monitoring Security Control Evaluation Plan, with results reported to the ISO, CIO, and Information System Owner. Self-assessments are conducted using a VA-approved FISMA database.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Rather than only checking security controls once during initial authorization, the organization continuously monitors them on an ongoing basis — different controls get checked at different frequencies based on risk tier — so problems are caught between formal reauthorizations.

evidence_required.description: Continuous monitoring strategy/plan.
Continuous monitoring dashboards/reports showing ongoing control testing per the tiered schedule.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Vulnerability scanning is a core input to the continuous monitoring program.
Continuous monitoring reduces the burden of periodic formal reassessment.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Conduct penetration testing on organization-defined systems or system components.
nist_800_53.discussion: Penetration testing typically includes pretest analysis based on full knowledge of the target system, pretest identification of potential vulnerabilities, and testing designed to determine exploitability.
assessment_objectives: Determine if penetration testing is conducted on defined systems or system components.

va_odp_values.value: Quarterly, on one-fourth of the total number of VA High-impact systems

controls.plain_english_explanation: For the organization's highest-risk systems, actual simulated attacks (penetration tests) are conducted to see whether vulnerabilities can really be exploited, not just theoretically identified.

evidence_required.description: Penetration test report/results.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Penetration testing often builds on vulnerability scan results.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Authorize internal connections of system components or classes of components to the system; document interface characteristics, security requirements, and the nature of the information communicated for each internal connection.
nist_800_53.discussion: Applies to connections between organizational systems and separate constituent components, including mobile devices, printers, and sensors.
assessment_objectives: Determine if internal connections of system components/classes are authorized.
Determine if interface characteristics, security requirements, and nature of information communicated are documented for each internal connection.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping; VA notes this covers all intra-system connections including mobile devices, printers, copiers, fax machines, scanners, sensors, and servers.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Even connections between components inside the same system (like a printer or sensor connecting to the network) need to be authorized and documented, not just external connections.

evidence_required.description: Internal connection inventory/authorization documentation.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Internal connection documentation overlaps with the system component inventory.

control_families.family_description: Governs baseline configurations, change control, least functionality, component inventory, and software usage restrictions.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate a configuration management policy and procedures; review/update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for the CM family.
assessment_objectives: Determine if configuration management policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written configuration management policy, reviewed periodically.

evidence_required.description: Configuration management policy document.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same policy documentation pattern.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and maintain under configuration control, a current baseline configuration of the system.
nist_800_53.discussion: The baseline configuration provides information about system components (standard software loads, network topology, logical placement within the architecture) and serves as a basis for future builds/releases/changes.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a current baseline configuration is developed, documented, and maintained under configuration control.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Review and update the baseline configuration periodically, when required due to system changes, and as an integral part of installations/upgrades.

va_odp_values.value: Annually, and whenever a significant change affecting security occurs

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The baseline configuration document isn't a one-time snapshot — it's revisited at least annually and whenever a major change happens, so it always reflects what the system's approved settings should currently be.

evidence_required.description: Annual baseline configuration review/update record.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Automation Support for Accuracy and Currency

nist_800_53.control_statement: Maintain the currency, completeness, accuracy, and availability of the baseline configuration using automated mechanisms.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, tools automatically track and verify that the actual system configuration matches the documented baseline, rather than relying on manual spot-checks.

evidence_required.description: Automated configuration management tool output confirming baseline accuracy.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Retain a defined number of previous baseline configuration versions to support rollback.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Older versions of the baseline configuration are kept on file so that if a new change causes problems, the system can be rolled back to a known-good prior configuration.

evidence_required.description: Archive of previous baseline configuration versions.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Configure Systems and Components for High-Risk Areas

nist_800_53.control_statement: Issue systems/components with defined configurations to individuals traveling to high-risk locations, and apply security safeguards upon return.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: A mobile device with a sanitized hard drive and limited applications may be issued; upon return, the device is examined for tampering and the hard drive purged/reimaged.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Employees traveling to high-risk countries get a specially prepared, stripped-down device (rather than their normal laptop) for the trip, and that device is inspected and wiped/reimaged when they return, in case it was compromised while abroad.

evidence_required.description: High-risk travel device issuance and post-travel inspection/reimaging procedure.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: OI&T develops, implements, and approves system security baseline configurations for all VA platforms, leveraging FDCC/USGCB/DISA STIG standards. Systems unable to meet the approved baseline require an OIS Risk-Based Decision (RBD). VA compliance with baseline settings is scanned regularly using a NIST-validated Security Content Automation Protocol tool.
va_specific_requirements: Baselines must adhere to FDCC/USGCB/DISA STIG standards.
An OIS RBD is required for systems that cannot meet the approved baseline.
Regular automated compliance scanning against baseline configuration.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Every system needs a documented 'gold standard' configuration (approved settings, installed software, patch levels) that changes are measured against. VA requires this to follow federal hardening standards (like DISA STIGs) and checks compliance with automated scanning tools.

evidence_required.description: Documented baseline configuration (standard build, hardening guide reference).
Automated compliance scan results (e.g., SCAP) against the baseline.
OIS RBD documentation for any systems deviating from the approved baseline.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Configuration settings (CM-6) are the granular parameters that make up the baseline configuration.
The component inventory documents what's covered by the baseline.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Determine the types of changes to the system that are configuration-controlled; review and approve/disapprove proposed changes with explicit consideration of security impact; document change decisions; implement approved changes; retain records of changes; audit change activities; and coordinate oversight through a change control element.
nist_800_53.discussion: Involves systematic proposal, justification, implementation, testing, review, and disposition of changes.
assessment_objectives: Determine if types of configuration-controlled changes are determined.
Determine if proposed changes are reviewed and approved/disapproved with security impact consideration.
Determine if change decisions are documented and approved changes implemented.
Determine if records of changes are retained and change activities audited.
Determine if oversight is coordinated through a change control element (e.g., CCB) on an assigned schedule.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Automated Documentation, Notification, and Prohibition of Changes

nist_800_53.control_statement: Use automated mechanisms to document proposed changes, notify approval authorities, highlight unapproved changes, prohibit changes until approved, document all changes, and notify officials when changes are completed.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, the change management workflow is automated end-to-end: proposed changes are logged automatically, approvers are notified automatically, and the system won't let a change through without documented approval.

evidence_required.description: Automated change management tool workflow logs (proposal, approval, notification).

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Testing, Validation, and Documentation of Changes

nist_800_53.control_statement: Test, validate, and document changes before implementing them on the operational system.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Changes are tested and validated in a non-production environment first, with the results documented, before they're ever applied to the live system.

evidence_required.description: Pre-implementation testing/validation records for system changes.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require an information security representative and privacy representative to be a member of the configuration change control element.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not separately allocated in VA 6500; VA's CCB structure typically includes ISO/security participation informally rather than as a mandated enhancement.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Not separately mandated by VA as a distinct enhancement — though VA's Change Control Boards typically already involve security personnel informally as part of their standard membership.

va_odp_values.value: Per NARA 806-3 (PC Baseline Management): destroy/delete records 5 years after a baseline is superseded

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: All IT systems/components are covered by a chartered local or national Change Control Board (CCB). No system may be modified without CCB approval; unauthorized changes trigger an immediate rollback process. Emergency changes must be documented and approved either before or immediately after the fact.
va_specific_requirements: A CCB must exist and approve all changes; unauthorized changes require immediate rollback.
Emergency changes documented and approved before or immediately after implementation.
Testing conducted in a manner that does not interfere with operations; may require offline/replicated testing.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Changes to a system (patches, upgrades, configuration tweaks) can't just happen ad hoc — they go through a formal review and approval process (a Change Control Board), get tested first, and are documented. If an unapproved change slips through, it must be rolled back immediately.

evidence_required.description: Configuration/change management policy establishing the CCB process.
CCB meeting minutes/change request tickets showing review and approval.
Test/validation results for changes prior to production deployment.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Security impact analysis is a required part of the change approval decision.
Patch deployment (flaw remediation) flows through the same change control process.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Analyze changes to the system to determine potential security and privacy impacts prior to change implementation.
nist_800_53.discussion: Conducted by personnel with appropriate skills and technical expertise; may include reviewing security plans and assessing risk.
assessment_objectives: Determine if changes to the system are analyzed for potential security/privacy impacts prior to implementation.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Analyze changes to the system in a separate test environment before implementation in an operational environment, looking for security impacts due to flaws, weaknesses, incompatibility, or intentional malice.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, the security impact analysis of a proposed change happens in a dedicated test environment completely separate from production, specifically to check for flaws, weaknesses, or malicious intent before the change ever touches the live system.

evidence_required.description: Security impact analysis performed in a separate test environment.

nist_800_53.control_statement: After system changes, verify that the impacted controls are implemented correctly, operating as intended, and producing the desired outcome.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not separately allocated in VA 6500; conceptually addressed by post-change control assessment activities under CA-2.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Not separately mandated by VA as a distinct enhancement — though VA's broader control assessment process (CA-2) can serve a similar verification purpose after significant changes.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Before making a change, someone qualified analyzes what security impact that change could have — for the riskiest systems, this analysis happens in a separate test environment rather than directly on production.

evidence_required.description: Security impact analysis records for changes.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Impact analysis is an input to the change approval decision.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Define, document, approve, and enforce physical and logical access restrictions associated with changes to the system.
nist_800_53.discussion: Only qualified and authorized individuals should be allowed to obtain access to system components to initiate changes.
assessment_objectives: Determine if physical and logical access restrictions associated with changes are defined, documented, approved, and enforced.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Enforce access restrictions and support auditing of enforcement actions using automated mechanisms.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The technical restrictions on who can make configuration changes are enforced automatically by the system itself, and every time that enforcement kicks in (blocking or allowing a change attempt), it's logged.

evidence_required.description: Automated access enforcement audit logs for configuration change actions.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Review system changes to determine whether unauthorized changes have occurred.

va_odp_values.value: Monthly audits of changes

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Every month, someone reviews the changes that were actually made to the system to confirm they all went through the proper approval process — catching any changes that slipped through without authorization.

evidence_required.description: Monthly change review/audit records confirming no unauthorized changes occurred.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Prevent installation of software/firmware without verification the component has been digitally signed using an approved certificate.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The system technically refuses to install software or firmware updates unless they carry a valid digital signature from an approved source — this prevents tampered or counterfeit software from being installed even if someone tries.

evidence_required.description: Configuration enforcing digital signature verification prior to software/firmware installation.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Only specifically authorized people can access the mechanisms used to make changes to a system — and for high-risk systems, changes are actively reviewed afterward to catch anything unauthorized, and software installations require verified digital signatures.

evidence_required.description: Access control configuration restricting who can make configuration changes.
Monthly change review/audit records.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Restricting change access is an application of least privilege.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish and document configuration settings using security configuration checklists reflecting the most restrictive mode consistent with operational requirements; implement the settings; identify/document/approve deviations; and monitor/control changes.
nist_800_53.discussion: Configuration settings are parameters that can be changed in hardware, software, or firmware affecting security posture. Security-related parameters include registry settings, account/file/directory permissions, and port/protocol/service settings.
assessment_objectives: Determine if configuration settings are established and documented using security configuration checklists.
Determine if configuration settings are implemented.
Determine if deviations from established settings are identified, documented, and approved based on operational requirements.
Determine if changes to configuration settings are monitored and controlled.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Use automated mechanisms to centrally manage, apply, and verify configuration settings.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, configuration settings (like password policy or registry values) are pushed out, managed, and verified automatically from a central tool rather than being manually configured on each machine.

evidence_required.description: Centralized configuration management tool output (e.g., Group Policy/SCCM reports).

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ security safeguards to respond to unauthorized changes to defined configuration settings.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: If someone changes a configuration setting without authorization (e.g., disabling a firewall rule), the system automatically takes a defined action in response — such as reverting the setting or alerting security staff.

evidence_required.description: Configuration drift detection/auto-remediation tool settings.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Configuration settings use Service Delivery and Engineering-approved configuration checklists; deviations require Service Delivery and Engineering/OIS review.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Specific technical settings (password policy settings, registry values, open ports, etc.) must be locked down to the most secure setting that still lets the system function — and any exceptions to those settings must be documented and approved, not silently allowed.

evidence_required.description: Configuration settings checklist (e.g., STIG-based) applied to the system.
Documented and approved deviations from standard configuration settings.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Configuration settings are the granular detail underlying the baseline configuration.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Configure the system to provide only essential capabilities, and prohibit or restrict use of defined functions, ports, protocols, software, and/or services.
nist_800_53.discussion: Organizations review functions/services periodically to determine which are candidates for elimination (e.g., unnecessary ports, protocols like FTP or Telnet).
assessment_objectives: Determine if the system is configured to provide only essential capabilities.
Determine if use of defined non-essential functions, ports, protocols, or services is prohibited/restricted.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Review the system periodically to identify unnecessary/non-secure functions, ports, protocols, and services, and disable those deemed unnecessary.

va_odp_values.value: At minimum, annually

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: At least once a year, the system is reviewed to check for open ports, unused services, or outdated protocols that aren't actually needed — anything found unnecessary gets turned off.

evidence_required.description: Annual review record of open ports/services/protocols with disabled-unnecessary-items log.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Prevent program execution per defined policies on software program usage and restrictions.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The system technically blocks programs from running if they violate the organization's software usage policy — this isn't just a written rule, it's enforced by the software.

evidence_required.description: Application control/execution prevention tool configuration.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify software not authorized to execute; employ a deny-all, permit-by-exception policy.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Any software not approved through the TRM (Technical Reference Model) process is considered unauthorized.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: VA 6500 applies this at Moderate under Rev 4 numbering; Rev 5 restructured CM-7(4)/(5) blacklisting/whitelisting enhancements. Best-effort mapping preserved.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Software not on VA's approved technology list (TRM) is automatically treated as unauthorized and blocked — the default assumption is 'not allowed' unless it's specifically been vetted and approved.

evidence_required.description: Application blacklisting tool configuration and logs.
TRM approved technology list against which software is checked.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify software authorized to execute; employ a deny-all, permit-by-exception policy allowing only authorized software.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: OI&T's TRM Management Team continuously reviews and updates approved/disapproved technologies; existing entries reviewed annually.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, only software explicitly on the approved list can run at all — everything else is blocked by default, which is a stricter approach than just blacklisting known-bad software.

evidence_required.description: Application whitelisting tool configuration and logs.
Current TRM approved technology whitelist.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Restricts use of ports/services to only what is essential based on business need and risk; open ports/services must be justified in the SSP; all others closed.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping for base control; enhancement (4)/(5) allocation differs slightly by baseline as noted.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Systems should only run the services, ports, and software they actually need — everything else gets turned off or blocked. VA maintains an approved technology list (TRM); anything not on it is considered unauthorized software.

evidence_required.description: List of open ports/services/software with business justification, documented in the SSP.
Application whitelisting/blacklisting tool configuration and logs.
TRM (Technical Reference Model) approved/disapproved technology list.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: User-installed software restrictions work together with least functionality's software execution controls.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop and document an inventory of system components that accurately reflects the system, includes all components within the authorization boundary, is at the appropriate level of granularity, and includes information necessary for accountability; review and update the inventory on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Component accountability information may include hardware inventory specifications, software license information, and system/component owner.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a system component inventory is developed, documented, and maintained.
Determine if the inventory is reviewed and updated at a defined frequency.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Update the inventory as an integral part of component installations, removals, and system updates.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The component inventory is updated as a routine step whenever something is installed, removed, or upgraded — not as a separate, easily-forgotten task done later.

evidence_required.description: Installation/removal procedure showing inventory update as a required step.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Use automated mechanisms to maintain an up-to-date, complete, accurate, and available inventory.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, the component inventory is maintained by automated discovery tools rather than manual spreadsheet updates, keeping it continuously accurate.

evidence_required.description: Automated asset discovery/inventory tool output.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Use automated mechanisms to detect unauthorized hardware/software/firmware, and disable network access, isolate, or notify defined personnel when detected.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Tools automatically scan for rogue or unauthorized devices/software connecting to the network, and when one is found, the system can automatically cut off its network access, isolate it, or alert security staff.

evidence_required.description: Unauthorized component detection alerts/logs and resulting containment actions.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Include a means for identifying individuals responsible/accountable for administering inventoried components.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The component inventory records not just what equipment exists, but who is specifically responsible for administering each item — so there's a clear point of contact for every asset.

evidence_required.description: Component inventory records showing assigned administrator/owner per component.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Verify all components within the authorization boundary are not duplicated in other component inventories.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: A component belonging to this system's inventory isn't also double-counted in some other system's inventory — each piece of equipment is accounted for exactly once, avoiding confusion about ownership.

evidence_required.description: Cross-inventory reconciliation record confirming no duplicate component listings.

va_odp_values.value: Annually

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization keeps a complete, accurate list of all hardware/software components in a system, updated whenever something is added or removed, and reviewed at least annually. For higher-risk systems, tools automatically detect unauthorized/rogue components that shouldn't be there.

evidence_required.description: Current system component inventory export.
Annual inventory review/reconciliation record.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Inventory documents the components covered by the baseline configuration.
System-level inventory feeds the organization-wide information system inventory.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and implement a configuration management plan that addresses roles/responsibilities/processes, establishes a process for identifying and managing configuration items, defines configuration items, and protects the plan from unauthorized disclosure/modification.
nist_800_53.discussion: Configuration items include hardware, software, firmware, and documentation throughout the SDLC.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a configuration management plan addressing roles, processes, and configuration item identification/protection is developed, documented, and implemented.

controls.plain_english_explanation: There must be a documented plan describing how configuration management actually works for this system: who's responsible, what counts as a 'configuration item,' and how that plan itself is protected from tampering.

evidence_required.description: System-level configuration management plan.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: The CM plan documents the change control process referenced by CM-3.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Use software and associated documentation in accordance with contract agreements and copyright laws; track use of software protected by quantity licenses; control and document peer-to-peer file sharing to prevent unauthorized distribution of copyrighted work.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses software license tracking and prevents inadvertent copyright violation.
assessment_objectives: Determine if software is used per contract agreements and copyright laws.
Determine if licensed software use is tracked to control copying/distribution.
Determine if peer-to-peer file sharing is controlled/documented.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must use software only as its license permits, keep track of how many license seats are in use, and prevent things like unauthorized peer-to-peer file sharing that could violate copyright.

evidence_required.description: Software license inventory/tracking records.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Software license tracking overlaps with the component inventory.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish policies governing the installation of software by users; enforce software installation policies through defined methods; monitor policy compliance.
nist_800_53.discussion: Permitted installations may include updates/patches to existing software; prohibited installations may include software with unknown/suspect origin.
assessment_objectives: Determine if policies governing user software installation are established.
Determine if software installation policies are enforced through defined methods.
Determine if policy compliance is monitored.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Enforced via approved policies/guidance (ROB, TRM, Enterprise System Build Guides), limiting user ability to install software and monitored through application whitelisting and compliance monitoring tools, as part of VA's continuous monitoring processes.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Regular users generally can't install arbitrary software themselves — only approved software (per the TRM/build guides) can be installed, and compliance with this rule is actively monitored.

evidence_required.description: User-installed software policy/ROB provisions.
Application whitelisting tool logs showing enforcement.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Software execution restrictions overlap with least functionality controls.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify and document the location of information and the specific system components on which the information is processed and stored; identify and document users who have access to the system and system components where the information is processed and stored.
nist_800_53.discussion: Helps organizations understand and mitigate risk related to data storage location, especially for cloud/distributed environments.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time (newer Rev 5 addition, postdates VA 6500's Rev 4-based Appendix F).
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in VA 6500; introduced in Rev 5 after VA 6500 was authored.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this newer control would require documenting exactly where data is stored/processed and who has access to those specific locations.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop and document a data action mapping for systems, applications, or environments of operation to identify and understand data actions.
nist_800_53.discussion: A newer Rev 5 control supporting privacy risk analysis by mapping how data is processed throughout its lifecycle.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time (newer Rev 5 addition, postdates VA 6500's Rev 4-based Appendix F).
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in VA 6500; introduced in Rev 5 after VA 6500 was authored.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this newer control would require mapping out how personal data flows and is processed throughout a system.

control_families.family_description: Governs planning, training, testing, backup, and alternate-site strategies to maintain and restore essential missions/business functions after a disruption, compromise, or failure.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate a contingency planning policy and procedures; review/update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for contingency planning.
assessment_objectives: Determine if contingency planning policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written contingency planning policy, reviewed periodically.

evidence_required.description: Contingency planning policy document.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same policy documentation pattern.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop a contingency plan identifying essential missions/business functions, recovery objectives, roles/responsibilities, and procedures for maintaining functions during disruption and restoring the system afterward; distribute copies; coordinate with incident handling activities; review and update the plan.
nist_800_53.discussion: Contingency planning addresses both system restoration and implementation of alternative business processes when systems are compromised.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a contingency plan identifying essential missions/business functions and recovery requirements is developed.
Determine if the plan is reviewed, approved, and distributed to defined personnel.
Determine if contingency planning is coordinated with incident handling.
Determine if the plan is reviewed and updated to address changes/problems encountered.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Coordinate contingency plan development with organizational elements responsible for related plans.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The contingency plan isn't developed in a vacuum — it's coordinated with the teams responsible for related plans (like incident response or emergency management) so all the plans work together consistently.

evidence_required.description: Coordination records with related plan owners (IR, COOP, emergency management).

nist_800_53.control_statement: Conduct capacity planning so necessary capacity exists during contingency operations.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The organization plans ahead to make sure there's actually enough processing power, storage, and bandwidth available to run essential operations during a disruption, not just a theoretical plan that would fail under real load.

evidence_required.description: Capacity planning analysis for contingency/disaster recovery operations.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Resume Essential Missions and Business Functions

nist_800_53.control_statement: Plan for resumption of essential missions/business functions within a defined time period of contingency plan activation.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The plan specifies a target timeframe (e.g., within 4 hours, within 24 hours) for getting the most critical functions back up and running after the contingency plan is activated.

evidence_required.description: Contingency plan section specifying recovery time objectives for essential functions.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Resume All Missions and Business Functions

nist_800_53.control_statement: Plan for resumption of all missions/business functions within a defined time period of contingency plan activation.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Beyond just the most critical functions, the plan also specifies a timeframe for restoring every function of the system (even lower-priority ones) back to normal operation.

evidence_required.description: Contingency plan section specifying recovery time objectives for all business functions.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Continue Essential Missions and Business Functions

nist_800_53.control_statement: Plan for continuance of essential missions and business functions with little or no loss of operational continuity.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, the plan doesn't just aim to restore functions quickly after an outage — it aims to keep the most essential functions running continuously through the disruption, with little to no visible interruption at all.

evidence_required.description: Contingency plan demonstrating continuity-of-operations design for essential functions.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify critical system assets supporting essential missions and business functions.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The contingency plan explicitly identifies which specific hardware, software, and infrastructure assets are critical to keeping essential functions running, so those assets get priority attention during recovery.

evidence_required.description: List of critical system assets documented in the contingency plan.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Information System Owners coordinate with business/service lines to identify essential missions and functions. Additional detail is provided in VA Handbook 6500.8, Information System Contingency Planning.
va_specific_requirements: Contingency plan reviewed annually and after significant changes.

controls.plain_english_explanation: There must be a written plan for what to do if the system is disrupted, compromised, or fails — identifying which functions are essential, how quickly they need to come back online, and who's responsible for what during recovery.

evidence_required.description: System contingency plan.
Annual contingency plan review/update record.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: The contingency plan is what's actually tested under CP-4.
Contingency planning is coordinated with incident response planning.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide contingency training to system users consistent with assigned roles/responsibilities within a defined time period of assuming a contingency role, when required by system changes, and thereafter at a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Training content and detail should be linked to assigned contingency roles (e.g., regular users vs. system administrators vs. senior leaders).
assessment_objectives: Determine if contingency training is provided within a defined time period of assuming a role.
Determine if training is provided when required by changes and at a defined frequency thereafter.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Incorporate simulated events into contingency training.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Contingency training includes realistic simulated scenarios (like a mock system outage), not just reading through a written plan, so personnel actually practice responding under conditions similar to a real event.

evidence_required.description: Contingency training materials/records showing simulated event exercises.

va_odp_values.value: Within 30 days of assuming the role
Annually thereafter

controls.plain_english_explanation: People with a role in the contingency plan must be trained on that role within 30 days of taking it on, and refreshed annually.

evidence_required.description: Contingency role training completion records.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Training content is based on the roles defined in the contingency plan.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Test the contingency plan using defined tests to determine plan effectiveness and organizational readiness; review test results; initiate corrective actions.
nist_800_53.discussion: Testing methods include walk-through/tabletop exercises, checklists, parallel/full interrupt simulations, and comprehensive exercises.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the contingency plan is tested using defined tests to determine effectiveness and readiness.
Determine if test results are reviewed and corrective actions initiated.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Coordinate contingency plan testing with organizational elements responsible for related plans.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: When the contingency plan is tested, that testing is coordinated with teams responsible for related plans (like incident response), so the exercise reflects how all the plans would actually work together in a real event.

evidence_required.description: Contingency plan test records showing coordination with related plan owners.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Test the contingency plan at the alternate processing site to familiarize personnel and evaluate site capabilities.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The contingency plan is actually tested at the backup/alternate processing site itself (not just discussed on paper), so personnel become familiar with that location and any gaps in its readiness are identified before a real disaster.

evidence_required.description: Test results/exercise report conducted at the alternate processing site.

va_odp_values.value: Annually
e.g., availability/validity of backup files, fire/evacuation procedure implementation, manual procedure implementation

controls.plain_english_explanation: The contingency plan isn't just written and shelved — it's actually tested at least annually (through exercises, walkthroughs, or simulations), and any problems found are fixed.

evidence_required.description: Annual contingency plan test/exercise results and after-action report.
Documentation of corrective actions taken based on test findings.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Tests validate the plan developed under CP-2.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Withdrawn; incorporated into CP-2.
nist_800_53.discussion: Requirements folded into CP-2 (Contingency Plan).

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Withdrawn control; not separately tracked by VA 6500.

controls.plain_english_explanation: This control no longer exists on its own — its requirements are now covered under the Contingency Plan control (CP-2).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Absorbed this withdrawn control's requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish an alternate storage site including necessary agreements to permit storage/retrieval of backup information, and ensure the site provides security safeguards equivalent to the primary site.
nist_800_53.discussion: An alternate storage site maintains duplicate copies of information/data in the event the primary site is unavailable.
assessment_objectives: Determine if an alternate storage site with necessary agreements is established.
Determine if the alternate site provides safeguards equivalent to the primary site.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify an alternate storage site separated from the primary site to reduce susceptibility to the same threats.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The backup storage site is far enough away from the primary site that a regional event (like a hurricane or power grid failure) affecting one wouldn't also take out the other.

evidence_required.description: Documentation showing geographic/threat separation between primary and alternate storage sites.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Configure the alternate storage site to facilitate recovery operations per recovery time/point objectives.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The alternate storage site is specifically set up (network connectivity, storage capacity, retrieval speed) to actually meet the recovery time and data-loss targets defined for the system, not just serve as a generic backup location.

evidence_required.description: Alternate storage site configuration demonstrating alignment with defined RTO/RPO.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify potential accessibility problems to the alternate storage site in the event of an area-wide disruption and outline mitigation actions.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The plan anticipates situations where even the backup site might be hard to reach (like a widespread regional disaster affecting travel/access) and has a documented fallback for that scenario.

evidence_required.description: Documented accessibility risk analysis and mitigation actions for the alternate storage site.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: The alternate storage facility must have controlled access and proper environmental controls; access is stringently controlled and periodically tested. System/application documentation and an up-to-date hardcopy of contingency plans are stored securely at the alternate location.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Backups need to be stored somewhere physically separate from the primary system, with equivalent security protections, so a disaster affecting the main site doesn't also destroy the backups.

evidence_required.description: Alternate storage site agreement/contract.
Description of alternate site security controls demonstrating equivalence to primary site.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Backups created under CP-9 are what gets stored at the alternate site.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish an alternate processing site including necessary agreements to permit transfer/resumption of essential functions when primary processing is unavailable; ensure equipment/supplies are available or can be delivered within a defined time period; ensure equivalent security safeguards.
nist_800_53.discussion: Alternate processing sites are geographically distinct from primary sites and provide processing capability when the primary site is unavailable.
assessment_objectives: Determine if an alternate processing site with necessary agreements is established.
Determine if equipment/supplies are available or can be delivered within a defined time period.
Determine if the alternate site provides equivalent safeguards.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify an alternate processing site separated from the primary site to reduce susceptibility to the same threats.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The backup processing site (where operations could actually run from, not just store data) is geographically distant enough from the primary site that a regional disaster wouldn't take out both.

evidence_required.description: Documentation showing geographic/threat separation between primary and alternate processing sites.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify potential accessibility problems to the alternate processing site and outline mitigation actions.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The plan considers what could prevent staff or systems from actually reaching/using the alternate processing site during a widespread disruption, with documented workarounds for that scenario.

evidence_required.description: Documented accessibility risk analysis and mitigation actions for the alternate processing site.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop alternate processing site agreements containing priority-of-service provisions aligned with availability requirements.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The contract with the alternate processing site guarantees VA gets priority access to that site's resources during an emergency, rather than competing with the provider's other customers who might also be affected by the same regional event.

evidence_required.description: Alternate processing site contract containing priority-of-service clauses.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Prepare the alternate processing site so it is ready to be used as the operational site.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The alternate site isn't just a bare facility on paper — it's pre-configured, stocked, and kept ready so it could actually be activated and used as the live operational site with minimal setup time.

evidence_required.description: Documentation confirming alternate site readiness/pre-configuration status.

controls.plain_english_explanation: If the main data center/processing site goes down, there needs to be a pre-arranged alternate location where operations can resume, with equipment and priority-of-service agreements already in place.

evidence_required.description: Alternate processing site agreement with priority-of-service provisions.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Alternate processing and storage sites are often planned together as part of the same disaster recovery strategy.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish alternate telecommunications services including necessary agreements to permit resumption of essential functions when primary telecommunications capabilities are unavailable.
nist_800_53.discussion: Applies to telecommunications services (data and voice) for primary and alternate processing/storage sites.
assessment_objectives: Determine if alternate telecommunications services with necessary agreements are established.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop primary/alternate telecommunications agreements with priority-of-service provisions; request Telecommunications Service Priority when provided by a common carrier.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Telecommunications contracts include priority-of-service terms, and where a commercial carrier provides the service, VA requests the federal Telecommunications Service Priority designation to jump the queue for restoration during a widespread outage.

evidence_required.description: Telecommunications service contract with priority-of-service provisions.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Obtain alternate telecommunications services to reduce the likelihood of sharing a single point of failure with primary services.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The backup telecommunications service doesn't rely on the exact same physical infrastructure (like the same cable route or central office) as the primary service, so a single cut cable or equipment failure can't take down both.

evidence_required.description: Telecommunications infrastructure analysis demonstrating no shared single point of failure.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Separation of Primary and Alternate Providers

nist_800_53.control_statement: Obtain alternate telecommunications services from providers separated from primary providers to reduce susceptibility to the same threats.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, the backup telecom provider is a genuinely different company from the primary provider, not just a different service plan from the same carrier — reducing the chance a single provider's outage affects both.

evidence_required.description: Contracts showing primary and alternate telecommunications services from separate providers.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require telecommunications providers to have contingency plans, review those plans, and obtain evidence of contingency testing/training.

va_odp_values.value: Annually or as stated in the contract

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: VA's telecom providers are required to have their own contingency plans, and VA reviews those plans and gets proof (annually or per the contract terms) that the providers actually test their own disaster preparedness.

evidence_required.description: Telecommunications provider contingency plan review records and testing evidence.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Backup telecommunications (phone/data lines) must be arranged in advance, ideally from a different provider or path than the primary connection, so a single outage doesn't take down both primary and backup communications.

evidence_required.description: Alternate telecommunications service agreement.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Telecommunications continuity supports the alternate processing site's operation.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Conduct backups of user-level information, system-level information, and system documentation (including security-related documentation) consistent with recovery time and recovery point objectives; protect the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of backup information.
nist_800_53.discussion: System-level information includes system state information, OS/application software, and licenses.
assessment_objectives: Determine if backups of user-level, system-level, and documentation information are conducted consistent with recovery objectives.
Determine if the confidentiality, integrity, and availability of backup information is protected.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Test backup information to verify media reliability and information integrity.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Backups aren't just created and forgotten — they're periodically tested to confirm the backup media actually works and the data hasn't been corrupted, so there are no surprises during an actual recovery.

evidence_required.description: Backup integrity/reliability test results.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Use a sample of backup information in restoration of selected system functions as part of contingency plan testing.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: As part of testing the overall contingency plan, a sample of backed-up data is actually restored to confirm the restoration process itself works end-to-end, not just that backups exist.

evidence_required.description: Sample restoration test results conducted as part of contingency plan testing.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Store backup copies of critical system software/security-related information in a separate facility or fire-rated container not co-located with the operational system.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Backups of the most critical software and security-related information are physically stored somewhere separate from the live system (a different facility or at least a fire-rated safe), so a local disaster like a fire doesn't destroy both the system and its backups.

evidence_required.description: Documentation of the separate/fire-rated storage location for critical backup copies.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Transfer system backup information to the alternate storage site at a frequency/rate consistent with recovery time/point objectives.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Backups are transferred to the offsite alternate storage location frequently enough to actually meet the system's recovery objectives — if the recovery point objective allows only an hour of data loss, backups need to move offsite roughly that often, not just once a week.

evidence_required.description: Backup transfer logs showing frequency consistent with defined RPO.

va_odp_values.value: Semi-annually (Low); monthly (Moderate/High), per Information System Owner/Information Owner determination
FIPS 140-2 (or successor) validated encryption

va_specific_requirements: Mobile/portable storage devices must not contain the only copy of VA information; backups must be created at regular intervals.
Backups labeled, packed, and transported securely to off-site storage.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Regular backups of both data and full system state must be taken and encrypted, with the frequency matching how much data loss the organization can tolerate — and backups must be periodically tested to make sure they actually work when needed.

evidence_required.description: Backup job logs/schedules and completion records.
Backup restoration/integrity test results.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Backups are stored at the alternate storage site.
Backup encryption must meet the same FIPS 140-2 cryptographic protection requirement.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide for the recovery and reconstitution of the system to a known state after a disruption, compromise, or failure.
nist_800_53.discussion: Recovery is executing contingency plan activities to restore essential functions; reconstitution follows and returns the system to full operational status.
assessment_objectives: Determine if recovery and reconstitution of the system to a known state after disruption/compromise/failure is provided.
