nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement transaction recovery for systems that are transaction-based.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For systems that process transactions (like financial or benefits processing), there's a specific mechanism to recover any transaction that was in progress when a disruption occurred, so partial or lost transactions can be identified and completed correctly.

evidence_required.description: Transaction logging/recovery mechanism configuration for transaction-based systems.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide the capability to restore system components from configuration-controlled and integrity-protected information representing a known, operational state for the components within a defined restoration time period.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, there's a demonstrated capability to actually restore components to a known-good, verified state within a specific, defined timeframe — not just an aspirational goal.

evidence_required.description: Restoration test demonstrating components restored to a known operational state within the defined time period.

controls.plain_english_explanation: After a disruption, the organization must be able to restore the system to a known-good state and eventually return it to full normal operation — not just get it partially running.

evidence_required.description: System recovery/reconstitution procedures.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Recovery relies directly on the backups created under CP-9.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide the capability to employ alternative communications protocols in support of maintaining continuity of operations.
nist_800_53.discussion: Useful when primary communications protocols become unavailable or unreliable during a disruption.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would provide a fallback communications protocol if the primary one fails during a disruption.

nist_800_53.control_statement: When certain conditions are detected, enter a safe mode of operation with defined restrictions of safe mode operation.
nist_800_53.discussion: Common in industrial control systems and specialized environments requiring a degraded-but-safe operational state.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would allow a system to enter a restricted, safer operating mode when certain risk conditions are detected.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ alternative or supplemental security mechanisms for satisfying security functions when the primary means of implementing the function is unavailable or compromised.
nist_800_53.discussion: Provides redundancy in security function implementation.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would provide backup security mechanisms if the primary security function becomes unavailable.

control_families.family_description: Governs how users, devices, and processes are uniquely identified and authenticated before being granted access to systems.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate an identification and authentication policy and procedures; review/update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for identification/authentication.
assessment_objectives: Determine if identification and authentication policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: User identification and authentication must be consistent with HSPD-12, OMB M-04-04, FIPS 140-2, FIPS 201, NIST SP 800-63/73/76/78, and current VA PIV procedures.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written identification and authentication policy, consistent with federal identity standards like PIV/HSPD-12, reviewed periodically.

evidence_required.description: Identification and authentication policy document.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same policy documentation pattern.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Uniquely identify and authenticate organizational users (or processes acting on behalf of users).
nist_800_53.discussion: Users are uniquely identified for all accesses other than those explicitly identified under AC-14. Multi-factor authentication requires two or more different factors: something you know, something you have, or something you are.
assessment_objectives: Determine if organizational users (or processes acting on their behalf) are uniquely identified and authenticated.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement multi-factor authentication for network access to privileged accounts.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Admin-level accounts logging in over the network must use two-factor authentication (like a password plus a PIV smart card) — a password alone isn't enough for privileged access.

evidence_required.description: Multi-factor authentication configuration for privileged account network access.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement multi-factor authentication for network access to non-privileged accounts.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Even regular (non-admin) user accounts must use two-factor authentication when logging in over the network — this isn't limited to privileged users.

evidence_required.description: Multi-factor authentication configuration for non-privileged account network access.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement multi-factor authentication for local access to privileged accounts.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Even when logging into an admin account directly at the machine (not over a network), two-factor authentication is still required — physical presence at the console doesn't lower the bar.

evidence_required.description: Multi-factor authentication configuration for local/console privileged account access.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement multi-factor authentication for local access to non-privileged accounts.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, even regular users logging in directly at the machine (not remotely) must use two-factor authentication.

evidence_required.description: Multi-factor authentication configuration for local/console non-privileged account access.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for network access to privileged accounts.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The authentication method used for privileged network access is designed so that even if an attacker captured the authentication exchange, they couldn't reuse it later to log in themselves (protecting against 'replay attacks').

evidence_required.description: Authentication protocol configuration demonstrating replay resistance (e.g., time-based tokens, challenge-response).

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Network Access to Non-Privileged Accounts — Replay Resistant

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement replay-resistant authentication mechanisms for network access to non-privileged accounts.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, this same replay-attack protection also extends to regular (non-privileged) user accounts logging in over the network, not just admin accounts.

evidence_required.description: Authentication protocol configuration demonstrating replay resistance for non-privileged accounts.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement multi-factor authentication for remote access such that one factor is provided by a device separate from the system gaining access, meeting defined strength-of-mechanism requirements.

va_odp_values.value: FIPS 201-1 requirements apply; non-privileged users use PIV; privileged accounts require certificate-based authentication or one-time-passcode token authentication

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For remote access, one of the two authentication factors must come from a physically separate device from the computer being used to log in — for example, a PIV card or a one-time-passcode token, not just something typed on the same laptop.

evidence_required.description: Remote access authentication configuration showing use of a separate physical device (PIV card, token).

nist_800_53.control_statement: Accept and electronically verify Personal Identity Verification (PIV) credentials.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The system accepts and can electronically verify federal PIV smart cards as a valid form of credential — not just usernames/passwords.

evidence_required.description: PIV card reader/verification integration configuration.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Identification/authentication requirements are satisfied by complying with HSPD-12 per VA's implementation plan. Remote access users who cannot use multi-factor authentication must request an OIS Risk-Based Decision (RBD).
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping across base control and enhancements.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Every individual user must have their own unique login — no shared accounts — and for most access types (especially remote and privileged access), a second authentication factor (like a PIV smart card) is required in addition to a password.

evidence_required.description: Multi-factor authentication configuration (PIV/CAC integration, token-based auth).
OIS RBD for any exception to multi-factor remote access.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Remote access requires the multi-factor authentication defined here.
IA-2 covers organizational users; IA-8 covers the parallel requirement for non-organizational users.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Uniquely identify and authenticate defined devices before establishing a connection.
nist_800_53.discussion: Devices requiring unique identification/authentication may be defined by specific device or type. Systems typically use shared known information (MAC/IP addresses) or an approved authentication solution.
assessment_objectives: Determine if defined devices are uniquely identified and authenticated before establishing a connection.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: All internal servers use FIPS 140-2 (or successor) validated server certificates for inter-server and server-to-user communications.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Devices connecting to the network (not just people) must also be identified and authenticated before being allowed to connect.

evidence_required.description: Device authentication/certificate configuration.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Parallel to user identification/authentication, but for devices.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Manage system identifiers by receiving authorization to assign an identifier, selecting/assigning the identifier, preventing reuse of identifiers for a defined period, and disabling the identifier after a defined period of inactivity.
nist_800_53.discussion: Common device identifiers include MAC/IP addresses. When the identifier is associated with an individual, identifier management is largely addressed by AC-2 account management activities.
assessment_objectives: Determine if authorization is received from designated personnel prior to assigning an identifier.
Determine if identifiers are selected and assigned to the intended individual/group/role/device.
Determine if reuse of identifiers is prevented for a defined time period.
Determine if identifiers are disabled after a defined period of inactivity.

va_odp_values.value: At least 2 years
90 days

controls.plain_english_explanation: Once assigned, a user ID (or device ID) shouldn't be reassigned to someone else for at least 2 years, and it gets disabled automatically after 90 days of no use.

evidence_required.description: Identifier assignment/reuse records.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Identifier management is closely tied to account creation/disablement under AC-2.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Manage system authenticators by verifying identity at initial distribution, establishing initial content, ensuring sufficient strength, establishing distribution/revocation procedures, changing default authenticator content prior to installation, establishing lifetime/reuse restrictions, refreshing authenticators, protecting authenticator content, and changing group/role authenticators when membership changes.
nist_800_53.discussion: Individual authenticators include passwords, tokens, biometrics, and PKI certificates.
assessment_objectives: Determine if authenticators are managed per the full lifecycle requirements defined in the control.

nist_800_53.control_statement: For password-based authentication, enforce minimum complexity, minimum changed characters, cryptographically-protected storage/transmission, lifetime restrictions, reuse prohibition, and temporary password immediate-change requirement.

va_odp_values.value: At least 8 non-blank characters (12 for admin/service accounts); 3 of 4 character categories (uppercase, lowercase, digit, special character); 6 characters must not repeat
At least 4 characters changed from old to new password
User accounts changed every 90 days; admin accounts changed every 30-90 days; service accounts changed at minimum every 3 years
Not reused if used within past 2 years, or within last 3 password changes, whichever is greater restriction

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping; VA specifies exact numeric password requirements.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: This is VA's specific, numeric password policy: at least 8 characters (12 for admin/service accounts), mixing character types, changed every 90 days for regular users, and old passwords can't be reused for at least 2 years.

evidence_required.description: Password policy configuration (complexity, expiration, reuse rules) in Active Directory/identity system.

nist_800_53.control_statement: For PKI-based authentication, validate certificates by constructing/verifying a certification path, enforce authorized access to the private key, map the authenticated identity, and implement a local cache of revocation data.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: When authentication uses digital certificates (PKI), the system properly validates the certificate chain, ensures only the authorized person can use the associated private key, and checks whether the certificate has been revoked — even without live internet access to the revocation service.

evidence_required.description: PKI authentication configuration showing certificate path validation and revocation checking.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: In-Person or Trusted External Party Registration

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require in-person or trusted third-party registration for defined types of authenticators before a registration authority.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For certain types of high-assurance credentials (like a PIV card), the person must register in person or through a trusted verification process, rather than self-registering remotely — this confirms they really are who they claim to be.

evidence_required.description: In-person/trusted-party registration procedure for issuing high-assurance authenticators.

nist_800_53.control_statement: For hardware token-based authentication, employ mechanisms satisfying defined token quality requirements.

va_odp_values.value: PIV card using VA's approved PKI technology

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: When a physical hardware token is used for authentication, it must meet specific quality standards — at VA, this means the PIV smart card using VA's approved PKI infrastructure, not just any generic security key.

evidence_required.description: PIV card technology specification/configuration meeting VA's approved PKI standards.

va_specific_requirements: Passwords must not be shared except in documented emergency circumstances.
Passwords must not be displayed/printed as entered, and browsers must not be configured to save them for reuse.
Passwords for servers/network devices/security tools must be encrypted when stored.
Passwords transmitted across a WAN/Internet must be encrypted (except single-use one-time passwords).

controls.plain_english_explanation: This is VA's actual password policy: minimum length and complexity, mandatory expiration timelines, reuse restrictions, and rules against sharing, displaying, or insecurely storing passwords. It also governs PIV card and PKI certificate management.

evidence_required.description: Password policy configuration (Group Policy/AD settings) showing complexity/expiration/reuse enforcement.
Authenticator management policy covering distribution and protection requirements.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Authenticators managed here are what's used to satisfy IA-2's authentication requirement.
Password/authenticator failure thresholds are enforced alongside account lockout settings.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Obscure feedback of authentication information during the authentication process to protect it from possible exploitation by unauthorized individuals.
nist_800_53.discussion: Displaying asterisks when a user types a password is a common example of obscuring feedback.
assessment_objectives: Determine if feedback of authentication information is obscured during the authentication process.

controls.plain_english_explanation: When typing a password, the system shows asterisks or dots instead of the actual characters, so someone looking over your shoulder can't read it.

evidence_required.description: Login screen showing obscured password entry.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement mechanisms for authentication to a cryptographic module that meet applicable federal requirements for such authentication.
nist_800_53.discussion: Authentication mechanisms may be required within a cryptographic module to authenticate an operator and verify authorization to assume a requested role.
assessment_objectives: Determine if mechanisms for authentication to a cryptographic module meet applicable federal requirements.

controls.plain_english_explanation: When cryptographic modules (encryption hardware/software) require an operator to authenticate to use them, that authentication must meet federal standards.

evidence_required.description: Cryptographic module authentication configuration.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Governs the cryptographic protection the module itself provides.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Uniquely identify and authenticate non-organizational users (or processes acting on their behalf).
nist_800_53.discussion: Non-organizational users include all system users other than organizational users explicitly covered by IA-2.
assessment_objectives: Determine if non-organizational users are uniquely identified and authenticated.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Acceptance of PIV Credentials from Other Agencies

nist_800_53.control_statement: Accept and electronically verify PIV credentials from other federal agencies.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: If an employee from a different federal agency (with their own agency-issued PIV card) needs access, VA's systems can accept and verify that PIV credential rather than requiring a separate VA-issued credential.

evidence_required.description: Configuration demonstrating acceptance/verification of external agency PIV credentials.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Accept only FICAM-approved third-party credentials.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For non-federal users (like veterans logging into a public portal), only credential providers that have gone through the federal FICAM approval process are accepted — random third-party login providers can't be used.

evidence_required.description: Public-facing authentication configuration limited to FICAM-approved third-party credential providers.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ only FICAM-approved system components to accept third-party credentials.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Rev 5 withdrew/consolidated some FICAM-related sub-enhancements relative to Rev 4; VA's allocation is preserved here as a best-effort mapping.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The actual software/hardware components used to process third-party logins must themselves be on the approved FICAM products list, not just accept FICAM-approved credentials using unapproved technology.

evidence_required.description: Identity verification system component list confirming FICAM-approved products are in use.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Conform to FICAM-issued profiles.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The technical implementation of external authentication follows the specific federal-approved protocol profiles (like SAML 2.0 or OpenID as defined by FICAM), ensuring interoperability and a consistent security baseline across government systems.

evidence_required.description: Authentication protocol implementation demonstrating conformance to FICAM-issued profiles.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Non-VA users (e.g., veterans accessing a public portal, other federal agency staff) must also be uniquely identified and authenticated, typically via PIV or an approved external credential provider — not anonymous access.

evidence_required.description: External/public-facing authentication configuration.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: IA-8 is the non-organizational-user parallel to IA-2's organizational-user requirement.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify and authenticate system services and applications using defined security safeguards.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses authentication of automated services (not just human users or devices), such as APIs or system-to-system service calls.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time; OI&T may elect to implement service identification/authentication at their discretion.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would require identifying and authenticating automated services/APIs, not just human users.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require that individuals accessing the system employ supplemental authentication techniques or mechanisms under specific defined circumstances or situations.
nist_800_53.discussion: Enables risk-based/context-aware authentication (e.g., requiring extra verification for unusual login locations).

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would require extra authentication steps in specific risky situations (e.g., login attempts from unusual locations).

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require users and devices to re-authenticate when defined circumstances or situations require re-authentication.
nist_800_53.discussion: Common triggers include role changes, privilege escalation, or extended periods of inactivity.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would force users/devices to log in again under specific circumstances like privilege escalation.

control_families.family_description: Governs preparation, detection, analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery from security and privacy incidents, plus related training, testing, and reporting.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate an incident response policy and procedures; review/update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for incident response.
assessment_objectives: Determine if incident response policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Additional detail in VA Handbook 6500.2.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written incident response policy, reviewed periodically.

evidence_required.description: Incident response policy document.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same policy documentation pattern.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide incident response training to system users consistent with assigned roles/responsibilities within a defined time period of assuming a role, when required by system changes, and thereafter at a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Training content is linked to assigned roles; regular users need to know how to recognize/report an incident, while responders need forensics/reporting/recovery training.
assessment_objectives: Determine if incident response training is provided within a defined time period of assuming a role, when required by changes, and at a defined frequency thereafter.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Incorporate simulated events into incident response training.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Incident response training includes realistic simulated attack scenarios (like a mock ransomware event) rather than just reviewing a written procedure, so responders get hands-on practice under conditions similar to a real incident.

evidence_required.description: Incident response training materials/records showing simulated event exercises.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automated mechanisms to provide a more thorough and realistic training environment.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, incident response training uses automated tools/platforms (like a cyber range) to create a more realistic, hands-on training environment rather than relying solely on tabletop discussions.

evidence_required.description: Description of automated training environment/platform used for incident response training.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping; role-based incident response training incorporated with IT competency modeling (see AT-3).

controls.plain_english_explanation: Anyone with a role in incident response (from general users reporting suspicious activity to dedicated responders doing forensics) receives training appropriate to that role, before taking it on and periodically thereafter.

evidence_required.description: Incident response training completion records.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Incident response training is incorporated into VA's broader role-based training/competency model.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Test the incident response capability using defined tests to determine effectiveness and document results.
nist_800_53.discussion: Testing methods include checklists, walkthroughs/tabletop exercises, simulations, and comprehensive exercises.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the incident response capability is tested using defined tests to determine effectiveness, and results documented.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Coordinate incident response testing with organizational elements responsible for related plans.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: When testing the incident response plan, that testing is coordinated with teams responsible for related plans (like contingency planning), ensuring the exercise reflects how everything works together in practice.

evidence_required.description: Incident response test records showing coordination with related plan owners (e.g., contingency planning).

va_odp_values.value: Annually

va_specific_requirements: All tests documented in the SSP.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The incident response plan is tested at least annually to confirm it actually works, not just assumed to work because it's written down.

evidence_required.description: Annual incident response test/exercise results.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Incident response testing is often coordinated with contingency plan testing.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement an incident handling capability covering preparation, detection/analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery; coordinate with contingency planning; incorporate lessons learned into procedures/training/testing.
nist_800_53.discussion: Incident-related information can be obtained from audit monitoring, network monitoring, physical access monitoring, and user reports.
assessment_objectives: Determine if an incident handling capability covering preparation, detection/analysis, containment, eradication, and recovery is implemented.
Determine if incident handling is coordinated with contingency planning.
Determine if lessons learned are incorporated into procedures, training, and testing.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automated mechanisms to support the incident handling process.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Incident handling uses automated tools (like a SOAR platform) to speed up detection, ticketing, and initial containment actions, rather than every step being entirely manual.

evidence_required.description: Automated incident handling tool (SOAR/case management) configuration and workflow logs.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Correlate incident information and individual incident responses to achieve an organization-wide perspective.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Individual incidents aren't handled in isolation — information from separate incidents across the organization is correlated to spot broader patterns, such as multiple related incidents indicating a coordinated attack campaign.

evidence_required.description: Cross-incident correlation reports/analysis demonstrating organization-wide incident perspective.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA-NSOC develops remediation instructions and timelines when a system requires remediation due to an incident. Information System Owners must implement remediation requirements within the established timelines or submit an RBD to VA-NSOC.
va_specific_requirements: Information System Owners must meet VA-NSOC established remediation timelines or submit a Risk-Based Decision.
VA establishes performance metrics to measure incident response effectiveness.

controls.plain_english_explanation: When an incident happens, the organization follows a structured process: detect it, analyze it, contain it, eliminate the threat, and recover — then feed lessons learned back into future training and procedures. VA's central security operations (VA-NSOC) sets remediation deadlines that system owners must meet.

evidence_required.description: Incident handling procedures covering the full lifecycle (detection through recovery).
Incident tickets/case records demonstrating the handling process was followed.
RBD documentation for any missed VA-NSOC remediation timeline.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Incident handling and incident reporting are two halves of the same overall response process.
Incident handling is explicitly coordinated with contingency planning activities.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Track and document incidents.
nist_800_53.discussion: Documenting incidents includes maintaining records about each incident, status, and other pertinent information for forensics and trend evaluation.
assessment_objectives: Determine if incidents are tracked and documented.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Automated Tracking, Data Collection, and Analysis

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automated mechanisms to assist in tracking security incidents and in collecting/analyzing incident information.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, incident tracking and data collection are automated (via a case management/SIEM platform) rather than relying on manually maintained spreadsheets or logs.

evidence_required.description: Automated incident tracking system configuration and data collection logs.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Every incident is tracked and documented in a case-management system with enough detail to support later forensic investigation or trend analysis.

evidence_required.description: Incident tracking system records/tickets.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Monitoring records are generated as part of the incident handling process.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require personnel to report suspected incidents to the incident response capability within a defined time period; report incident information to defined authorities.
nist_800_53.discussion: Federal policy requires agencies to report incidents to US-CERT within specified time frames.
assessment_objectives: Determine if personnel are required to report suspected incidents within a defined time period.
Determine if incident information is reported to defined authorities.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automated mechanisms to assist in reporting security incidents.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Reporting a security incident is partially automated (e.g., a ticketing tool automatically notifies VA-NSOC and generates the required report fields), reducing the chance of a delayed or incomplete manual report.

evidence_required.description: Automated incident reporting tool configuration and sample generated report.

va_odp_values.value: Immediately upon suspicion, to ISO, PO, and supervisor
To US-CERT

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: The ISO/PO contact VA-NSOC within one hour to coordinate response. If criminal activity is suspected, local VA Police and OIG are also contacted.
va_specific_requirements: VA-NSOC must be notified within one hour of a suspected/confirmed incident.
Privacy-related incidents reported to US-CERT within one hour of discovery.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping. VA's one-hour reporting SLA is notably stricter than the generic 'organization-defined time period' in the base NIST control.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Anyone who suspects a security incident must report it immediately — VA requires notification to the ISO, Privacy Officer, and supervisor right away, and to VA's central security operations center within one hour.

evidence_required.description: Incident reporting policy specifying timelines and reporting chain.
Incident reports/tickets with timestamps demonstrating the 1-hour VA-NSOC notification SLA was met.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Reported incidents are what feeds the incident handling process.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide an incident response support resource that offers advice and assistance to users for the handling and reporting of incidents.
nist_800_53.discussion: This support resource is integral to the organizational incident response capability.
assessment_objectives: Determine if an incident response support resource offering advice/assistance is provided.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Automation Support for Availability of Information and Support

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automated mechanisms to increase the availability of incident response-related information and support.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Incident response support and guidance (like knowledge base articles or a self-service portal) are made available through automated tools, so users/staff can quickly find help without waiting for a live person during a busy incident.

evidence_required.description: Automated incident response support resource (knowledge base, self-service portal) availability documentation.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA-NSOC provides internal assistance to VA in handling incidents, technical queries, alerts and advisories, with a 24-hour incident response center.

controls.plain_english_explanation: There's a dedicated support resource (VA-NSOC, available 24/7) that users and staff can call for help handling or reporting a security incident.

evidence_required.description: Incident response support resource contact information/availability documentation.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: The support resource is the point of contact for reporting.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop an incident response plan that provides a roadmap for implementing the incident response capability, defines reportable incidents, and is reviewed/approved; distribute the plan; review and update it; protect it from unauthorized disclosure/modification.
nist_800_53.discussion: The incident response plan describes the structure/organization of the incident response capability and defines resources/management support needed.
assessment_objectives: Determine if an incident response plan providing a roadmap for implementing the incident response capability is developed and approved.
Determine if the plan is distributed to defined personnel and organizational elements.
Determine if the plan is reviewed and updated.
Determine if changes are communicated to defined personnel.

va_odp_values.value: Annually
Key personnel identified in the incident response plan

controls.plain_english_explanation: There's a formal, written incident response plan (the master roadmap for how the organization responds to incidents), reviewed annually and distributed to the people who need it.

evidence_required.description: Incident response plan.
Annual IR plan review record.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: The plan documents the incident handling process required by IR-4.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Respond to information spills by identifying the specific information involved, alerting designated personnel using a communication method not associated with the spill, isolating the contaminated system/component, eradicating the information, identifying other potentially contaminated systems, and performing other defined actions.
nist_800_53.discussion: An 'information spillage' occurs when sensitive information is placed on a system not authorized to process that information.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time; OI&T may elect to implement an information spillage response at their discretion.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA as a distinct control — this would cover the specific response process for when sensitive information ends up on a system not authorized to handle it.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish an integrated team of forensic/malware analysts, tool developers, and real-time operations personnel.
nist_800_53.discussion: A dedicated, cross-functional team combining incident response, forensics, and tool development capabilities.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would establish a dedicated, cross-functional forensics/malware analysis team.

control_families.family_description: Governs system maintenance activities including scheduling, tools, personnel, remote maintenance, and timely repair.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate a system maintenance policy and procedures; review/update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for maintenance.
assessment_objectives: Determine if system maintenance policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written system maintenance policy, reviewed periodically.

evidence_required.description: System maintenance policy document.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same policy documentation pattern.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Schedule, document, and review records of maintenance/repairs on system components per manufacturer specifications; approve and monitor maintenance activities; require approval for removal of components for off-site maintenance; sanitize equipment before off-site removal; verify security controls post-maintenance; include maintenance information in records.
nist_800_53.discussion: Applies to all types of maintenance (in-contract, warranty, in-house) on any component including non-processing devices like scanners/copiers/printers.
assessment_objectives: Determine if maintenance/repairs are scheduled, performed, documented, and reviewed per manufacturer/organizational requirements.
Determine if maintenance activities are approved and monitored.
Determine if removal of components for off-site maintenance requires approval.
Determine if equipment is sanitized before off-site removal.
Determine if security controls are verified as functioning properly following maintenance.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automated mechanisms to schedule/conduct/document maintenance and repairs, producing up-to-date records.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, maintenance scheduling and documentation are handled through automated tools rather than manually written maintenance logs, keeping records more current and less prone to gaps.

evidence_required.description: Automated maintenance scheduling/documentation tool output.

va_odp_values.value: Date/time, personnel/group performing maintenance, escort name (if applicable), description of maintenance performed, components removed/replaced with identification numbers

controls.plain_english_explanation: Maintenance on equipment (including things like printers/scanners, not just servers) must be scheduled, approved, and documented — and if equipment leaves the building for repair, it must first be wiped of sensitive data.

evidence_required.description: Maintenance logs/records including required data fields.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Sanitization of equipment prior to off-site maintenance uses the same media sanitization requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Approve, control, and monitor system maintenance tools.
nist_800_53.discussion: Maintenance tools can include hardware, software, and firmware items, and are potential vehicles for introducing malicious code.
assessment_objectives: Determine if maintenance tools are approved, controlled, and monitored.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Inspect maintenance tools carried into a facility for improper or unauthorized modifications.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: When a technician brings diagnostic or repair tools into a facility, those tools are physically inspected first to make sure they haven't been tampered with or modified to include hidden malicious functionality.

evidence_required.description: Maintenance tool inspection log/checklist.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Check media containing diagnostic/test programs for malicious code before use in the system.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Diagnostic disks, USB drives, or other media used for maintenance are scanned for malware before being connected to the system — a technician's tool media could otherwise be an infection vector.

evidence_required.description: Malware scan logs for maintenance/diagnostic media prior to use.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Prevent unauthorized removal of maintenance equipment containing organizational information by verifying no sensitive data remains, sanitizing/destroying the equipment, retaining it, or obtaining an exemption.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, equipment used for maintenance can't just be taken off-site by a technician if it might still contain sensitive VA data — it must first be verified clean, sanitized, kept on-site, or specifically exempted with approval.

evidence_required.description: Maintenance equipment removal authorization/sanitization verification record.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Tools used to maintain/diagnose systems (including diagnostic hardware/software) must be inspected before use to make sure they haven't been tampered with or infected with malware.

evidence_required.description: Maintenance tool approval/inspection log.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Malicious code scanning of maintenance media overlaps with general malicious code protection.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Approve and monitor nonlocal maintenance/diagnostic activities; allow use of nonlocal maintenance tools only consistent with policy; employ strong authenticators; maintain records; terminate sessions/connections when maintenance is complete.
nist_800_53.discussion: Nonlocal maintenance is conducted by individuals communicating through a network rather than being physically present.
assessment_objectives: Determine if nonlocal maintenance/diagnostic activities are approved and monitored.
Determine if strong authenticators are employed in establishing nonlocal maintenance sessions.
Determine if records are maintained and sessions terminated upon completion.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Document in the security plan the policies/procedures for establishment and use of nonlocal maintenance connections.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The rules for how remote (over-the-network) maintenance connections are set up and used are written down in the system's security plan, not left as informal practice.

evidence_required.description: SSP section documenting nonlocal maintenance policies/procedures.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require nonlocal maintenance/diagnostics be performed from a system with comparable security capability, or sanitize the component before/after service.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, remote maintenance can only be performed from a system that has equally strong security protections as the system being maintained — or if that's not possible, the component is sanitized before and after the maintenance session.

evidence_required.description: Verification of comparable security on the remote maintenance system, or sanitization records if used instead.

controls.plain_english_explanation: When maintenance is performed remotely (over the network rather than in person), it must be approved, use strong authentication, be logged, and the connection closed when finished.

evidence_required.description: Remote maintenance session logs.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Nonlocal maintenance is a form of remote access and shares similar authentication/monitoring requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish a process for maintenance personnel authorization and maintain a list of authorized maintenance organizations/personnel; ensure non-escorted personnel have required access authorizations; designate personnel with required authorizations/technical competence to supervise maintenance by personnel who lack required access authorizations.
nist_800_53.discussion: Applies to individuals performing hardware/software maintenance; physical access for maintenance personnel is addressed separately under PE-2.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a process for maintenance personnel authorization is established and a list maintained.
Determine if non-escorted personnel have required access authorizations.
Determine if qualified personnel are designated to supervise unauthorized maintenance personnel.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement procedures for maintenance personnel lacking appropriate access authorizations, including escort/supervision and sanitization of volatile/non-volatile storage before maintenance.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: If a maintenance technician doesn't have the appropriate security clearance/authorization, they must be escorted/supervised the entire time, and any storage that could contain sensitive data is wiped before they begin working on it.

evidence_required.description: Escort/supervision and pre-maintenance sanitization procedure for unauthorized maintenance personnel.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Temporary credentials may be issued for maintenance personnel needing little/no-notice access (e.g., vendors, systems integrators); must be documented for one-time use or a limited period.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Only authorized, vetted people (or properly escorted/supervised unauthorized personnel) can perform maintenance on a system — vendors doing repairs on short notice may get temporary, documented, limited-duration credentials.

evidence_required.description: List of authorized maintenance personnel/organizations.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Third-party maintenance personnel are subject to the same third-party personnel security requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Obtain maintenance support and/or spare parts for defined system components within a defined time period of failure.
nist_800_53.discussion: The organization specifies which components result in increased risk to operations when not operational.
assessment_objectives: Determine if maintenance support and/or spare parts are obtained within a defined time period for defined critical components.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Components selected per criticality/business need/risk; semi-annual component review; changes documented and SSP updated as needed.

controls.plain_english_explanation: For critical system parts, the organization arranges maintenance/spare-part support in advance so a failure doesn't cause extended downtime waiting for repairs.

evidence_required.description: Maintenance contract/warranty terms for critical components.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Critical components requiring timely maintenance are identified via the component inventory.

control_families.family_description: Governs access to, marking, storage, transport, sanitization, and use of both digital and non-digital media.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate a media protection policy and procedures; review/update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for media protection.
assessment_objectives: Determine if media protection policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written media protection policy, reviewed periodically.

evidence_required.description: Media protection policy document.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same policy documentation pattern.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Restrict access to defined types of digital and non-digital media to a defined list of authorized individuals.
nist_800_53.discussion: This control applies to both electronic and physical (paper) media.
assessment_objectives: Determine if access to defined types of media is restricted to a defined list of authorized individuals.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Use of VA information system media within an Operating Unit must first be authorized by the Information System Owner, local CIO, or designee.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Access to media (both paper documents and digital storage) containing sensitive information is limited to specifically authorized people.

evidence_required.description: Media access authorization list.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Mobile/portable storage device controls overlap with media access restrictions.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Mark system media indicating distribution limitations, handling caveats, and applicable security markings; exempt specific types of media from marking as long as they remain within defined controlled areas.
nist_800_53.discussion: The term security marking refers to the application/use of human-readable security attributes.
assessment_objectives: Determine if system media is marked with distribution limitations, handling caveats, and security markings.
Determine if exempted media types remain within designated controlled areas.

va_odp_values.value: Removable media documented in SSP (e.g., disk packs, backup tapes) within the designated secured computer room

controls.plain_english_explanation: Media containing sensitive information should be labeled to indicate handling restrictions, unless it stays within a designated secure area the entire time (e.g., backup tapes that never leave the secured server room).

evidence_required.description: Media marking policy and list of exempted media types/controlled areas.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Marking informs the handling requirements applied when media is transported.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Physically control and securely store defined types of digital and non-digital media within controlled areas; protect media until destroyed or sanitized.
nist_800_53.discussion: Controlled areas provide sufficient physical/procedural safeguards for protecting information.
assessment_objectives: Determine if defined types of media are physically controlled and securely stored within controlled areas.
Determine if media is protected until destroyed or sanitized.

va_specific_requirements: Mobile devices, portable storage, and hardcopy sensitive information stored securely when not in use (locked cabinets/drawers/rooms).

controls.plain_english_explanation: Sensitive media (both digital storage devices and paper) must be physically secured (locked storage) when not actively in use, until it's properly destroyed or wiped.

evidence_required.description: Evidence of secure storage practices (locked cabinets, controlled rooms).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Media storage areas rely on the same physical access control mechanisms.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Protect and control defined types of media during transport outside of controlled areas using defined security safeguards; maintain accountability during transport; document transport activities; restrict transport activities to authorized personnel.
nist_800_53.discussion: Physical/technical safeguards are commensurate with the security category of the information residing on the media.
assessment_objectives: Determine if media is protected/controlled during transport outside controlled areas.
Determine if accountability is maintained and transport activities documented and restricted to authorized personnel.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to protect the confidentiality/integrity of information stored on digital media during transport outside of controlled areas.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Digital media (like backup drives) being physically transported outside a secure facility is encrypted, so even if it's lost or stolen in transit, the data on it can't be read.

evidence_required.description: Encryption configuration for digital media transported outside controlled areas.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Media should be double-wrapped and secured in a physical container when appropriate to prevent loss/compromise.

controls.plain_english_explanation: When media leaves a secure area (e.g., shipping backup tapes to an offsite facility), it must be encrypted and physically protected (e.g., sealed container), with a documented chain of custody.

evidence_required.description: Media transport procedure including packaging/encryption requirements.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Encryption of media in transit shares the same cryptographic protection requirement.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Sanitize system media prior to disposal, release out of organizational control, or release for reuse, using defined sanitization techniques/procedures per applicable standards/policies; employ sanitization mechanisms with strength commensurate with the information's security category.
nist_800_53.discussion: Applies to all media subject to disposal or reuse, whether or not considered removable/portable/mobile.
assessment_objectives: Determine if system media is sanitized prior to disposal/release/reuse using defined techniques per applicable standards.
Determine if sanitization mechanisms have strength/integrity commensurate with the information's sensitivity.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Review, Approve, Track, Document, and Verify

nist_800_53.control_statement: Review, approve, track, document, and verify media sanitization and disposal actions.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, media sanitization/disposal isn't just performed and forgotten — each action is reviewed, formally approved, tracked, and verified as actually complete, with a documented record.

evidence_required.description: Media sanitization/disposal approval, tracking, and verification records.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Test sanitization equipment/procedures to verify intended sanitization is achieved.

va_odp_values.value: Annually

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The actual equipment/tools used to wipe media (like degaussers or wiping software) are tested annually to confirm they actually achieve complete sanitization — not just assumed to work.

evidence_required.description: Annual sanitization equipment testing/verification results.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Apply nondestructive sanitization techniques to portable storage devices prior to connecting to the system under defined circumstances.

va_odp_values.value: When devices are first purchased prior to initial use, or when chain of custody is lost

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: New portable storage devices are sanitized (using a technique that doesn't destroy the device) before their first use, and again if the chain of custody is ever broken — ensuring nothing unexpected is already on the device.

evidence_required.description: Nondestructive sanitization procedure for new/chain-of-custody-broken portable storage devices.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Sanitization must remove all VA sensitive data and render it unreadable. Hard drives encrypted with FIPS 140-2 (or successor) validated encryption do not require pre-sanitization prior to leaving VA control. The ISO coordinates/audits the media sanitization process annually.
va_specific_requirements: ISO conducts an annual audit of the media sanitization process.
Inventory and disposition records maintained for sanitized media.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping. See VA Handbook 6500.1 for approved sanitization equipment/techniques.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Before media is thrown away, given away, or reused, all sensitive data must be completely and irreversibly wiped from it — the ISO audits this process annually to make sure it's actually happening correctly.

evidence_required.description: Media sanitization procedure (referencing VA Handbook 6500.1 methods).
Sanitization/disposal certificates or logs.
Annual ISO audit of the sanitization process.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Equipment sanitized before off-site maintenance uses the same sanitization requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Restrict the use of defined types of system media on systems or system components using defined security safeguards.
nist_800_53.discussion: In contrast to MP-2 (which restricts access to media), this control restricts use of certain types of media on systems, e.g., restricting/prohibiting flash drives.
assessment_objectives: Determine if use of defined types of media is restricted using defined security safeguards.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Prohibit the use of portable storage devices in organizational systems when such devices have no identifiable owner.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: A USB drive or other portable storage device found without a clear, identifiable owner (like one found in a parking lot) is technically blocked from connecting to VA systems — an unidentified device is treated as a potential threat, not just plugged in.

evidence_required.description: Device control configuration blocking unregistered/ownerless portable storage devices.

va_specific_requirements: Non-VA-approved USB flash drives are blocked from connecting to VA systems; only FIPS 140-2 validated USB devices permitted.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Only approved, identifiable, encrypted removable media (like specific FIPS-validated USB drives) can be used with VA systems — unknown or unauthorized USB devices are technically blocked.

evidence_required.description: Device control/USB blocking technology configuration.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Approved encrypted USB/portable device requirements are shared between media use and mobile device access control.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish a media downgrading process that includes employing downgrading mechanisms with strength/integrity commensurate with the security category/classification level of the information to be removed; identify media requiring downgrading and downgrade the identified media using the established process.
nist_800_53.discussion: Media downgrading refers to changing the classification/sensitivity level of media (e.g., after appropriate sanitization) to allow broader use or handling.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time; OI&T may elect to employ media downgrading at their discretion.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this control would formalize a process for downgrading the sensitivity classification of media (e.g., after sanitization) to allow broader handling.

control_families.family_description: Governs physical access control, monitoring, environmental protections (fire, power, temperature, water), and secure handling of equipment at facilities.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate a physical and environmental protection policy and procedures; review/update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for physical/environmental protection.
assessment_objectives: Determine if physical and environmental protection policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA Handbook 0730 applies in addition to and in conjunction with the physical controls in VA Handbook 6500.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written physical and environmental security policy, reviewed periodically.

evidence_required.description: Physical and environmental protection policy document.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same policy documentation pattern.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, approve, and maintain a list of individuals with authorized access to the facility; issue authorization credentials; review the access list; remove individuals from the list when access is no longer required.
nist_800_53.discussion: Applies to employees and visitors; individuals with permanent access credentials are not considered visitors.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a list of individuals with authorized facility access is developed, approved, and maintained.
Determine if authorization credentials are issued.
Determine if the access list is reviewed.
Determine if individuals are removed from the list when access is no longer required.

va_odp_values.value: Bi-annually for Low; quarterly for Moderate and High

controls.plain_english_explanation: There's a maintained list of exactly who is authorized to physically access a facility, with credentials issued (like badges) and the list reviewed periodically to remove people who no longer need access.

evidence_required.description: Physical access authorization list/PACS export.
Periodic access list review record.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Personnel termination triggers removal from the physical access list.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Enforce physical access authorizations at entry/exit points by verifying authorizations and controlling ingress/egress using physical access control systems, devices, or guards; maintain physical access audit logs; control access to publicly accessible areas; escort/monitor visitors under defined circumstances; secure and inventory keys/combinations/access devices; change combinations/keys per schedule or when compromised.
nist_800_53.discussion: Facility guards may be professional physical security staff or other personnel. Physical access devices include keys, locks, combinations, and card readers.
assessment_objectives: Determine if physical access authorizations are enforced at entry/exit points via verification and controlled ingress/egress.
Determine if physical access audit logs are maintained for entry/exit points.
Determine if security safeguards control access to publicly accessible areas.
Determine if visitors are escorted/monitored under defined circumstances.
Determine if keys/combinations/access devices are secured and inventoried.
Determine if combinations/keys are changed per the security plan and/or when compromised.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Enforce physical access authorizations to the system in addition to facility-level physical access controls, at physical spaces containing system components.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, getting into the building isn't enough on its own — there's an additional layer of physical access control specifically for the rooms/areas where the actual system components (servers, network gear) are located, like a separately badged server room within an already-secured building.

evidence_required.description: Evidence of additional physical access controls for spaces containing system components (e.g., separate server room badge access).

va_odp_values.value: VHA medical facilities: visitors escorted/monitored after operating hours (facilities generally open to the public with official business per 38 C.F.R. 1.218). VBA regional offices: visitors sponsored and escorted at all times.
Every 12 months

controls.plain_english_explanation: Physical entry to a facility is controlled with badges/access systems or guards, entry/exit is logged, and visitors are escorted according to the facility type. Physical access devices (keys, badges) are inventoried annually.

evidence_required.description: Physical access control system (PACS) logs.
Visitor escort policy per facility type.
Annual physical access device inventory.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Physical access control enforces the authorization list maintained under PE-2.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Control physical access to system distribution and transmission lines within organizational facilities using defined security safeguards.
nist_800_53.discussion: Physical safeguards help prevent accidental damage, disruption, physical tampering, or eavesdropping/in-transit modification of unencrypted transmissions.
assessment_objectives: Determine if physical access to system distribution/transmission lines is controlled using defined safeguards.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Safeguards include locked wiring closets, disconnected/locked spare jacks, and protection of cabling via conduit/cable trays.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Network cabling and wiring closets are physically secured (locked) so someone can't tap into or damage them.

evidence_required.description: Evidence of locked wiring closets/cable protection.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Wiring closet access relies on the same physical access control mechanisms.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Control physical access to output devices to prevent unauthorized individuals from obtaining the output.
nist_800_53.discussion: Monitors, printers, copiers, scanners, and fax machines are examples of output devices.
assessment_objectives: Determine if physical access to output devices is controlled to prevent unauthorized individuals from obtaining output.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Monitors used by employees in public areas should be positioned so the public cannot view the screen; when not possible, privacy screens are used.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Printouts, printer output trays, and monitor screens must be positioned or controlled so unauthorized people (like members of the public) can't see or grab sensitive printed/displayed information.

evidence_required.description: Evidence of monitor positioning/privacy screens in public-facing areas.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Physical placement of output devices overlaps with general component location considerations.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Monitor physical access to the facility to detect and respond to physical security incidents; review physical access logs at a defined frequency and upon occurrence of defined events; coordinate results of reviews with the incident response capability.
nist_800_53.discussion: Suspicious physical access activities include access outside normal work hours, repeated access to unusual areas, or out-of-sequence access.
assessment_objectives: Determine if physical access is monitored to detect/respond to incidents.
Determine if physical access logs are reviewed at a defined frequency and upon defined events.
Determine if review results are coordinated with incident response.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Monitor physical intrusion alarms and surveillance equipment.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Physical intrusion alarms and security cameras aren't just installed — they're actively monitored (either by staff or a monitoring service) so an alert or camera feed actually triggers a response.

evidence_required.description: Physical security monitoring staffing/service documentation confirming active alarm/camera monitoring.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Monitor physical access to the system in addition to facility-level monitoring, at physical spaces containing system components.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, physical access monitoring goes beyond the general facility level — there's dedicated monitoring specifically for the rooms/areas containing system components, like camera coverage focused on the server room door specifically.

evidence_required.description: Physical access monitoring logs specific to system component locations (e.g., server room access logs).

controls.plain_english_explanation: Physical access to the facility is actively monitored (cameras, alarms), and access logs are periodically reviewed for suspicious patterns (like access at 3 AM or repeated unusual entries) — findings are shared with incident response.

evidence_required.description: Physical access/surveillance monitoring logs.
Physical access log review records.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Physical access review can be correlated with audit log review for a fuller security picture.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Withdrawn; incorporated into PE-2 and PE-3.
nist_800_53.discussion: Requirements folded into PE-2 (Physical Access Authorizations) and PE-3 (Physical Access Control).

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Withdrawn control; VA 6500 explicitly notes this as incorporated into PE-2 and PE-3.

controls.plain_english_explanation: This control no longer exists on its own — its requirements are now covered under Physical Access Authorizations (PE-2) and Physical Access Control (PE-3).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Absorbed part of this withdrawn control's requirements.
Absorbed part of this withdrawn control's requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Maintain visitor access records to the facility for a defined time period; review visitor access records at a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Visitor access records are not required for publicly accessible areas.
assessment_objectives: Determine if visitor access records are maintained for a defined time period.
Determine if visitor access records are reviewed at a defined frequency.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automated mechanisms to facilitate maintenance and review of visitor access records.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk facilities, visitor logs are maintained and reviewed using an automated system (like an electronic visitor management platform) rather than a handwritten paper sign-in sheet.

evidence_required.description: Electronic visitor management system records/reports.

va_odp_values.value: 1 year
Quarterly for Low; weekly for Moderate; daily for High

va_specific_requirements: Visitor records include: name/organization of visitor, signature, ID type, date/time of entry and departure, purpose of visit, and name/organization of person visited.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Visitor sign-in logs (name, purpose, who they visited, time in/out) are kept for a year and reviewed regularly — more often for higher-risk facilities.

evidence_required.description: Visitor log/sign-in records.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Visitor escort requirements under PE-3 generate the records tracked here.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Protect power equipment and power cabling for the system from damage and destruction.
nist_800_53.discussion: Protection needs vary based on location (internal cabling within a data center vs. external generators/cabling).
assessment_objectives: Determine if power equipment and cabling are protected from damage and destruction.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Power cables and equipment (generators, UPS units, etc.) are physically protected from accidental or intentional damage.

evidence_required.description: Evidence of power equipment protection measures.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Power equipment protection supports the emergency power capability.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide the capability of shutting off power to the system or individual components in emergency situations; place emergency shutoff switches/devices in accessible locations; protect emergency power shutoff capability from unauthorized activation.
nist_800_53.discussion: Applies primarily to facilities containing concentrations of system resources (data centers, server rooms).
assessment_objectives: Determine if emergency power shutoff capability is provided.
Determine if shutoff switches are placed to facilitate safe/easy access.
Determine if the shutoff capability is protected from unauthorized activation.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Data centers/server rooms have an emergency power shutoff switch that's accessible in an emergency but protected from accidental or malicious triggering.

evidence_required.description: Evidence of emergency shutoff switch installation and protection.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Emergency shutoff is often part of the broader fire protection/emergency response plan.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide a short-term uninterruptible power supply to facilitate an orderly shutdown or transition to long-term alternate power in the event of a primary power loss.
nist_800_53.discussion: Long-term alternate power can be provided via secondary commercial power or other external supply.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a short-term uninterruptible power supply is provided to facilitate orderly shutdown or transition to alternate power.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Long-Term Alternate Power — Minimal Operational Capability

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide a long-term alternate power supply capable of maintaining minimally required operational capability during an extended loss of primary power.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Beyond short-term battery backup, the highest-risk facilities also have a longer-term power solution (like a generator) that can keep at least essential functions running through an extended outage, not just long enough for a graceful shutdown.

evidence_required.description: Generator/long-term alternate power specifications and testing records.

controls.plain_english_explanation: There's backup power (like a UPS/battery backup, and possibly a generator for extended outages) so systems can shut down gracefully or keep running during a power loss.

evidence_required.description: UPS/generator specifications and testing records.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Alternate processing sites also require emergency power capability.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ and maintain automatic emergency lighting that activates in the event of a power outage/disruption and covers emergency exits/evacuation routes.
nist_800_53.discussion: Applies primarily to facilities containing concentrations of system resources.
assessment_objectives: Determine if automatic emergency lighting is employed and maintained, covering emergency exits and evacuation routes.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Emergency lighting automatically turns on during a power outage to illuminate exits and evacuation routes.

evidence_required.description: Evidence of functioning emergency lighting.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Part of the broader physical emergency response infrastructure.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ and maintain fire suppression and detection devices/systems supported by an independent energy source.
nist_800_53.discussion: Fire suppression/detection devices include sprinkler systems, handheld extinguishers, fixed fire hoses, and smoke detectors.
assessment_objectives: Determine if fire suppression and detection devices/systems supported by an independent energy source are employed and maintained.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ fire detection devices/systems that activate automatically and notify defined personnel and emergency responders.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Fire detection systems in the highest-risk facilities automatically alert both internal personnel and external emergency responders (like the fire department) as soon as smoke/fire is detected, without requiring a person to manually call it in.
