evidence_required.description: Fire detection system configuration showing automatic notification to personnel and emergency responders.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ fire suppression devices/systems that provide automatic notification of activation to defined personnel and emergency responders.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: If the fire suppression system (like sprinklers) actually activates, that activation itself automatically triggers a notification to personnel and emergency responders — so people know a fire event occurred even if nobody witnessed it directly.

evidence_required.description: Fire suppression system configuration showing automatic activation notification.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automatic fire suppression capability when the facility is not staffed on a continuous basis.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For facilities that aren't staffed around the clock, fire suppression happens automatically (like an automatic sprinkler or gas suppression system) rather than relying on someone being present to manually respond.

evidence_required.description: Automatic fire suppression system installation/maintenance records.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Facilities have fire detection and suppression systems (smoke detectors, sprinklers) that work independently of the main power supply and, for higher-risk facilities, automatically notify emergency responders.

evidence_required.description: Fire suppression/detection system inspection/maintenance records.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Fire systems have an independent energy source separate from primary facility power.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Maintain temperature and humidity levels within the facility at acceptable levels; monitor temperature and humidity levels.
nist_800_53.discussion: Applies primarily to facilities containing concentrations of system resources.
assessment_objectives: Determine if temperature/humidity levels are maintained at acceptable levels.
Determine if temperature/humidity levels are monitored.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Acceptable levels documented in the SSP in compliance with manufacturer requirements.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Server rooms/data centers maintain and monitor appropriate temperature and humidity levels to prevent equipment damage.

evidence_required.description: Environmental monitoring system logs (temperature/humidity).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Environmental controls and fire protection are both part of facility infrastructure protection.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Protect the system from damage resulting from water leakage by providing master shutoff or isolation valves that are accessible, working properly, and known to key personnel.
nist_800_53.discussion: Applies primarily to facilities containing concentrations of system resources.
assessment_objectives: Determine if master shutoff/isolation valves are accessible, working properly, and known to key personnel.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ mechanisms to detect the presence of water near the system and alert defined personnel.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The highest-risk facilities have automated water-detection sensors (not just manual shutoff valves) that alert staff the moment water is detected near sensitive equipment, catching leaks before they cause major damage.

evidence_required.description: Water detection sensor installation and alert configuration records.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Data centers have accessible water shutoff valves that key staff know how to use, and higher-risk facilities have automated water-detection sensors that trigger alerts.

evidence_required.description: Evidence of accessible/functioning water shutoff valves.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Part of general facility environmental risk protection.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Authorize, monitor, and control defined types of system components entering and exiting the facility, and maintain records of those items.
nist_800_53.discussion: Effective enforcement may require restricting access to delivery areas and possibly isolating them from the system/media libraries.
assessment_objectives: Determine if defined types of system components entering/exiting the facility are authorized, monitored, and controlled, with records maintained.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Facilities maintain an approved list of personnel authorized to deliver/remove IT equipment, in conjunction with a property pass system per VA Handbook 7002-1.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Equipment coming into or leaving a facility (like a new server or an old laptop) is tracked and requires authorization — VA uses a property pass system for this.

evidence_required.description: Property pass/equipment delivery-removal log.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Equipment entering/leaving affects the component inventory.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ defined security controls at alternate work sites; assess the effectiveness of controls at alternate sites; provide a means for employees to communicate with security personnel in case of incidents.
nist_800_53.discussion: Alternate work sites may include government facilities and private residences; supports telework and contingency operations.
assessment_objectives: Determine if defined security controls are employed at alternate work sites.
Determine if control effectiveness at alternate sites is assessed.
Determine if employees have a means to communicate with security personnel regarding incidents.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Telework/alternate work site practices are conducted per VA Directive/Handbook 5011, Hours of Duty and Leave, and related VA teleworking directives.

controls.plain_english_explanation: When employees work from home or another alternate location, appropriate security controls still apply there too, and they have a way to reach security staff if something goes wrong.

evidence_required.description: Telework/alternate work site security policy.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Remote access requirements are the technical enforcement mechanism for alternate work site security.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Position system components within the facility to minimize potential damage from physical/environmental hazards and to minimize opportunity for unauthorized access.
nist_800_53.discussion: Physical/environmental hazards include flooding, fire, tornados, earthquakes, and acts of terrorism.
assessment_objectives: Determine if system components are positioned to minimize damage from hazards and unauthorized access opportunity.

controls.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, equipment is physically placed to reduce risk from natural disasters and to make unauthorized physical access more difficult.

evidence_required.description: Facility hazard assessment and equipment placement rationale.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Component placement affects output device access control as well.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Protect the system from information leakage due to electromagnetic signals emanations.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses TEMPEST-type concerns regarding unintentional compromising emanations from equipment.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time; OI&T may elect to protect against information leakage at their discretion.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would protect against unintentional electromagnetic signal leakage that could reveal sensitive information (a TEMPEST-type concern).

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ asset location technologies to track and monitor the location and movement of assets within controlled areas; ensure asset location technologies are employed in accordance with applicable laws/regulations/policies.
nist_800_53.discussion: Typically implemented via RFID or similar tracking technology for high-value or sensitive equipment.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time; OI&T may elect to employ asset monitoring and tracking at their discretion.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would use technology like RFID tags to actively track the physical location of equipment within a facility.

control_families.family_description: Governs system security plans, rules of behavior, information security architecture, and central management of controls.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate a security planning policy and procedures; review/update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for security planning.
assessment_objectives: Determine if security planning policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written security planning policy, reviewed periodically.

evidence_required.description: Security planning policy document.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same policy documentation pattern.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop a security plan that is consistent with the enterprise architecture, explicitly defines the authorization boundary, describes the operational context and security requirements, describes the security controls in place/planned, and is approved by the authorizing official prior to plan implementation; distribute the plan; review and update it.
nist_800_53.discussion: The security plan is a living document, updated throughout the system lifecycle, and is a major component of the authorization package.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a security plan explicitly defining the authorization boundary, operational context, and security requirements is developed.
Determine if the plan describes security controls in place or planned, with tailoring rationale.
Determine if the plan is reviewed and approved by the authorizing official prior to implementation.
Determine if copies of the plan are distributed and changes communicated to designated personnel.
Determine if the plan is reviewed and updated to address changes/problems identified.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Plan and Coordinate with Other Organizational Entities

nist_800_53.control_statement: Plan and coordinate security-related activities affecting the system with defined individuals/groups before conducting such activities, to reduce impact on other organizational entities.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Before conducting security-related activities that could affect other parts of the organization (like a major system update or a penetration test), the team coordinates with those other groups in advance so nobody is caught off guard by unexpected disruptions.

evidence_required.description: Coordination records showing advance notice/planning with affected organizational entities.

va_odp_values.value: Annually

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Every VA information system must be covered by a System Security Plan (SSP) compliant with NIST SP 800-18 and 800-53, maintained in the VA-approved FISMA database. SSPs are dynamic documents undergoing constant updates throughout the system life cycle.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Every system needs a formal, comprehensive System Security Plan (SSP) documenting its boundaries, requirements, and the security controls in place — approved before the system goes live and kept updated continuously, not just written once.

evidence_required.description: Current System Security Plan (SSP).
Annual SSP review/approval record.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: The SSP is the core document supporting the system's authorization decision.
Security categorization results are documented within the SSP.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Withdrawn; incorporated into PL-2.
nist_800_53.discussion: Requirements folded into PL-2 (System Security and Privacy Plans).

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Withdrawn control; not separately tracked by VA 6500.

controls.plain_english_explanation: This control no longer exists on its own — its requirements are now covered under the System Security and Privacy Plans control (PL-2).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Absorbed this withdrawn control's requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish and make readily available rules describing responsibilities and expected behavior for information/system usage; receive a signed acknowledgment from individuals before authorizing access; review/update the rules; require re-signature when rules are revised.
nist_800_53.discussion: Rules of behavior represent a type of access agreement and are established for both privileged and general users.
assessment_objectives: Determine if rules of behavior are established and made available to individuals.
Determine if a signed acknowledgment is received before access is authorized.
Determine if the rules are reviewed and updated.
Determine if individuals who signed a previous version re-sign when rules are revised.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Social Media and External Site/Application Usage Restrictions

nist_800_53.control_statement: Include explicit restrictions on the use of social media/networking sites and posting organizational information on public websites.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The Rules of Behavior explicitly spell out what employees can and can't post on social media or public websites regarding VA information — this isn't left as an unwritten assumption.

evidence_required.description: Rules of Behavior section containing explicit social media/public posting restrictions.

va_odp_values.value: At least every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: The VA National ROB must be signed annually by all users of VA information systems or VA information. Contractors sign the Contractor ROB (in VA Handbook 6500.6) instead. Both are typically included as part of electronic security/privacy awareness training.
va_specific_requirements: VA National ROB signed annually by all users.
Refusal to sign results in denial of access.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Everyone must read, understand, and sign a Rules of Behavior document describing what they can and can't do with VA systems/information — and VA requires this signature annually, not just once at hire.

evidence_required.description: Signed Rules of Behavior (annual) for all users.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: ROB signature is typically bundled with the annual security awareness training event.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Withdrawn; incorporated into the PT family (PII Processing and Transparency).
nist_800_53.discussion: Rev 5 consolidated privacy impact assessment requirements into the new PT family and related PM controls.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Withdrawn/relocated control; VA 6500 Appendix F itself notes this control 'will be incorporated into policy created by Office of Privacy and Records Management,' effectively deferring to VA's separate Appendix E privacy overlay (AR-2, Privacy Impact and Risk Assessment).

controls.plain_english_explanation: This control no longer exists as a standalone security control — Privacy Impact Assessment requirements are now addressed under the newer PT family, and VA separately covers this through its Appendix E privacy program (AR-2).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: PIA requirements are now addressed within the PT family and related privacy program controls.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Withdrawn; incorporated into PL-2.
nist_800_53.discussion: Requirements folded into PL-2 (System Security and Privacy Plans).

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Withdrawn control; not separately tracked by VA 6500.

controls.plain_english_explanation: This control no longer exists on its own — its requirements are now covered under the System Security and Privacy Plans control (PL-2).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Absorbed this withdrawn control's requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop a Concept of Operations (CONOPS) for the system describing how the organization intends to operate the system from the perspective of information security and privacy; review and update the CONOPS.
nist_800_53.discussion: Provides a high-level operational narrative complementing the more technical SSP.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time; OI&T may elect to develop a security Concept of Operations at their discretion.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would be a high-level narrative document describing how the organization intends to operate the system from a security perspective, distinct from the more technical SSP.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop an information security architecture describing the overall philosophy/approach to protecting confidentiality/integrity/availability, how it integrates into the enterprise architecture, and dependencies on external services; review/update the architecture to reflect enterprise architecture updates; ensure planned changes are reflected in the security plan/procurements.
nist_800_53.discussion: The information security architecture at the system level complements the broader organization-wide architecture developed under PM-7.
assessment_objectives: Determine if an information security architecture describing protection philosophy, EA integration, and external dependencies is developed.
Determine if the architecture is reviewed/updated to reflect EA updates.
Determine if planned changes are reflected in the security plan and procurements.

va_odp_values.value: Annually, or whenever significant changes are made

controls.plain_english_explanation: There's a documented security architecture explaining the overall approach to protecting the system, how that fits into the broader enterprise architecture, and any dependencies on outside services — kept current as the architecture evolves.

evidence_required.description: Information security architecture document.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System-level security architecture must align with the organization-wide enterprise architecture.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Centrally manage defined security controls and related processes.
nist_800_53.discussion: Enables consolidated management of controls that apply across multiple systems, reducing duplication of effort.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time; OI&T may elect to employ central management at their discretion. Note: VA does implement centralized common controls conceptually (see Appendix F, Attachment 1), but this is not tracked as a formal PL-9 allocation.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline as a distinct control, though VA's common-control structure (Attachment 1) achieves similar centralization informally.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not formally required by VA as a distinct control — though VA does informally achieve centralized control management through its 'common controls' structure (Attachment 1 of Appendix F).

control_families.family_description: Governs position risk designation, personnel screening, termination, transfer, third-party personnel, access agreements, and sanctions.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate a personnel security policy and procedures; review/update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for personnel security.
assessment_objectives: Determine if personnel security policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written personnel security policy, reviewed periodically.

evidence_required.description: Personnel security policy document.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same policy documentation pattern.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Assign a risk designation to all organizational positions; establish screening criteria for individuals filling those positions; review/update position risk designations on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Position risk designations reflect the potential for adverse impact to the organization's mission/business functions.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a risk designation is assigned to all positions.
Determine if screening criteria are established.
Determine if designations are reviewed/updated on a defined frequency.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Per VA Directive/Handbook 0710.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Every job position is assigned a risk level (e.g., low/moderate/high risk to the organization), which determines what level of background screening that position requires.

evidence_required.description: Position risk designation records/position descriptions.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Position risk designation directly determines the screening level required under PS-3.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Screen individuals prior to authorizing access to the system; rescreen individuals per defined conditions and frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Personnel screening activities involve the assessment of conduct, integrity, judgment, loyalty, reliability, and stability.
assessment_objectives: Determine if individuals are screened prior to authorizing access.
Determine if individuals are rescreened per defined conditions/frequency.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: All personnel must be subject to a successfully adjudicated background screening (e.g., Special Agreement Check) prior to permanent access, per VA Directive/Handbook 0710 and VA Directive 0735 (HSPD-12). Compensated Work Therapy patients are not permitted access since VA cannot background-screen them.
va_specific_requirements: Successfully adjudicated background investigation required prior to permanent access.
Level of investigation varies with position sensitivity/risk.
Contractors must meet screening requirements specified in the contract/agreement.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Before anyone gets access to VA systems, they must pass a background investigation appropriate to the sensitivity of their position — and certain categories of individuals (like Compensated Work Therapy patients) simply cannot be screened and therefore cannot be granted access at all.

evidence_required.description: Background investigation completion/adjudication records.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Screening level required is determined by the position's risk designation.
Account creation approval workflow verifies screening was completed before granting access.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Upon termination of individual employment: disable system access; terminate/revoke authenticators and credentials; conduct exit interviews including a discussion of security topics; retrieve security-related system-related property; retain access to information formerly controlled by the individual; notify defined personnel within a defined time period.
nist_800_53.discussion: Automated mechanisms can facilitate timely notification and revocation upon termination.
assessment_objectives: Determine if information system access is disabled upon termination.
Determine if authenticators/credentials are terminated/revoked.
Determine if exit interviews including security topics are conducted.
Determine if security-related system-related property is retrieved.
Determine if access to information formerly controlled by the individual is retained by the organization.
Determine if defined personnel/roles are notified within a defined time period.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automated mechanisms to notify defined personnel/roles upon termination of an individual.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: When someone is terminated, an automated system (like an HR-to-IT integration) automatically notifies the relevant personnel (ISO, system administrators) rather than relying on someone remembering to send a manual email.

evidence_required.description: Automated termination notification workflow logs (HR system to IT/security team).

va_odp_values.value: At the same time (or just before) the employee is notified of dismissal, or upon receipt of resignation

controls.plain_english_explanation: When someone leaves the organization, their system access is cut off — timed carefully so access is disabled right at (or just before) the point they're informed of their termination, not left open afterward.

evidence_required.description: Account disablement timestamp/log tied to termination notification.
Documentation of exit interview including security topics discussed.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Termination triggers the 24-hour account disablement requirement in AC-2's VA overlay.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Review/confirm ongoing operational need for current access authorizations when individuals are reassigned/transferred; initiate transfer/reassignment actions promptly; modify access as needed; notify defined personnel within a defined time period.
nist_800_53.discussion: Actions may include reissuing keys/IDs/badges, closing old accounts, establishing new accounts, and changing system access authorizations.
assessment_objectives: Determine if access authorizations are reviewed/confirmed upon reassignment/transfer.
Determine if transfer actions are initiated promptly.
Determine if access is modified to correspond with the new role.
Determine if defined personnel are notified within a defined time period.

va_odp_values.value: As soon as possible, no later than 30 days after the transfer action

controls.plain_english_explanation: When someone changes jobs internally, their old access is reviewed and adjusted to match their new role (removing what they no longer need, adding what they now do) within 30 days.

evidence_required.description: Access modification records tied to internal transfer notification.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Transfer triggers access modification under account management.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop and document access agreements; review/update the agreements; ensure individuals requiring access sign appropriate agreements prior to being granted access and re-sign when agreements are updated or at a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Access agreements include nondisclosure agreements, acceptable use agreements, rules of behavior, and conflict-of-interest agreements.
assessment_objectives: Determine if access agreements are developed, documented, reviewed, and updated.
Determine if individuals sign appropriate access agreements prior to being granted access.
Determine if individuals re-sign when agreements are updated or at a defined frequency.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Access agreements include the VA National ROB (Appendix D) and the Contractor ROB (attached to VA Handbook 6500.6).

controls.plain_english_explanation: Anyone accessing VA systems must sign formal access agreements (like the Rules of Behavior) before getting access, and re-sign when those agreements are updated.

evidence_required.description: Signed access agreements (ROB, NDA, etc.) for each user.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Rules of Behavior is the primary access agreement referenced by both controls.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish personnel security requirements (including roles/responsibilities) for external providers; require compliance with organizational personnel security policies; document requirements; require notification of personnel transfers/terminations affecting credentialed individuals; monitor provider compliance.
nist_800_53.discussion: External providers include service bureaus, contractors, and other organizations providing IT services or outsourced applications.
assessment_objectives: Determine if personnel security requirements are established for external providers.
Determine if external providers are required to comply with organizational personnel security policies.
Determine if requirements are documented.
Determine if providers are required to notify the organization of personnel transfers/terminations.
Determine if provider compliance is monitored.

va_odp_values.value: Immediately, when a contractor is reassigned or leaves the contractor's/subcontractor's employ, or prior to an unfriendly termination

controls.plain_english_explanation: Contractors and other outside personnel must meet the same personnel security requirements as VA employees, and the contracting company must promptly notify VA if one of their credentialed people leaves or is reassigned.

evidence_required.description: Contract language requiring personnel security compliance and notification obligations.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Contractor personnel are subject to the same screening requirements.

AO approval of the categorization decision.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Security categorization results are documented within the SSP.

Determine if scanning information is shared to eliminate similar vulnerabilities in other systems.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ vulnerability scanning tools that include the capability to readily update the vulnerabilities to be scanned.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The vulnerability scanning tool can be quickly updated with new vulnerability definitions as they're discovered, rather than being stuck scanning only for older, known issues.

evidence_required.description: Vulnerability scanner configuration showing update mechanism for new vulnerability signatures.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Update by Frequency, Prior to New Scan, or When Identified

nist_800_53.control_statement: Update the system vulnerabilities scanned at a defined frequency, prior to a new scan, or when new vulnerabilities are identified/reported.

va_odp_values.value: Monthly and/or randomly per OI&T-approved process

evidence_required.description: Vulnerability scanner update logs showing monthly/random refresh cadence.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Determine what information about the system is discoverable by adversaries and take corrective actions.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, the organization actively checks what information about the system an attacker could discover from the outside (like software version banners or exposed metadata) and takes steps to hide or remove that information.

evidence_required.description: Discoverable information assessment (e.g., external reconnaissance test) and corrective action records.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement privileged access authorization to defined system components for selected vulnerability scanning activities.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Some vulnerability scans require elevated/privileged access to check deeper (like scanning inside a system rather than just from the network), and this privileged scanning access is specifically authorized rather than granted broadly.

evidence_required.description: Privileged access authorization records for vulnerability scanning accounts/tools.

va_odp_values.value: Critical: 30 days; High: 60 days; Moderate: 90 days; Low: Information System Owner determines; Emergent: as soon as possible

controls.plain_english_explanation: Systems are regularly scanned for known vulnerabilities, and any vulnerabilities found must be fixed within specific deadlines based on severity — critical vulnerabilities get patched within 30 days, while lower-severity ones have more time.

evidence_required.description: Vulnerability scan reports.
Patch/remediation tracking demonstrating compliance with VA's tiered SLA timelines.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Vulnerability findings are remediated via the flaw remediation (patch management) process.
Unresolved vulnerabilities become POA&M line items.
Penetration testing often builds directly on vulnerability scan findings.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Determine security requirements in mission/business process planning; determine/document/allocate resources for security as part of capital planning; establish a discrete line item for information security in budgeting documentation.
nist_800_53.discussion: Security is built into and funded as part of the system architecture, not treated as an afterthought.
assessment_objectives: Determine if security requirements are determined in mission/business planning.
Determine if resources for security are determined, documented, and allocated in capital planning.
Determine if a discrete line item for information security exists in budgeting documentation.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Consistent with NIST SP 800-65 and OMB Circular A-11/Memorandum M-00-07 requiring security to be built into and funded as part of system architecture.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Security costs are planned and budgeted for explicitly as part of the system's lifecycle — not squeezed in after the fact once money runs out.

evidence_required.description: Budget/capital planning documentation showing a discrete security line item.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System-level resource allocation feeds the organization-wide information security resources requirement.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Manage the system using a defined SDLC that incorporates information security considerations; define/document security roles/responsibilities throughout the SDLC; identify individuals with those roles; integrate the risk management process into SDLC activities.
nist_800_53.discussion: Performing security engineering activities throughout hardware/software/firmware development is an effective means of achieving system resiliency.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the system is managed using a defined SDLC incorporating security considerations.
Determine if security roles/responsibilities are defined and documented throughout the SDLC.
Determine if individuals with those roles are identified.
Determine if the risk management process is integrated into SDLC activities.

va_specific_requirements: Recovery/decryption capability for encrypted data must be demonstrated prior to ATO.

Locally-developed systems follow SDLC steps and are assessed/authorized prior to implementation.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Security must be baked into the system's development process from the start, not bolted on at the end. nist_800_53.control_statement: Include security functional/strength/assurance requirements, security-related documentation requirements, protection requirements for that documentation, a description of the development/operational environment, and acceptance criteria in acquisition contracts.
nist_800_53.discussion: Security requirements are expressed in terms of security controls/enhancements selected through the tailoring process.
assessment_objectives: Determine if security functional/strength/assurance requirements are included in acquisition contracts.
Determine if security-related documentation and protection requirements are included.
Determine if the development/operational environment description and acceptance criteria are included.

evidence_required.description: Vendor/developer-provided description of security control functional properties.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Design and Implementation Information for Security Controls

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require the developer to provide design/implementation information for security controls at a defined level of detail.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Early in development, the developer must specify exactly which network ports, protocols, and services the system will actually use — this lets VA plan firewall rules and least-functionality restrictions before the system is even built, rather than discovering this information after the fact.

evidence_required.description: Developer-provided list of functions/ports/protocols/services intended for use, documented early in the SDLC.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ only information technology products on the FIPS 201-approved products list for PIV capability.

evidence_required.description: Procurement documentation confirming PIV-related products are sourced from the FIPS 201-approved products list.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Additional contract security policy/procedures in VA Handbook 6500.6.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Contracts for buying or building systems must explicitly spell out security requirements — what security functions are needed, how strong they must be, what documentation the vendor must provide — rather than leaving security as an afterthought in the contract.

evidence_required.description: Acquisition contract language specifying security requirements.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Acquisition security requirements are integrated with SDLC security activities.

evidence_required.description: System administrator and user documentation.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System documentation supports the completeness of the SSP.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Systems are designed with established security engineering best practices from the start (layered defenses, sound architecture) rather than security being an afterthought bolted on later.

evidence_required.description: Design documentation referencing security engineering principles applied.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Security engineering principles inform the system's security architecture.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require that providers of external system services comply with organizational security requirements and employ defined security controls; define/document government oversight and user roles/responsibilities for external services; employ defined processes to monitor security control compliance by external providers.

Determine if defined processes are employed to monitor provider compliance.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require the developer to perform configuration management during system/component/service design, development, implementation, and/or operation; document and control the integrity of changes to defined configuration items; implement only approved changes; document changes and their potential security impacts; track security flaws and their resolution and report to authorized personnel.
nist_800_53.discussion: Maintaining integrity of changes requires configuration control throughout the SDLC to track authorized changes and prevent unauthorized changes.

Determine if changes to defined configuration items are documented, managed, and controlled.
Determine if only approved changes are implemented.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Developer-side change control mirrors the organization's own configuration change control process.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require the developer to create/implement a security assessment plan; perform unit/integration/system/regression testing at a defined depth and coverage; produce evidence of the execution of the plan and results; implement a verifiable flaw remediation process; correct flaws identified during testing.
nist_800_53.discussion: Developmental testing occurs at all post-design phases of the SDLC to confirm required security controls are correctly implemented.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the developer creates and implements a security assessment plan.
Determine if unit/integration/system/regression testing is performed at a defined depth/coverage.
Determine if evidence of test execution and results is produced.
Determine if a verifiable flaw remediation process is implemented and flaws corrected.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: De-identified test data should be used for systems that have not yet undergone security A&A; production data should not be used for testing.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Before a system is deployed, the developer must actually test it for security flaws (not just functionality) and fix what's found — and critically, live/production data (with real sensitive information) shouldn't be used for this testing before the system is authorized.

evidence_required.description: Developer security testing plan and results.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Developer testing results feed into the broader control assessment.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Supply chain protection requirements are incorporated into acquisition contract language.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Require the developer to follow a documented development process addressing security requirements, identify standards/tools used, document tool options/configurations, and manage integrity of changes to the process/tools; review the development process/standards/tools to determine if they can satisfy security requirements.

assessment_objectives: Determine if the developer produces a design specification and security/privacy architecture consistent with organizational architecture requirements.

controls.plain_english_explanation: For high-risk systems, the developer must produce a detailed design/architecture document showing how the system's security features work together and align with the organization's overall security architecture.

evidence_required.description: Developer security architecture and design specification.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Developer architecture must align with the organization's information security architecture.

Documented approval for continued use of any unsupported component.

controls.control_name: Separation of System and User Functionality

nist_800_53.control_statement: Separate user functionality, including user interface services, from system management functionality.
nist_800_53.discussion: System management functionality includes functions necessary to administer databases, network components, workstations, or servers, and typically requires privileged access.
assessment_objectives: Determine if user functionality is separated from system management functionality.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The parts of a system that regular users interact with are kept separate from the administrative functions used to manage the system, so a normal user can't accidentally (or intentionally) access admin-level controls.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Functional separation supports least privilege enforcement.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Isolate security functions from nonsecurity functions by means of an isolation boundary implemented via partitions and domains, including control of access to and integrity of the hardware/software/firmware performing those functions.

assessment_objectives: Determine if security functions are isolated from nonsecurity functions via an isolation boundary.

controls.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, the code that implements security functions is technically isolated from regular application code, so a bug or compromise in the regular application can't easily reach and tamper with security-critical functions.

evidence_required.description: System architecture documentation demonstrating security function isolation.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Process isolation is a general mechanism supporting security function isolation.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Prevent unauthorized and unintended information transfer via shared system resources.
nist_800_53.discussion: This control (sometimes called 'object reuse') prevents information produced by a prior user/process from being available to a subsequent user/process accessing a shared resource (e.g., memory, disk) after it has been released.
assessment_objectives: Determine if unauthorized/unintended information transfer via shared system resources is prevented.

controls.plain_english_explanation: When shared system resources (like memory or disk space) are reused by a new process, no leftover data from the previous user/process should be accessible to the new one.

evidence_required.description: OS/memory management configuration demonstrating resource clearing between uses.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Both controls address unauthorized information flow, though at different technical layers.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Protect against or limit the effects of defined types of denial-of-service events by employing defined security safeguards.
nist_800_53.discussion: Technologies such as boundary protection devices can filter certain packet types to protect internal components; increased capacity/bandwidth combined with service redundancy may also reduce susceptibility.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the system is protected against or limits effects of defined DoS event types using defined safeguards.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Through VA-NSOC; examples include boundary protection devices filtering certain packet types and increased capacity/bandwidth combined with service redundancy.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Systems have protections against denial-of-service attacks (attempts to overwhelm a system with traffic to take it offline), such as filtering malicious traffic and having redundant capacity.

evidence_required.description: DoS protection/mitigation configuration (e.g., firewall rules, traffic filtering).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Boundary protection devices are often the same mechanism used for DoS mitigation.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Protect the availability of resources by allocating resources by priority, quota, or defined security safeguards.
nist_800_53.discussion: Ensures critical processes are not starved of resources during periods of high demand or attack.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time; OI&T may elect to limit resource use by priority at their discretion.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would allocate system resources by priority/quota to ensure critical functions aren't starved during high demand.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Monitor and control communications at the external boundary and key internal boundaries of the system; implement subnetworks for publicly accessible components that are physically or logically separated from internal networks; connect to external networks only through managed interfaces with boundary protection devices arranged per organizational security architecture.
nist_800_53.discussion: Managed interfaces include gateways, routers, firewalls, and encrypted tunnels arranged in a security architecture (e.g., DMZs).
assessment_objectives: Determine if communications at the external boundary and key internal boundaries are monitored and controlled.
Determine if subnetworks for publicly accessible components are implemented, physically or logically separated from internal networks.
Determine if connections to external networks are made only through managed interfaces with boundary protection devices.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Limit the number of external network connections to the system.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping; VA references the Trusted Internet Connection (TIC) initiative.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The number of places where the network connects to the outside internet is deliberately kept small (funneled through VA's approved TIC gateways) — fewer entry points means fewer places to monitor and defend.

evidence_required.description: Network diagram showing the limited number of external connection points.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement a managed interface for each external telecommunications service; establish a traffic flow policy; protect confidentiality/integrity of transmitted information; document/review exceptions to the traffic flow policy.

va_odp_values.value: As required, per justified need

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Every external telecom connection has a specific traffic policy governing what's allowed to flow through it, and any exceptions to that policy are documented and reviewed rather than being an open-ended free-for-all.

evidence_required.description: Traffic flow policy configuration for external telecommunications interfaces, plus exception documentation.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Deny by Default, Allow by Exception

nist_800_53.control_statement: Deny network communications traffic by default at managed interfaces and allow traffic by exception.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Firewalls are configured to block all traffic by default, only allowing through the specific types of traffic that have been explicitly approved — this is the more secure 'default deny' approach rather than 'default allow.'

evidence_required.description: Firewall rule set demonstrating deny-by-default configuration.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Split Tunneling for Remote Devices — Prevent

nist_800_53.control_statement: Prevent split tunneling for remote devices connecting to organizational systems unless the split tunnel is securely provisioned.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: When a remote user is connected via VPN, their device can't simultaneously maintain an unsecured direct internet connection alongside the VPN tunnel — this prevents an attacker from using the unsecured connection as a bridge into the VPN-connected VA network.

evidence_required.description: VPN client configuration preventing split tunneling.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Route Traffic to Authenticated Proxy Servers

nist_800_53.control_statement: Route defined internal communications traffic to defined external networks through authenticated proxy servers within managed interfaces.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, internal traffic heading out to the internet is routed through an authenticated proxy server first, rather than connecting directly — giving VA visibility and control over that traffic.

evidence_required.description: Proxy server configuration/routing rules for internal-to-external traffic.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Fail securely in the event of an operational failure of a boundary protection device.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: If a firewall or other boundary protection device crashes or fails, it fails into a secure state (blocking traffic) rather than an insecure one (letting all traffic through) — a failure shouldn't accidentally open the network up.

evidence_required.description: Boundary protection device fail-secure configuration/testing documentation.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ boundary protection mechanisms to separate system components supporting different missions and/or business functions.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Example: the Medical Device Isolation Architecture (MDIA) for medical devices.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Different types of system components serving different purposes (like medical devices vs. general IT systems) are network-isolated from each other, so a compromise in one area (e.g., a general workstation) can't spread into a more sensitive area (e.g., medical devices) — VA's MDIA architecture is a real example of this.

evidence_required.description: Network segmentation diagram showing isolation between different mission/business function components (e.g., MDIA for medical devices).

controls.plain_english_explanation: The system's boundary with outside networks (like the internet) is tightly controlled through firewalls/gateways: only explicitly allowed traffic gets through (deny-by-default), the number of connection points to the outside is minimized, and internet-facing systems are isolated from internal systems.

evidence_required.description: Firewall/gateway configuration demonstrating deny-by-default, managed interfaces, and network segmentation.
Network architecture diagram showing boundary protection and DMZ/subnetwork placement.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Information flow enforcement is technically implemented through the same boundary protection devices.
Boundary protection devices are a common mechanism for DoS mitigation as well.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Protect the confidentiality and/or integrity of transmitted information.
nist_800_53.discussion: This control applies to both internal and external networks and all system components from which information can be transmitted.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the confidentiality and/or integrity of transmitted information is protected.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement cryptographic mechanisms to prevent unauthorized disclosure of and/or detect changes to information during transmission, unless otherwise protected by alternative physical safeguards.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Data sent over the network is encrypted so it can't be read if intercepted, and any tampering with the data in transit would be detectable — unless a physical protection (like a dedicated private line) is used instead of encryption.

evidence_required.description: Transmission encryption configuration (TLS/VPN) demonstrating confidentiality and integrity protection.

va_specific_requirements: Email containing VA sensitive information must be encrypted using VA-approved encryption; auto-forwarding to external addresses is prohibited.
Fax transmissions of individually identifiable information limited to situations with no reasonable alternative, sent to a secure/attended location, with required disclaimer language.
PBX/telephone systems must maintain audit trails and follow specific security hardening practices per VA guidance.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping; VA provides extensive detail on specific transmission channels (email, fax, PBX) not found in the generic NIST control text.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Information sent over a network (email, data transfers, etc.) must be protected from being read or altered in transit — VA gets very specific: sensitive email must be encrypted and can't auto-forward externally, and faxing sensitive information is only allowed when there's truly no other option.

evidence_required.description: Email encryption gateway configuration; TLS/transport encryption configuration.
Email/fax handling policy for sensitive information.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Cryptographic protection of transmitted data uses the same FIPS 140-2 requirement as general cryptographic protection.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Withdrawn; incorporated into SC-8.
nist_800_53.discussion: Requirements folded into SC-8 (Transmission Confidentiality and Integrity).

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Withdrawn control; not separately tracked by VA 6500.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Terminate the network connection associated with a communications session at the end of the session or after a defined period of inactivity.
nist_800_53.discussion: This applies to both internal and external networks; terminating a network connection includes de-allocating associated TCP/IP address/port pairs.
assessment_objectives: Determine if network connections are terminated at the end of a session or after a defined period of inactivity.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Network connections are actually closed (not just the user session locked) after a period of inactivity or when the session ends.

evidence_required.description: Network session timeout configuration.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Network disconnect and logical session termination are often configured together.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide a mechanism to establish a trusted communications path between the user and defined security functions of the system.
nist_800_53.discussion: A high-assurance mechanism to ensure users are actually communicating with legitimate system components (not spoofed interfaces).

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — a high-assurance mechanism ensuring the user is genuinely communicating with the real system, not a spoofed interface.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish and manage cryptographic keys when cryptography is employed within the system, in accordance with requirements for key generation, distribution, storage, access, and destruction.
nist_800_53.discussion: Key management can be performed using manual procedures or automated mechanisms with supporting manual procedures.
assessment_objectives: Determine if cryptographic keys are established and managed per key generation/distribution/storage/access/destruction requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Maintain availability of information in the event of the loss of cryptographic keys by users.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: If a user loses their encryption key, there's a backup mechanism (like a key escrow/recovery process) to still get access to the encrypted data — so encryption doesn't accidentally cause permanent data loss.

evidence_required.description: Cryptographic key recovery/escrow procedure for lost user keys.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA manages trust stores to ensure only approved trust anchors are included.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Encryption keys are properly generated, distributed, stored, and destroyed following a formal process — and there's a way to recover data if a user loses their key, so encryption doesn't accidentally cause permanent data loss.

evidence_required.description: Cryptographic key management procedures.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Key management supports the cryptographic protection mechanisms required under SC-13.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Determine the cryptographic uses and the types of cryptography required for each use; implement the required cryptography per applicable federal laws/policies/regulations/standards.
nist_800_53.discussion: Cryptography can be employed to support various security solutions including protection of classified/sensitive information and provision of digital signatures.
assessment_objectives: Determine if cryptographic uses are determined and required cryptography is implemented per applicable federal requirements.

va_specific_requirements: VA sensitive information must be encrypted during transmission and at rest when outside VA-owned or managed facilities.
All cryptographic modules used must be FIPS 140-2 (or successor) validated, operating in approved modes.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Any encryption used must be a FIPS 140-2 (federally validated) implementation — not just any encryption algorithm someone chooses. VA sensitive data specifically must be encrypted both in transit and at rest whenever it's outside VA's own facilities.

evidence_required.description: FIPS 140-2 validation certificate for encryption modules in use.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Encryption at rest requirements share the same FIPS 140-2 validation requirement.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Withdrawn; incorporated into AC-2, AC-3, AC-5, AC-6, SI-3, SI-4, SI-5, SI-7, SI-10.
nist_800_53.discussion: Requirements distributed across multiple existing AC and SI controls.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: One of several controls that absorbed this withdrawn control's requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Prohibit remote activation of collaborative computing devices/applications except for defined exceptions where remote activation is allowed; provide an explicit indication of use to users physically present at the devices.
nist_800_53.discussion: Collaborative computing devices/applications include networked whiteboards, cameras, and microphones.
assessment_objectives: Determine if remote activation of collaborative computing devices is prohibited except for defined exceptions.
Determine if an explicit indication of use is provided to users physically present.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Devices like conference room cameras and microphones can't be remotely turned on without the people in the room knowing — there must be a clear indicator when they're active.

evidence_required.description: Collaborative computing device configuration showing remote activation restrictions.

controls.control_name: Transmission of Security and Privacy Attributes

nist_800_53.control_statement: Associate defined security/privacy attributes with information exchanged between systems and system components.
nist_800_53.discussion: Enables attribute-based access control decisions to follow data as it moves between systems.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would attach security/privacy labels to data that travel with it between systems.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Issue public key certificates under an organization-defined certificate policy or obtain public key certificates from an approved service provider.
nist_800_53.discussion: For all certificates, organizations manage trust stores to ensure only approved trust anchors are included.
assessment_objectives: Determine if public key certificates are issued under a defined certificate policy or obtained from an approved service provider.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA purchases public key certificates from an approved, shared service provider.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Digital certificates (used for encryption/authentication) must come from an approved, trusted source, not just any certificate authority.

evidence_required.description: List of approved certificate providers/trust anchors.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Certificate management is part of the broader cryptographic key management process.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Define acceptable and unacceptable mobile code and mobile code technologies; establish usage restrictions and implementation guidance; authorize, monitor, and control the use of mobile code.
nist_800_53.discussion: Mobile code technologies include Java, JavaScript, ActiveX, PDF, Flash, and VBScript.
assessment_objectives: Determine if acceptable/unacceptable mobile code and technologies are defined.
Determine if usage restrictions/implementation guidance are established.
Determine if mobile code use is authorized, monitored, and controlled.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Per NIST SP 800-28, VA assesses the risk of harm from allowing mobile code (e.g., JavaScript) on its systems.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Web technologies that can execute code on a user's system (like JavaScript or Flash) are evaluated for risk, and the organization controls which of these are permitted and how they're monitored.

evidence_required.description: Mobile code usage policy identifying acceptable/prohibited technologies.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Malicious code protection often screens for malicious mobile code specifically.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish usage restrictions and implementation guidance for VoIP technologies based on the potential to cause damage if used maliciously; authorize, monitor, and control the use of VoIP.
nist_800_53.discussion: VoIP presents unique security considerations compared to traditional telephony.
assessment_objectives: Determine if usage restrictions/implementation guidance are established for VoIP.
Determine if VoIP use is authorized, monitored, and controlled.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA requires Information System Owners to implement protective measures consistent with NIST SP 800-58.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VoIP (voice-over-internet phone systems) usage is authorized, monitored, and controlled per federal security guidance since it introduces different risks than traditional phone lines.

evidence_required.description: VoIP system security configuration.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: VoIP traffic is subject to the same boundary protection controls as other network traffic.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide additional data origin authentication and integrity verification artifacts along with the authoritative name resolution data the system returns in response to external name/address resolution queries; provide the means to indicate the security status of child zones when operating as part of a distributed, hierarchical namespace.
nist_800_53.discussion: Enables external clients to obtain origin authentication and integrity assurances for host/service name to network address resolution information (e.g., DNSSEC).
assessment_objectives: Determine if additional authentication/integrity artifacts are provided with authoritative name resolution data.
Determine if the security status of child zones can be indicated.

controls.plain_english_explanation: When the organization's DNS servers answer requests about its own domain names, they provide cryptographic proof (like DNSSEC signatures) that the answer is authentic and hasn't been tampered with.

evidence_required.description: DNSSEC configuration for authoritative DNS servers.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Complementary control addressing the client/resolver side of secure name resolution.

controls.control_name: Secure Name/Address Resolution Service (Recursive or Caching Resolver)

nist_800_53.control_statement: Request and perform data origin authentication and data integrity verification on the name/address resolution responses the system receives from authoritative sources.
nist_800_53.discussion: Each client of name resolution services either performs this validation itself or has an authenticated channel to a trusted validation provider.
assessment_objectives: Determine if data origin authentication and integrity verification are requested/performed on name/address resolution responses.

controls.plain_english_explanation: When the organization's systems look up domain names (e.g., resolving a website address), they verify that the response is cryptographically authentic and hasn't been spoofed.

evidence_required.description: DNS resolver configuration validating DNSSEC signatures.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Complementary control addressing the authoritative-source side of secure name resolution.

controls.control_name: Architecture and Provisioning for Name/Address Resolution Service

nist_800_53.control_statement: Ensure the systems that collectively provide name/address resolution service for the organization are fault-tolerant and implement internal/external role separation.
nist_800_53.discussion: To eliminate single points of failure, organizations typically employ at least two authoritative DNS servers, geographically separated.
assessment_objectives: Determine if name/address resolution services are fault-tolerant.
Determine if internal/external role separation is implemented.

controls.plain_english_explanation: DNS services are designed with redundancy (multiple servers, geographically separated) so a single failure doesn't take down name resolution, and internal DNS queries are kept separate from external ones.

evidence_required.description: DNS architecture diagram showing redundancy and internal/external separation.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Part of the broader secure DNS architecture.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Protect the authenticity of communications sessions.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses communications protection at the session level and establishes grounds for confidence in the identity of parties and validity of transmitted information (e.g., protecting against session hijacking).
assessment_objectives: Determine if the authenticity of communications sessions is protected.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Failure state preservation supports subsequent system recovery/reconstitution.
