nist_800_53.discussion: A physical hardening measure to eliminate unneeded hardware attack surfaces (e.g., disabling unused USB ports).

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time; note some VA guidance elsewhere addresses USB port restriction via technical controls (see MP-7) rather than physical removal.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected as a distinct baseline control in VA 6500, though conceptually related to VA's MP-7 USB restriction guidance.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not formally required by VA as a distinct control — though VA achieves a similar outcome for USB ports through technical blocking controls under Media Use (MP-7) rather than physically removing hardware ports.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: VA's technical USB restriction approach achieves a similar goal to this control.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Prohibit the remote activation of environmental sensing capabilities except for defined exceptions; provide an explicit indication of sensor use to a defined class of users.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses privacy/security concerns around device sensors like cameras, microphones, and GPS.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would restrict remote activation of device sensors (cameras, microphones, GPS) and require clear indication when they're active.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish usage restrictions and implementation guidance for defined system components based on the potential to cause damage if used maliciously; authorize, monitor, and control the use of such components.
nist_800_53.discussion: A general-purpose control for restricting use of specific higher-risk component types not otherwise covered.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this is a general-purpose control for restricting use of higher-risk component types not otherwise addressed elsewhere.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ a detonation chamber capability within the system, system component, or designated location.
nist_800_53.discussion: Refers to sandboxed environments used to safely execute and analyze suspicious files/code (malware sandboxing).

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would use sandboxed environments ('detonation chambers') to safely analyze suspicious files before they reach production systems.

control_families.family_description: Governs flaw remediation, malicious code protection, system monitoring, security alerts, software/firmware/information integrity, and related information handling controls.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate a system and information integrity policy and procedures; review/update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for system/information integrity.
assessment_objectives: Determine if system and information integrity policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written system and information integrity policy, reviewed periodically.

evidence_required.description: System and information integrity policy document.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same policy documentation pattern.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify, report, and correct system flaws; test software/firmware updates for effectiveness/side effects before installation; install security-relevant updates within a defined time period of release; incorporate flaw remediation into configuration management.
nist_800_53.discussion: Security-relevant updates include patches, service packs, hotfixes, and anti-virus signatures.
assessment_objectives: Determine if system flaws are identified, reported, and corrected.
Determine if software/firmware updates are tested for effectiveness/side effects prior to installation.
Determine if security-relevant updates are installed within a defined time period of release.
Determine if flaw remediation is incorporated into the configuration management process.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automated mechanisms to determine the state of system components with regard to flaw remediation.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The organization uses automated tools to quickly check which systems are missing patches, rather than manually auditing patch status system by system.

evidence_required.description: Patch management dashboard/report showing automated patch compliance status across systems.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA operates a Patch and Vulnerability Management Program managed by the PVT (Patch and Vulnerability Team) under a charter approved by OI&T management, consistent with NIST SP 800-40. Patches are prioritized by severity, tested centrally before deployment, and applied in a phased approach starting with standard system builds.
va_specific_requirements: Remediation timelines align with RA-5's SLA tiers (Critical: 30 days; High: 60 days; Moderate: 90 days; Emergent: ASAP).
Patches tested on non-production systems prior to deployment.
Phased rollout: standard builds first, then non-standard/one-off builds, then legacy/antiquated platforms.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Software vulnerabilities and bugs must be identified, tracked, and fixed (patched) within defined timeframes based on severity — patches are tested first on non-production systems before being rolled out broadly.

evidence_required.description: Patch management system reports showing deployment status and timelines.
Patch testing records prior to production deployment.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Vulnerability scan findings drive the flaw remediation/patching process, sharing the same SLA timelines.
Patch deployment flows through the same change control process.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ malicious code protection mechanisms at system entry/exit points to detect and eradicate malicious code; update protection mechanisms when new releases are available; configure mechanisms to perform periodic scans and real-time scans of files as they are downloaded/opened/executed; address the receipt of false positives.
nist_800_53.discussion: Malicious code includes viruses, worms, Trojan horses, and spyware, and can be transported via web access, email, or portable storage devices.
assessment_objectives: Determine if malicious code protection mechanisms are employed at system entry/exit points.
Determine if protection mechanisms are updated when new releases are available.
Determine if mechanisms perform periodic and real-time scans, and take defined action upon detection.
Determine if the potential impact of false positives on system availability is addressed.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Centrally manage malicious code protection mechanisms.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Antivirus/anti-malware software across all endpoints is managed from a central console, so policy updates and signature pushes happen consistently across the whole organization rather than being configured separately on each machine.

evidence_required.description: Centralized antivirus/EDR management console configuration.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Automatically update malicious code protection mechanisms (including signature definitions).

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Antivirus signature definitions update automatically without requiring manual intervention, so protection stays current against newly discovered malware.

evidence_required.description: Antivirus signature update logs showing automatic update frequency.

va_odp_values.value: Daily basis with daily virus definition updates

controls.plain_english_explanation: Antivirus/anti-malware protection runs at network entry/exit points and on endpoints, scanning files in real-time as they're downloaded or opened, with virus definitions updated daily.

evidence_required.description: Antivirus/EDR console showing deployment coverage and signature update status.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Malicious code detections are a key input to broader system monitoring.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Monitor the system to detect attacks/indicators of potential attacks and unauthorized connections; identify unauthorized use of the system; deploy monitoring devices strategically; protect monitoring information from unauthorized access/modification/deletion; heighten monitoring during periods of increased risk; provide monitoring information to defined personnel.
nist_800_53.discussion: Monitoring includes both external monitoring (at system boundaries) and internal monitoring (within the system). Output feeds continuous monitoring and incident response programs.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the system is monitored to detect attacks and unauthorized connections.
Determine if unauthorized use of the system is identified.
Determine if monitoring devices are deployed strategically.
Determine if monitoring information is provided to defined personnel/roles.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automated tools to support near real-time analysis of events.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Security events are analyzed by automated tools (like a SIEM) close to real-time, rather than someone manually reviewing logs hours or days after something happened.

evidence_required.description: SIEM/real-time monitoring tool configuration and sample near-real-time alert.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Monitor inbound and outbound communications traffic for unusual/unauthorized activities or conditions.

va_odp_values.value: Daily; inspects/monitors all packets inbound and outbound

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Network traffic coming into and going out of the system is inspected daily for anything unusual — like unexpected data leaving the network, which could indicate exfiltration.

evidence_required.description: Network traffic monitoring logs/alerts for inbound/outbound anomalies.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Alert defined personnel when indications of compromise or potential compromise occur.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: When monitoring tools detect signs that the system may be compromised, an automatic alert is sent to the appropriate security personnel, rather than relying on someone happening to notice it during a manual log review.

evidence_required.description: Sample system-generated compromise-indicator alert and notification record.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The system is actively and continuously monitored for signs of attack, misuse, or unauthorized activity — network traffic in both directions is inspected daily, with automated alerts sent to appropriate personnel when something suspicious is found.

evidence_required.description: SIEM/IDS-IPS logs and alert history.
Monitoring device placement diagram (strategic sensor locations).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System monitoring and audit log review are closely related and often share SIEM tooling.
Monitoring alerts trigger the incident handling process.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Receive system security alerts/advisories/directives from defined external organizations on an ongoing basis; generate internal alerts as needed; disseminate alerts/advisories/directives to defined personnel/elements/external organizations; implement security directives per established timeframes or notify the issuing organization of noncompliance.
nist_800_53.discussion: Security alerts and advisories are generated by US-CERT to maintain situational awareness across the federal government.
assessment_objectives: Determine if security alerts/advisories/directives are received from defined external organizations.
Determine if alerts/advisories/directives are disseminated to defined personnel/elements/organizations.
Determine if security directives are implemented per established timeframes or noncompliance is reported.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automated mechanisms to make security alert/advisory information available throughout the organization.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, threat advisories (like a US-CERT bulletin) are distributed to relevant personnel throughout the organization via automated tools, rather than manual email forwards that could get missed or delayed.

evidence_required.description: Automated alert distribution tool configuration and sample disseminated advisory.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Sources include US-CERT (Einstein sensor alerting), other government agencies, and open-source research.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization receives threat intelligence and security advisories from external sources like US-CERT and distributes relevant information internally, and must comply with mandatory federal security directives within set timeframes.

evidence_required.description: Record of security alerts/advisories received and disseminated.
Documentation of security directive implementation or noncompliance notification.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Security alerts often drive urgent patching/flaw remediation actions.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Verify the correct operation of defined security/privacy functions; perform verification at defined transitional states or upon command; alert defined personnel of failed verification tests; take defined action when anomalies are discovered.
nist_800_53.discussion: Ensures security controls are actually functioning as intended over time, not just at initial configuration.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time as a formal baseline allocation; conceptually addressed via continuous monitoring under CA-7.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not separately allocated in VA 6500; overlaps conceptually with VA's continuous monitoring program (CA-7).

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not formally required by VA as a distinct control — though VA's broader continuous monitoring program (CA-7) achieves a similar goal of verifying security functions continue operating correctly over time.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Continuous monitoring achieves a similar verification purpose.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ integrity verification tools to detect unauthorized changes to defined software, firmware, and information.
nist_800_53.discussion: Unauthorized changes can occur due to errors or malicious activity (tampering); integrity-checking mechanisms include parity checks, cryptographic hashes, and cyclical redundancy checks.
assessment_objectives: Determine if integrity verification tools are employed to detect unauthorized changes to defined software, firmware, and information.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Perform an integrity check of software/firmware/information at startup, at defined transitional states/security-relevant events, and/or at a defined frequency.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Every time the system starts up (and at other key moments), it checks that its software/firmware/critical data hasn't been tampered with, using techniques like checksums or digital signatures.

evidence_required.description: Startup/periodic integrity check logs.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ automated tools to notify defined personnel upon discovering discrepancies during integrity verification.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: If an integrity check finds that something has been tampered with, an automated alert immediately notifies security personnel — the discovery isn't dependent on someone manually reviewing check results later.

evidence_required.description: Sample automated integrity violation alert/notification record.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Automatically shut down the system, restart the system, and/or implement defined security safeguards when integrity violations are discovered.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: For the highest-risk systems, discovering a serious integrity violation can trigger an automatic protective response (like shutting down or restarting the affected component) without waiting for a person to decide and act.

evidence_required.description: Automated response configuration triggered by integrity violation detection.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Incorporate detection of unauthorized security-relevant changes into the incident response capability.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Detecting an unauthorized change to a critical system file isn't just logged and forgotten — it automatically feeds into the organization's incident response process, so it gets investigated as a potential security incident.

evidence_required.description: Incident response procedure showing integration with integrity violation detection.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Prohibit the use of binary or machine-executable code from sources with limited/no warranty without provision of source code, except for compelling mission/operational needs approved by the AO.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: The organization generally won't run compiled software from untrusted or unwarrantied sources without also having the source code available for review — an exception requires the Authorizing Official's specific sign-off for a compelling operational reason.

evidence_required.description: AO-approved exception documentation for any binary-only software from limited-warranty sources.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization uses tools (hash checks, digital signatures) to detect unauthorized tampering with software, firmware, or critical data — for high-risk systems, this happens automatically at startup and on a regular schedule, with automated alerts (and sometimes automatic shutdown) if tampering is detected.

evidence_required.description: File integrity monitoring (FIM) tool configuration and alert logs.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Integrity violation detection is integrated with the broader system monitoring capability.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ spam protection mechanisms at system entry/exit points to detect and act on unsolicited messages; update spam protection mechanisms when new releases are available.
nist_800_53.discussion: Spam can be transported via email, email attachments, and web access.
assessment_objectives: Determine if spam protection mechanisms are employed at entry/exit points.
Determine if spam protection mechanisms are updated when new releases are available.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Centrally manage spam protection mechanisms.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Spam filtering across the organization's email systems is managed from a central console, ensuring consistent rules and updates rather than each mail server having its own separate spam configuration.

evidence_required.description: Centralized spam filtering management console configuration.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Automatically update spam protection mechanisms.

control_enhancements.plain_english_explanation: Spam filtering rules and definitions update automatically, so the filter stays effective against new spam patterns without requiring manual intervention.

evidence_required.description: Spam filter update logs showing automatic update frequency.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Email/web gateways filter out spam automatically, and the spam-filtering rules are kept updated.

evidence_required.description: Email security gateway spam filtering configuration/logs.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Spam and malicious code protection are often part of the same email security gateway.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Withdrawn; incorporated into AC-2, AC-3, AC-5, AC-6.
nist_800_53.discussion: Requirements distributed across Access Control controls governing input restrictions.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Withdrawn control; VA 6500 explicitly notes this as incorporated into AC-2, AC-3, AC-5, AC-6.

controls.plain_english_explanation: This control no longer exists on its own — its requirements are now covered under several Access Control controls (AC-2, AC-3, AC-5, AC-6).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: One of several controls that absorbed this withdrawn control's requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Check the validity of defined information inputs.
nist_800_53.discussion: Rules for checking valid syntax/semantics of inputs (character set, length, range, acceptable values) help prevent attacks like SQL injection and cross-site scripting.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the validity of defined information inputs is checked.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Applications check that data entered by users (or from other systems) actually matches expected formats and values, which helps prevent attacks like SQL injection where malicious input is disguised as normal data.

evidence_required.description: Input validation rules/design documentation for the application.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Input validation and error handling work together to securely process unexpected input.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Generate error messages that provide information necessary for corrective action without revealing information that could be exploited by adversaries; reveal error messages only to defined personnel/roles.
nist_800_53.discussion: The structure and content of error messages should be carefully considered to avoid disclosing sensitive system details.
assessment_objectives: Determine if error messages provide necessary corrective information without revealing exploitable details.
Determine if error messages are revealed only to defined personnel/roles.

controls.plain_english_explanation: When an application encounters an error, the message shown to end users doesn't reveal technical details (like database structure or stack traces) that an attacker could exploit — detailed error information goes only to authorized technical staff.

evidence_required.description: Error handling design documentation showing sanitized user-facing error messages.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Error handling and input validation are complementary application security controls.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Manage and retain information within the system and information output from the system in accordance with applicable laws, executive orders, directives, regulations, policies, standards, and operational requirements.
nist_800_53.discussion: Information handling/retention requirements cover the full life cycle of information, in some cases extending beyond system disposal. NARA provides guidance on records retention.
assessment_objectives: Determine if information within the system and information output is managed and retained per applicable laws/regulations/policies/standards and operational requirements.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Data (both what's stored in the system and what's output/printed from it) must be handled and retained according to applicable legal/regulatory retention requirements — not deleted early, and not kept indefinitely beyond what's required either.

evidence_required.description: Records retention schedule applicable to the system's information.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Audit record retention is a specific application of the broader information retention requirement.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Determine mean time to failure for defined system components in specific environments of operation; provide substitute components and a means to exchange active/standby components at a defined mean time failure substitution criteria.
nist_800_53.discussion: Proactively swaps out components before they fail based on statistical failure predictions.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would proactively replace hardware components before they're statistically likely to fail.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement non-persistent defined system components and services that are initiated in a known state and terminated upon end of session or periodically at a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Limits the duration a compromised component remains active by refreshing it to a known-good state regularly.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would regularly refresh certain system components back to a known-good state to limit how long a compromise could persist.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Validate information output from defined software programs/applications to ensure the information is consistent with the expected content.
nist_800_53.discussion: Prevents data exfiltration or unintended information disclosure through malformed or unexpected output.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would validate application output to ensure it matches expected content, helping prevent unintended data leakage.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement defined security safeguards to protect system memory from unauthorized code execution.
nist_800_53.discussion: Security safeguards include data execution prevention and address space layout randomization, which can be hardware- or software-enforced.
assessment_objectives: Determine if defined security safeguards are implemented to protect system memory from unauthorized code execution.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Systems use technical safeguards (like data execution prevention) to stop malicious code from executing out of memory regions where it shouldn't be able to run — a common technique used in exploiting software vulnerabilities.

evidence_required.description: OS-level memory protection (DEP/ASLR) configuration.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Process isolation and memory protection are complementary system hardening controls.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement fail-safe procedures when defined failure conditions occur.
nist_800_53.discussion: Ensures the system defaults to a safe operational state under specified failure conditions, distinct from the more general SC-24 (Fail in Known State).

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in any VA baseline.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA — this would implement fail-safe procedures under specific defined failure conditions, distinct from the more general 'fail in known state' requirement (SC-24).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Related concept of failing to a known/safe state under failure conditions.

control_families.family_description: Governs organization-wide (not system-specific) security program management activities: the information security program plan, resource allocation, risk management strategy, enterprise architecture integration, and related department-level functions.

baselines: Program-level (applies organization-wide, not tied to individual system impact levels)
nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop and disseminate an organization-wide information security program plan; review the plan on a defined frequency; update the plan to address organizational changes/problems; protect the plan from unauthorized disclosure/modification.
nist_800_53.discussion: The security program plan provides an overview of security program requirements and describes program management controls and common controls in place or planned.
assessment_objectives: Determine if an organization-wide information security program plan is developed and disseminated.
Determine if the plan is reviewed and updated per organizational changes/problems.
Determine if the plan is protected from unauthorized disclosure/modification.

va_odp_values.value: Every 5 years per VA Directive/Handbook 6330

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA Directive and Handbook 6500, along with the other 6500-series handbooks, fulfill this control's requirement at the department level.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping; deployed VA-wide as a common control, not tied to individual system baselines.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA has a single, department-wide information security program plan (VA Handbook 6500 and the related 6500-series handbooks) that applies to the whole organization, not something each individual system needs to write separately.

evidence_required.description: VA Handbook 6500 and related 6500-series handbooks.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System-level policies reference and implement this overarching program plan.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Appoint a senior official with the mission and resources to coordinate, develop, implement, and maintain an organization-wide information security program.
nist_800_53.discussion: This role is commonly referred to as the Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) or Senior Agency Information Security Officer.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a senior official is appointed with the mission and resources to lead the information security program.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: The VA CIO has appointed a CISO with the mission and resources to coordinate, develop, implement, and maintain a VA-wide information security program.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA has a designated Chief Information Security Officer (CISO) responsible for leading the department's overall security program.

evidence_required.description: CISO appointment/designation record.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Ensure that all capital planning and investment requests include the resources needed to implement the information security/privacy program and document all exceptions; employ a business case to record resources required; ensure resources are available for expenditure as planned.
nist_800_53.discussion: Ensures security is funded as part of capital planning rather than treated as an unfunded mandate.
assessment_objectives: Determine if capital planning/investment requests include information security/privacy program resources.
Determine if a business case records the resources required.
Determine if resources are available for expenditure as planned.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA ensures its capital planning and budget requests explicitly include the funding needed to run its security program, rather than treating security as an afterthought.

evidence_required.description: Capital planning/budget documentation showing security program funding.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System-level resource allocation feeds this department-wide resource requirement.

controls.control_name: Plan of Action and Milestones Process

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement a process to ensure POA&Ms for the security/privacy program and associated systems are maintained and document remedial actions to reduce/eliminate known vulnerabilities; report POA&M status per OMB FISMA reporting requirements; review POA&Ms for consistency with the organizational risk management strategy.
nist_800_53.discussion: Provides department-wide oversight of the POA&M process defined at the system level under CA-5.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a POA&M process for the program and associated systems is implemented.
Determine if POA&M status is reported per FISMA requirements.
Determine if POA&Ms are reviewed for consistency with organizational risk management strategy.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: OI&T has implemented a standardized process for POA&M development/maintenance/reporting, tracked within the VA-approved FISMA database.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA has a standardized, department-wide process for tracking and reporting on security weaknesses (POA&Ms) across all its systems, feeding into federal FISMA reporting requirements.

evidence_required.description: VA-approved FISMA database POA&M tracking records.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System-level POA&Ms roll up into this department-wide process.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop and update an inventory of organizational systems.
nist_800_53.discussion: Provides an organization-wide inventory feeding from and complementing the system-level component inventory under CM-8.
assessment_objectives: Determine if an inventory of organizational systems is developed and updated.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: OI&T develops and maintains an inventory of its information systems, complying with OMB/FISMA guidance and including physical/logical location, ownership, tracking number, OS type/version, serial number, and model number.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA maintains a department-wide inventory of all its information systems (not just individual components within one system), tracked centrally.

evidence_required.description: VA-wide system inventory export.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System-level component inventories feed into this department-wide system inventory.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, monitor, and report on the results of information security and privacy measures of performance.
nist_800_53.discussion: Outcome-based performance metrics help demonstrate the effectiveness of the security program and guide improvement efforts.
assessment_objectives: Determine if information security/privacy measures of performance are developed, monitored, and reported.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: OI&T develops, monitors, and reports on outcome-based performance metrics, tracking performance and providing feedback to the field to improve performance.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA tracks specific metrics to measure how well its security program is actually performing, not just whether policies exist on paper.

evidence_required.description: Security program performance metrics/dashboards.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop and maintain an enterprise architecture with consideration for information security/privacy and the resulting risk to organizational operations/assets/individuals.
nist_800_53.discussion: Aligns organizational EA with the Federal EA design and integrates security requirements early in the SDLC.
assessment_objectives: Determine if an enterprise architecture incorporating security/privacy considerations is developed and maintained.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: OI&T aligns VA's EA with Federal EA design, integrates architectural design with security requirements early in the SDLC, and follows the Federal Segment Architecture Methodology.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA maintains a department-wide enterprise architecture that explicitly incorporates security requirements from the earliest design stages, aligned with federal enterprise architecture standards.

evidence_required.description: Enterprise architecture documentation.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System-level security architecture must align with this department-wide enterprise architecture.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Address information security/privacy issues in the development, documentation, and updating of a critical infrastructure and key resources protection plan.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses the organization's role in protecting critical infrastructure, including defining critical infrastructure, key resources, and key personnel.
assessment_objectives: Determine if information security/privacy issues are addressed in the critical infrastructure protection plan.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: OI&T defines critical infrastructure for VA information systems, key critical infrastructure resources, and key critical infrastructure personnel.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA maintains a department-wide plan identifying its critical infrastructure and key resources, with security considerations built in.

evidence_required.description: Critical infrastructure and key resources protection plan.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System-level contingency planning considers criticality identified at the program level.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop a comprehensive strategy to manage risk to organizational operations/assets/individuals/other organizations/the Nation; implement the strategy consistently across the organization; review and update the strategy to address organizational changes.
nist_800_53.discussion: The risk management strategy is a foundational document guiding risk-based decisions across the three-tier risk management hierarchy (organization, mission/business process, system).
assessment_objectives: Determine if a comprehensive risk management strategy is developed.
Determine if the strategy is implemented consistently across the organization.
Determine if the strategy is reviewed and updated to address organizational changes.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA OI&T has a comprehensive strategy to manage risk associated with the operation/use of information systems, implemented consistently across the organization.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA has an overarching, department-wide strategy for how it identifies and manages risk, applied consistently across all its systems and operations.

evidence_required.description: Department-wide risk management strategy.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System-level risk assessments implement this overarching strategy.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Manage (document, track, and report) the security/privacy state of organizational systems and the environments in which they operate through authorization processes; designate individuals to fulfill specific roles/responsibilities within the risk management process; fully integrate the authorization processes into an organization-wide risk management program.
nist_800_53.discussion: Ensures a consistent, department-wide approach to system authorization rather than ad hoc, inconsistent processes.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the security/privacy state of systems is managed through authorization processes.
Determine if individuals are designated to fulfill risk management roles/responsibilities.
Determine if authorization processes are integrated into the organization-wide risk management program.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: OI&T has developed a security authorization process to manage/control VA's information system security posture, detailed further in VA Handbook 6500.3.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA has a consistent, documented, department-wide process for authorizing systems to operate, rather than each system inventing its own approach.

evidence_required.description: VA Handbook 6500.3 authorization process documentation.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: System-level authorization decisions follow this department-wide process.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Define organizational mission/business processes with consideration for information security/privacy and the resulting risk; determine information protection/data privacy needs arising from the defined processes; revise the processes as necessary until achievable protection/privacy needs are obtained.
nist_800_53.discussion: Ensures security is considered as part of how the organization defines its core mission/business functions, not layered on afterward.
assessment_objectives: Determine if mission/business processes are defined with consideration for security/privacy risk.
Determine if information protection/privacy needs arising from those processes are determined.
Determine if processes are revised to achieve protection needs.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: OI&T continually defines VA mission/business processes with consideration for information security, working closely with VHA, VBA, and NCA to determine their security requirements/needs.

controls.plain_english_explanation: When VA defines how its core business processes work (across VHA, VBA, NCA, etc.), security and privacy considerations are built into that definition from the start.

evidence_required.description: Mission/business process documentation reflecting security/privacy considerations.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement an insider threat program that includes a cross-discipline insider threat incident handling team.
nist_800_53.discussion: Combines technical and non-technical information (e.g., HR records) to detect malicious insider activity, since insider crimes are often preceded by nontechnical behavioral indicators.
assessment_objectives: Determine if an insider threat program including a cross-discipline incident handling team is implemented.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA OI&T has an insider threat program including a cross-discipline insider threat incident handling team with representation from major departments, meeting regularly. Includes correlation of technical and nontechnical information (e.g., HR records) since insider crimes are often preceded by nontechnical behavioral indicators.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA has a dedicated, cross-functional team (combining IT security, HR, and other departments) specifically focused on detecting and responding to insider threats — recognizing that warning signs often show up in behavior/HR records before they show up in system logs.

evidence_required.description: Insider threat program charter and team composition.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Insider threat detection relies on audit log analysis as one data source.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish a security and privacy workforce development and improvement program.
nist_800_53.discussion: Includes defining knowledge/skill levels needed for security duties, developing role-based training, and establishing career paths for security professionals.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a security/privacy workforce development and improvement program is established.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA OI&T has an information security workforce development/improvement program defining knowledge/skill levels, developing role-based training programs, and establishing career paths for security professionals.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA invests in developing its security workforce — defining what skills security roles need, providing role-based training, and creating career paths for security professionals to grow within the organization.

evidence_required.description: Security workforce development program documentation.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Role-based training under AT-3 is a component of this broader workforce development program.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement a process for ensuring that organizational plans for conducting security/privacy testing, training, and monitoring activities associated with organizational systems are developed/maintained and continue to be executed in a timely manner; review testing/training/monitoring plans for consistency with the risk management strategy.
nist_800_53.discussion: Coordinates and consolidates testing/monitoring activities routinely conducted across systems, since continuous monitoring and common controls are widespread.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a process ensuring testing/training/monitoring plans are developed, maintained, and executed is implemented.
Determine if plans are reviewed for consistency with the risk management strategy.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA coordinates its security testing, training, and monitoring activities across the organization at a program level, rather than leaving each system to plan these activities in isolation.

evidence_required.description: Department-wide testing/training/monitoring coordination process.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Program-level coordination supports system-level continuous monitoring.

controls.control_name: Security and Privacy Groups and Associations

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish and institutionalize contact with selected groups and associations within the security/privacy community to facilitate ongoing education/training, maintain currency with recommended practices/techniques/technologies, and share current security-related information.
nist_800_53.discussion: Ongoing contact with security groups is important in an environment of rapidly changing technologies and threats.
assessment_objectives: Determine if contact with security/privacy groups and associations is established and institutionalized.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Clean mapping; this absorbed the withdrawn AT-5 control.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA maintains formal relationships with external security/privacy professional groups and associations to stay current with emerging threats and best practices.

evidence_required.description: Record of professional group/association memberships and participation.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: This control absorbed the withdrawn AT-5 requirements.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement a threat awareness program that includes a cross-organization information-sharing capability.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses the constantly changing and increasingly sophisticated adversary landscape, including the advanced persistent threat, through threat information sharing.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a threat awareness program including cross-organization information sharing is implemented.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA OI&T has a threat awareness program including a cross-VA information-sharing capability, addressing the increasing sophistication of adversaries including advanced persistent threats.

controls.plain_english_explanation: VA has a formal program for staying aware of current threats and sharing that threat intelligence across the organization.

evidence_required.description: Threat awareness program documentation.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Threat awareness feeds into the security alerts/advisories process.

control_families.family_description: Governs authority to collect PII, purpose specification, consent, privacy notice, and related transparency/processing requirements. This Rev 5 family did not exist under Rev 4; VA Handbook 6500 Appendix E's separate eight-family privacy overlay (AP, AR, DI, DM, IP, SE, TR, UL) predates and does not structurally align with it. Appendix E controls are attached below as cross-references to their closest conceptual Rev 5 match, not merged as equivalents.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate a PII processing and transparency policy and procedures; review/update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for PII processing/transparency.
assessment_objectives: Determine if PII processing and transparency policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: VA 6500 predates the Rev 5 PT family; there is no direct Appendix F allocation for this control. The closest conceptual match is the Appendix E privacy program governance requirements under AR-1 (Governance and Privacy Program), cross-referenced below.

va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_family: Accountability, Audit, and Risk Management (VA Handbook 6500, Appendix E)
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.relationship_description: VA's AR-1 requires appointing a SAOP/CPO and developing/disseminating operational privacy policies and procedures — the closest Rev 4-era equivalent to the policy/procedure structure required by Rev 5 PT-1.
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_control_statement: VA will appoint a SAOP/CPO accountable for developing, implementing, and maintaining a VA-wide governance and privacy program; monitor federal privacy laws/policy; allocate sufficient budget/staffing; develop a strategic VA privacy plan; develop/disseminate/implement operational privacy policies and procedures.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written policy governing how it handles personally identifiable information (PII) throughout its lifecycle, reviewed periodically. VA's older Appendix E framework covers similar ground through its privacy governance program requirements (AR-1) rather than a distinct PT-family policy control.

evidence_required.description: PII processing and transparency policy (or VA's equivalent privacy program policy under AR-1).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same general policy documentation pattern.

controls.control_name: Authority to Process Personally Identifiable Information

nist_800_53.control_statement: Determine and document the authority permitting the collection, use, maintenance, and sharing of PII, either generally or in support of a specific program/system need; restrict PII processing to only that which is authorized.
nist_800_53.discussion: Before collecting PII, organizations determine whether the contemplated collection is legally authorized.
assessment_objectives: Determine if the authority permitting collection/use/maintenance/sharing of PII is determined and documented.
Determine if PII processing is restricted to only that which is authorized.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: No direct VA 6500 Appendix F allocation; VA's parallel requirement is documented in Appendix E's AP-1.

va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_family: Authority and Purpose (VA Handbook 6500, Appendix E)
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.relationship_description: VA's AP-1 requires determining legal authority before PII collection — the closest Rev 4-era VA equivalent to Rev 5 PT-2's authority-to-process requirement.
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_control_statement: VA will determine the legal authority that permits the collection, use, maintenance, and sharing of PII, either generally or in support of a specific program or information system need. The authority to collect PII is documented in the SORN, Privacy Act Statement, and PIAs.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Before collecting personal information, the organization must confirm and document that it has legal authority to do so. VA documents this authority through its System of Records Notice (SORN), Privacy Act Statement, and Privacy Impact Assessment (PIA) processes under Appendix E's AP-1.

evidence_required.description: SORN, Privacy Act Statement, and/or PIA documenting the legal authority to collect PII.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Authority to process and purpose specification are closely linked; both are documented in the same PIA/SORN artifacts.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Identify and document the purpose(s) for processing PII; describe the purpose(s) in the public privacy notice; restrict PII processing to only that which is compatible with the identified purposes; monitor for changes in processing purposes.
nist_800_53.discussion: Purpose specification is closely tied to the concept of authority to process; once purposes are identified, they are described in privacy compliance documentation.
assessment_objectives: Determine if PII processing purposes are identified and documented.
Determine if purposes are described in the public privacy notice.
Determine if processing is restricted to purposes compatible with those identified.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: No direct VA 6500 Appendix F allocation; VA's parallel requirement is documented in Appendix E's AP-2.

va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_family: Authority and Purpose (VA Handbook 6500, Appendix E)
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.relationship_description: VA's AP-2 requires describing the purpose for PII collection/use/sharing in privacy notices — directly analogous to Rev 5 PT-3.
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_control_statement: VA will describe the purpose(s) for which PII is collected, used, maintained, and shared in its privacy notices. Purposes are clearly described in related privacy compliance documentation including PIAs, SORNs, and Privacy Act Statements.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must clearly state why it's collecting specific personal information, and that information can't later be used for a different, incompatible purpose without updating the relevant notices. VA documents this in the same PIA/SORN/Privacy Act Statement artifacts referenced above.

evidence_required.description: PIA, SORN, or Privacy Act Statement describing the specific purpose(s) of PII collection.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Purpose specification and authority to process share the same source documentation.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide means, where feasible/appropriate, for individuals to authorize the collection/use/maintenance/sharing of PII prior to collection; provide means to understand consequences of decisions to approve/decline; obtain consent prior to new uses/disclosures of previously collected PII.
nist_800_53.discussion: Consent can be obtained through opt-in, opt-out, or implied consent, with opt-in being preferred but not always feasible.
assessment_objectives: Determine if means are provided for individuals to authorize PII collection/use/sharing.
Determine if means are provided to understand the consequences of consent decisions.
Determine if consent is obtained prior to new uses/disclosures of previously collected PII.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: No direct VA 6500 Appendix F allocation; VA's parallel requirement is documented in Appendix E's IP-1.

va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_family: Individual Participation and Redress (VA Handbook 6500, Appendix E)
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.relationship_description: VA's IP-1 is directly analogous to Rev 5 PT-4, covering the same opt-in/opt-out/implied consent framework.
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_control_statement: VA will provide means, where feasible and appropriate, for individuals to authorize the collection, use, maintenance, and sharing of PII prior to its collection, and obtain consent prior to any new uses or disclosure of previously collected PII.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Where feasible, individuals should be given a way to consent to how their personal information is collected and used, and understand what happens if they decline. VA's Appendix E IP-1 control covers this same requirement using the same opt-in/opt-out consent model.

evidence_required.description: Consent mechanism/form design and associated privacy notice.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Consent and privacy notice are closely linked; the notice informs the consent decision.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Provide notice to individuals about the processing of PII, including the authority, purposes, choices, and consequences; describe the PII collected and how it's used/shared/protected; revise notices to reflect changes in practice.
nist_800_53.discussion: General public notice can be provided through SORNs, PIAs, or website privacy policies.
assessment_objectives: Determine if notice about PII processing is provided to individuals.
Determine if the notice describes PII collected, purposes, and protections.
Determine if notices are revised to reflect changes in practice.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: No direct VA 6500 Appendix F allocation; VA's parallel requirement is documented in Appendix E's TR-1 and TR-2.

va_privacy_overlay_crossref.relationship_description: VA's TR-1 is directly analogous to Rev 5 PT-5, requiring effective notice of PII collection/use/sharing activities.
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_control_statement: VA will provide effective notice to the public and to individuals regarding its activities that impact privacy, including collection, use, sharing, safeguarding, maintenance, and disposal of PII.

va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_control_name: System of Records Notices and Privacy Act Statements
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.relationship_description: VA's TR-2 covers the formal SORN publication requirement that provides notice at the system-of-records level, complementing TR-1's broader notice requirement.
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_control_statement: VA will publish SORNs for information systems containing PII in the Federal Register, keep SORNs current, and include Privacy Act Statements on forms that collect PII.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Individuals must be told what personal information is being collected about them, why, and how it will be used and protected. VA implements this through public-facing privacy notices (TR-1) and formal System of Records Notices published in the Federal Register (TR-2).

evidence_required.description: Published privacy notice/website privacy policy.
Published SORN and Privacy Act Statement.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: The privacy notice discloses the authority documented under PT-2.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Draft and publish system of records notices (SORNs) in the Federal Register per the Privacy Act, subject to required approvals; keep SORNs accurate/up to date; review SORNs periodically.
nist_800_53.discussion: A SORN is a formal notice published to inform the public of the existence of a system of records containing PII.
assessment_objectives: Determine if SORNs are drafted and published in the Federal Register per required approvals.
Determine if SORNs are kept accurate/up to date and reviewed periodically.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: No direct VA 6500 Appendix F allocation; overlaps with VA's TR-2 already cross-referenced under PT-5.

va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_control_name: System of Records Notices and Privacy Act Statements
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.relationship_description: TR-2 is the direct VA equivalent covering SORN publication and maintenance.
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_control_statement: VA will publish in the Federal Register SORNs for information systems containing PII, keep SORNs current, and include Privacy Act Statements on forms that collect PII.

controls.plain_english_explanation: This is essentially the same SORN publication requirement referenced under PT-5/TR-2 — Rev 5 splits it into its own dedicated control (PT-6) while VA's Appendix E covers it under the broader Transparency family control TR-2.

evidence_required.description: Published SORN in the Federal Register.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: SORN publication is part of the broader privacy notice requirement.

controls.control_name: Specific Categories of Personally Identifiable Information

nist_800_53.control_statement: Apply defined processing conditions for specific categories of PII (e.g., Social Security numbers, biometrics, health information).
nist_800_53.discussion: Specific categories of PII may be subject to additional legal or policy protections beyond general PII handling.
assessment_objectives: Determine if defined processing conditions are applied for specific categories of PII.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: No direct VA 6500 Appendix F allocation. VA has extensive separate handling requirements for categories like health information (governed largely outside Appendix E/F, e.g., 38 U.S.C. 7332, HIPAA) rather than a single consolidated control.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Certain categories of especially sensitive personal information (like Social Security numbers or medical/substance-abuse records) require extra handling protections beyond standard PII rules. VA governs this mostly through separate statutes (like 38 U.S.C. 7332 for certain medical records) rather than a single consolidated privacy-family control.

evidence_required.description: Documentation of special handling requirements for sensitive PII categories (e.g., 38 U.S.C. 7332 protected records).

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish policies/procedures for computer matching activities involving PII; establish a Data Integrity Board to oversee computer matching agreements when applicable.
nist_800_53.discussion: Computer matching provisions of the Privacy Act apply to certain automated comparisons of records for eligibility/benefit determinations.
assessment_objectives: Determine if policies/procedures for computer matching are established.
Determine if a Data Integrity Board is established to oversee matching agreements.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: No direct VA 6500 Appendix F allocation; VA's parallel requirement is documented in Appendix E's DI-2.

va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_control_name: Data Integrity and Data Integrity Board
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_family: Data Quality and Integrity (VA Handbook 6500, Appendix E)
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.relationship_description: VA's DI-2 directly addresses the Data Integrity Board and Computer Matching Agreement oversight requirement, matching Rev 5 PT-8.
va_privacy_overlay_crossref.va_control_statement: VA will document processes to ensure integrity of PII, and establish a Data Integrity Board when appropriate to oversee VA Computer Matching Agreements and ensure compliance with the computer matching provisions of the Privacy Act.

controls.plain_english_explanation: When the organization does automated comparisons of records across systems (e.g., matching benefit recipient data against another database) for eligibility determinations, a formal Data Integrity Board oversees this activity to ensure it complies with Privacy Act computer-matching rules.

evidence_required.description: Data Integrity Board charter and Computer Matching Agreement records.

control_families.family_description: Governs the identification, assessment, and mitigation of risks arising throughout the supply chain for systems, system components, and system services.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop, document, and disseminate a supply chain risk management policy and procedures; review/update on a defined frequency.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses purpose, scope, roles, responsibilities, management commitment, coordination, and compliance for supply chain risk management. This is a newer Rev 5 family that did not exist as a distinct family under Rev 4.
assessment_objectives: Determine if supply chain risk management policy and procedures are developed, documented, disseminated, reviewed, and updated.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: SR is a newer Rev 5 family (formalized as its own family separate from SA) that postdates VA 6500's Rev 4-based Appendix F structure. VA addresses supply chain risk conceptually within its SA-12 (Supply Chain Protection) implementation guidance rather than as a distinct family with its own policy control.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization must have a written supply chain risk management policy, reviewed periodically. This is a newer, dedicated NIST family; VA's existing documentation addresses similar ground under its SA-12 (Supply Chain Protection) control rather than as a separate policy family.

evidence_required.description: Supply chain risk management policy document (or VA's equivalent SA-12 guidance).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: VA's existing supply chain protection guidance under SA-12 addresses similar intent to this newer, dedicated SR family.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop a plan for managing supply chain risks associated with the research/development, design, manufacturing, acquisition, delivery, integration, operations/maintenance, and disposal of the system/component/service; review/update the plan on a defined frequency; protect the plan from unauthorized disclosure/modification.
nist_800_53.discussion: Addresses supply chain risk across the full lifecycle of a system or component, not just at initial acquisition.
assessment_objectives: Determine if a supply chain risk management plan covering the full system lifecycle is developed.
Determine if the plan is reviewed/updated and protected from unauthorized disclosure/modification.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish a supply chain risk management team consisting of personnel with responsibilities for both operational security and risk management functions to lead/support SCRM activities.

va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not separately allocated in VA 6500; postdates the Rev 4-based Appendix F structure.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not have a distinct baseline allocation for this newer control; SA-12's implementation guidance addresses standardizing a process for supply chain risk across procurement.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not separately allocated in VA 6500 as its own dedicated family control; conceptually addressed via SA-12.

controls.plain_english_explanation: There should be a documented plan for managing supply chain risk across a system's entire lifecycle, from initial design through disposal — not just a one-time vendor check at purchase. VA's existing SA-12 guidance addresses similar intent, though not as a separately named plan document.

evidence_required.description: Supply chain risk management plan (or VA's equivalent SA-12-based procurement risk documentation).

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: VA's existing supply chain protection control is the closest equivalent to this dedicated SCRM plan requirement.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish a process/processes to identify and address weaknesses/deficiencies in the supply chain elements/processes; employ defined controls to protect against supply chain risks; document the selected/implemented controls in a supply chain risk management plan.
nist_800_53.discussion: Ensures identified supply chain weaknesses are actively addressed, not just documented.
assessment_objectives: Determine if processes to identify/address supply chain weaknesses/deficiencies are established.
Determine if defined controls to protect against supply chain risks are employed and documented in the SCRM plan.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Not separately allocated in VA 6500; VA's SA-12 implementation guidance references using acquisition/procurement processes to require supply chain entities to implement necessary security safeguards.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Conceptually addressed via SA-12 rather than as a distinct SR control.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization needs a process to actively identify and fix weaknesses in its supply chain (e.g., a vendor with poor security practices), not just document the risk and move on. VA addresses this conceptually within its broader supply chain protection guidance (SA-12).

evidence_required.description: Supply chain weakness identification/remediation process.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares the same underlying supply chain risk management intent.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Document, monitor, and maintain valid provenance of defined systems, system components, and associated data throughout the system development life cycle.
nist_800_53.discussion: Provenance refers to the chronology of the origin, development, ownership, location, and changes to a system or component, and its associated data.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time as a formal baseline allocation.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in VA 6500; postdates the Rev 4-based Appendix F structure.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA as a distinct baseline control — this would document and track the full chronology/history of a system component from origin through its current state.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ defined acquisition strategies, contract tools, and procurement methods to protect against, identify, and mitigate supply chain risks.
nist_800_53.discussion: Strategies may include using trusted/controlled distribution, requiring tamper-evident packaging, or diversifying suppliers.
assessment_objectives: Determine if defined acquisition strategies/tools/methods are employed to protect against, identify, and mitigate supply chain risks.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Not separately allocated in VA 6500; conceptually addressed through VA's contract-based supply chain safeguards under SA-4 and SA-12.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Conceptually addressed via SA-4/SA-12 rather than as a distinct SR control.

controls.plain_english_explanation: The organization uses specific procurement strategies (like requiring tamper-evident packaging or diversifying suppliers) to reduce supply chain risk during the acquisition process itself. VA addresses similar ground through its acquisition contract security requirements (SA-4) and supply chain protection guidance (SA-12).

evidence_required.description: Procurement/contract language addressing supply chain risk mitigation strategies.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Acquisition contract security requirements overlap with supply-chain-focused procurement strategies.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Assess and review the supply chain-related risks associated with suppliers or contractors and the system, system component, or system service they provide.
nist_800_53.discussion: A formal, recurring review process for evaluating supplier risk, distinct from a one-time acquisition decision.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time as a formal baseline allocation.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in VA 6500; postdates the Rev 4-based Appendix F structure.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA as a distinct baseline control — this would formalize ongoing (not just one-time) risk assessments of suppliers/contractors.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Employ defined operations security safeguards to protect supply chain-related information for the system, system component, or system service throughout the SDLC.
nist_800_53.discussion: Focuses on protecting information about the supply chain itself (e.g., sourcing details) that could be exploited by adversaries.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Not selected in VA 6500; postdates the Rev 4-based Appendix F structure.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA as a distinct baseline control — this would protect sensitive information about the organization's supply chain sourcing from adversary exploitation.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Establish agreements and procedures with entities involved in the supply chain for the system/component/service for the notification of supply chain compromises and results of assessments/audits.
nist_800_53.discussion: Ensures the organization is proactively informed of supply chain issues by suppliers/contractors, rather than discovering them independently.
assessment_objectives: Determine if agreements/procedures for notification of supply chain compromises and assessment results are established with supply chain entities.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Not separately allocated in VA 6500 as a distinct baseline control; conceptually related to VA's third-party personnel security notification requirements under PS-7 and contract security provisions under SA-9.
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Conceptually overlaps with PS-7/SA-9 requirements but not separately baselined.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Contracts with suppliers/vendors should require them to notify VA if a supply chain compromise occurs or if audit results reveal problems — similar in spirit to VA's existing requirement that contractors notify VA of relevant personnel changes (PS-7) or service issues (SA-9).

evidence_required.description: Supplier/contractor notification agreement language.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: External service provider monitoring shares similar notification intent.
Supply chain compromise notifications feed into the broader incident reporting process.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Implement a tamper protection program for the system, system component, or system service.
nist_800_53.discussion: Protects physical hardware/components from being tampered with during manufacturing, shipping, or storage.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: VA does not require this control at this time.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Not currently required by VA as a distinct baseline control — this would implement a formal program to detect physical tampering with hardware components during manufacturing/shipping.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Inspect defined systems or system components at defined transition points to detect tampering.
nist_800_53.discussion: Common transition points include when systems/components are received from suppliers.
assessment_objectives: Determine if defined systems/system components are inspected at defined transition points to detect tampering.

va_overlay.va_implementation_guidance: Not separately allocated in VA 6500; VA's maintenance tool inspection requirements under MA-3 address a related, though narrower, concept (inspecting maintenance tools/media, not all incoming system components).
va_overlay.mapping_notes: Conceptually related to VA's MA-3 (Maintenance Tools) inspection requirements but not directly equivalent.

controls.plain_english_explanation: Systems/components should be inspected for signs of tampering when they arrive from a supplier or at other key transition points. VA has a related, narrower requirement under MA-3 for inspecting maintenance tools and diagnostic media specifically.

evidence_required.description: Component inspection procedure at receipt/transition points.

cross_reference_controls.relationship_description: Shares a similar tamper-inspection intent, though scoped specifically to maintenance tools/media in VA's implementation.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Develop and implement anti-counterfeit policy and procedures to detect and prevent counterfeit components from entering the system; report counterfeit components to defined personnel/organizations.
nist_800_53.discussion: Counterfeit components may not meet manufacturer specifications and can introduce reliability and security risks.
assessment_objectives: Determine if anti-counterfeit policy/procedures to detect/prevent counterfeit components are developed and implemented.
Determine if counterfeit components are reported to defined personnel/organizations.

nist_800_53.control_statement: Train defined personnel to detect counterfeit system components.

control_enhancements.enhancement_name: Configuration Control for Component Service and Repair

nist_800_53.control_statement: Maintain configuration control over defined system components awaiting service or repair, and components returned after service/repair.
